its missing mathematical and empirical obligations to be discharged,
rather than a new wrapper around an attractive estimator name.

The implemented examples that follow test this proposed composition at
three levels. A static adjustment query shares scores with an invitation
ratio. A dynamic funding study carries clocks, linkage uncertainty and
financial units through two consumers. The final comparison preserves
uncertainty and refusal across distinct scientific families. Each provides
evidence for specific shared operations within the wider specification.

\section{Executable composition across distinct scientific questions}
\label{s5:composition}
The common layer should earn its cost by preserving meaning across reused
operations. A small implemented composition begins with an
\texttt{AdjustmentQuery}: action, outcome, controls, population unit,
outcome units and sampling law. A supplied acyclic graph is checked using
the sufficient back-door criterion: reject action descendants among controls,
remove outgoing action arrows, take the ancestral moral graph and test
separation after removing the controls. A passing trace determines the
functional
\[
 \psi=\E_X[m_1(X)-m_0(X)]
\]
and the nuisance roles $(m_0,m_1,e)$. The graph is supplied scientific
knowledge; data do not certify its absent edges. Failure of this sufficient
criterion means this adjustment backend cannot identify the query, not that
no other identification strategy exists.

Whole-unit folds produce out-of-fold predictions. A separate score operation
forms
\[
 U=m_1(X)-m_0(X)+\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}
 -\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)}.
\]
The independent-unit mean operation returns an estimate and variance
$N^{-2}\sum_i(U_i-\bar U)^2$, conditional on the identification and
nuisance-rate arguments in Chapter~\ref{r3:learning}. It rejects a declared
calendar-dependent sampling law. The score algebra is reusable; its sampling
covariance is not automatically portable to common shocks or repeated rows.
Independent path checks include a blocked confounder, an unblocked hidden
confounder, an opened collider, an action descendant and a cyclic graph.

A second adjustment query substitutes participation for wealth as the
outcome, producing first-stage scores $U_D$ alongside reduced-form scores
$U_Y$ on identical customers and splits. The ratio operation composes them:
\[
 \hat\theta=\bar U_Y/\bar U_D,
 \qquad \hat\phi_i=(U_{Y,i}-\hat\theta U_{D,i})/\bar U_D.
\]
It uses their joint covariance and residual-test inversion to retain weak
denominator topology. Instrument independence, exclusion, monotonicity and
positive complier mass are additional obligations before calling this ratio
a LATE. They do not follow from the graph's eligibility-to-wealth adjustment
trace. Bernoulli participation regressions are constrained to $[0,1]$;
that support projection is recorded separately from propensity clipping.

The public household-finance study and a separate synthetic bank contact/profit
study use the same query, graph, nuisance, score and mean operations with
different fields, adjustment dimension, populations and currencies. The
longitudinal query in Section~\ref{s5:history-censoring} has a different
identification expression and backwards nuisance recursion but reuses the
independent-unit mean/variance operation on customer trajectory scores.
The temporal query in Section~\ref{s5:discovery} reuses the principle of an
explicit target and result state, while returning conditional curve sets
rather than forcing graph ambiguity into a mean-score interface. These are
distinct reusable module compositions. They do not constitute a generic
compiler for every SCM or a complete application workbench.

\subsection{A substantive package adapter with a matched reference}
DoubleML 0.11.4 provides an installed IRM ATE operation
\citep{doubleml2022,runtime_doubleml_scope}. The adapter supplies the exact
same folds and nuisance predictions as the independent score calculation,
uses unnormalized inverse weights and propensity truncation at .01, and
checks the resulting estimate and standard error. Across the six public
learner/split runs and the second bank-contact example, coefficient
discrepancy is zero and standard-error discrepancy is at most
$4.55\times10^{-13}$. This is a meaningful test of target, weight and
covariance semantics under matched inputs. Comparing independently fitted
learners would conflate those semantics with nuisance variation; the public
study reports that second comparison separately.

These matched examples support the selective-reuse choice developed in
Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software}: DoubleML supplies the qualified static
semiparametric operation, while Tigramite supplies qualified temporal search.
The shared layer adds observation clocks, identification traces, preserved
result states and comparisons across libraries. Controlled likelihoods,
dependence-sensitive moments and generated observation plans still need
explicit reference constructions because a generic estimator interface does
not supply their assumptions. Unrestricted PAG identification, general neural
POMDP inference and distributed execution remain extensions requiring their
own scientific and operational qualification.

The installed-source records supplement the 44-project document survey;
they do not retroactively turn that whole survey into runtime qualification.
DoubleML's archived distribution declares BSD licensing. Tigramite's
installed metadata declares GPLv3 or later, so the packaging/distribution
decision must preserve those obligations; a mathematical adapter test is
not distribution clearance. The standalone design exposes these operations
through explicit requests and preserved artifacts. Sibling integrations
map existing domain fields to those requests, with adapters tested here;
accepted execution inside the sibling repositories remains separate work.

\section{One dynamic scientific brief, two product consumers}
\label{s6:composition}
The treasury brief asks for a one-month ten-basis-point price shift's
seven-month funding contribution for a fixed portfolio. Source records
contain candidate entity assignments and delayed balance revisions.
The information plan specifies an independent nuisance pilot, independently
audited pair matches, fixed calendar origins, the conditional price-innovation
restriction, and the common-calendar covariance rule. A causal result
requires all of these inputs; a regression formula alone cannot substitute
for the observation and sampling experiment.

The local construction first materializes the two candidate outcome
histories. Predecision features must be available by the decision date.
Realized outcomes may arrive later, but only revisions available by the
fixed retrospective extraction cutoff enter the evaluation view. These
are different clocks: a realized four-month outcome cannot be required to
exist before its treatment. The raw fixture includes later revisions whose
balances depend on the action. They are excluded by their arrival time;
business dates alone would leak them into the view. Missing horizons,
duplicated origin features and unavailable predecision information are
rejected. Conflicting source semantics remain unresolved before fitting.
The selected materializer accepts the account unit and received-day
availability only. Even a uniquely supplied business-day interpretation is
rejected as unsupported by this operation. Source-owner assertions are
simulated provenance inputs here; real authentication and semantic review
are not established by the fixture's trusted flag.

The same observation object feeds the nuisance fit, stratum-specific response
moments, inverse-linkage correction, calendar plus calibration covariance
and funding account derived in Sections~\ref{s6:funding}
and~\ref{s6:linked-histories}. Source and audit identities are preserved
alongside hashes of the actual pilot, evaluation and audit arrays. Target
units, horizon, financial weights, linkage law, sampling law and bandwidth
and nuisance-selection candidates also enter the analysis identity. The
supplied source assertions and retrospective extraction cutoff are bound
as well, even when a changed assertion leaves numeric arrays unchanged.
Changing bytes while retaining an old
source name invalidates reuse, just as changing the sampling law does.

The treasury consumer displays total funding contribution, its interval
and the response curve. An application builder consumes the same result
and divides by an externally fixed 480,000-account exposure. In the
720-origin reference, the estimate is 132,418 currency units, with interval
$[-149{,}326,414{,}162]$. The second consumer reports .276 per account and
interval $[-.311,.863]$, carrying exactly the same scientific identity.
This rescaling is valid because its denominator is fixed. Estimating or
selecting the account population from outcomes would need an additional
influence term and target definition.

Changing the externally supplied funding margin from .002 to .0015 is
supported: the response estimate is reused scientifically, while the
financial linear combination and its covariance are recomputed under a
new identity. An attempted balance-stock-to-cash-flow reinterpretation is
rejected because the price cost and balance retention account no longer
apply. An independent-branch sampling request is rejected by the calendar
backend. Submitting an old cached identity after any of these economic or
data changes is rejected before its interval can be displayed. These are
executed interface outcomes, not only proposed validation messages.

The reusable layer therefore owns observation and intervention semantics,
uncertainty composition and economic result transformations. Numerical
regression, array algebra and mature graph search remain delegated to
qualified library operations. The direct statsmodels comparison uses the
same residuals and covariance convention \citep{runtime_statsmodels_dynamic};
the independent linked-response reference checks the complete correction
and financial covariance. The prototype deliberately has no generic
compiler for arbitrary identification formulas. New score/likelihood
families need an explicit implementation with its own assumptions.

This is a local common library and two reference consumers. FinMarketing,
dataml and MacroFinance can adapt their observation and result interfaces
to these objects, but no sibling adoption is asserted. A bank workbench
would add data access, review interaction, entitlement and lifecycle
features around these scientifically qualified operations. The build choice
is to own the common scientific contract, reuse numerical libraries and
defer unsupported nonlinear/PAG procedures. The observed small-workload
cost does not justify a distributed platform merely to run these examples.

\subsection{A financial set is a different public result}
\label{s61:projection-product}
The same public operation accepts the projection procedure in
Section~\ref{s61:linkage-sets}. Its result carries a finite list of interval
components, confidence level and the separate audit/response coverage
conditions. A missing lower or upper endpoint explicitly means an infinite
endpoint; it never means a missing estimate to be filled by zero. The treasury
view shows the monetary set, while the application view divides each
component by the fixed positive account count. A disconnected set remains
disconnected after this transformation. There is no invented point estimate
or symmetric standard error when the information only supports a set.

The regular and projection procedures are selected explicitly, and the
procedure, confidence level, fixed error allocation and sum/difference
coordinates enter the scientific identity. A caller cannot choose the
narrower interval after inspecting both and inherit either procedure's
coverage claim. Displaying them as sensitivity comparisons is different
from a prespecified inferential choice. The candidate-coordinate projection
is retained as a mathematical challenger, not an automatic width selector.

The input domain is part of the calculation. The public operation checks
finite observations and economic quantities, complete response dimensions,
the declared driver/stratum basis, full pilot-training rank, both evaluation
strata, residual price variation, binary calibration records and an integer
bandwidth below the calendar length. Conflicting copies of the same outcome
revision and nonfinite extraction clocks are rejected. Regular inverse-map
inference also needs audit records in both strata. Projection can instead
use $[0,1]$ for an unaudited stratum, often producing an uninformative set.
An unsupported variance or nonfinite financial result cannot carry a
successful computed status. These checks verify numerical and structural
compatibility; they do not establish the source owner's truth, pilot
independence, the causal innovation restriction or audit representativeness.

An executed adversarial case removes all audits from one stratum. The regular
operation rejects the missing calibration, while projection returns the
appropriate set under its larger probability region. Other retained cases
change the inference procedure and confidence level, remove an evaluation
stratum, introduce nonbinary audit labels, break the pilot basis, and supply
conflicting revisions. Their failures identify the particular information
or procedure that must change before a result can be requested again.

\section{Three experiments, shared meaning and deliberate refusal}
\label{c7:journeys}
The preceding constructions support reuse because they expose compatible
scientific meanings, not because every problem is converted into the same
regression. A request declares its population, intervention normalization,
unit, information clock, sampling law, inference method and fixed monetary
scale. The persistent-funding request invokes the independent-pair audited
moment. The servicing request invokes the identified nonlinear model and a
policy fixed independently of evaluation. The discovery request retains its
latent class or its separately justified encouragement restriction.

Each result distinguishes a numeric calculation from its uncertainty claim.
The inference description contains the method, nominal level, finite-sample
or asymptotic interpretation, assumptions, numerical status and adverse
empirical evidence. Both a treasury account and a customer-facing application
retain that description. The latter may divide a set by a fixed external
account count, preserving disconnected components and unbounded endpoints.
An estimated exposure denominator instead requires a joint influence argument.

This requirement repairs a practical defect in the earlier regular funding
path: its public consumers dropped the scope field even though the underlying
calculation carried it. The revised request makes the inference method explicit
before fitting. The retained regular method discloses its adverse calibration;
neither it nor the projection is selected after comparing favorable widths.
Legacy callers preserve their original procedure while receiving the fuller
description. The change preserves the original numeric results and changes
what their recipients are told.

The local examples execute two eligible requests within each family and send
each result to both consumers. The second funding request changes horizon and
sample size; the second servicing request changes the fixed observable policy;
the second discovery request supplies valid encouragement information. These
are new scientific inputs and receive new identities. The identity binds the
request, data and implementation, but it does not certify the truth of a
supplied assumption.

Incompatible requests fail at meaningful boundaries. A pair-level persistent
map cannot borrow a calendar HAC covariance. A current audited hidden state
cannot become an input to the deployed policy. An account-date cannot replace
the independent customer unit. A selected graph cannot inherit confidence from
an outer structural union without carrying the union's information conditions.
Wrong clocks, empty populations and unsupported inference combinations are
rejected. These refusals express missing scientific arguments and information,
not a generic software inconvenience.

Direct expert composition can call the same qualified kernels and satisfy the
same unit, provenance, uncertainty and reporting obligations. The shared product
is valuable only if it helps preserve those obligations across repeated tasks.
The local matched computation compares identical public output bytes; it does
not measure analyst savings or establish acceptance by FinMarketing,
BayesFilter, MacroFinance or dataml. Their inspected interfaces remain concrete
integration proposals until their owners qualify and adopt the mappings.

chapters.title: What the local study interfaces preserve

segments.text:
\chapter{What the local study interfaces preserve}
\label{scisyn:investment}

\section{One question through three ways of using the library}
An illustrative economist asks about the twelve-month value of an offer among
eligible accounts. The supplied diagram contains an arrow from offer to value,
and the sampling assumption is independent accounts. That diagram is explicitly
unverified. The local walkthrough sends the same question through the Python
library, a command-line process and a local MCP client. It exercises the
repository's existing implementation; it does not connect another repository,
invoke a language model or fit an external statistical package.

Four cases have distinct economic interpretations. The diagram check preserves
the supplied graph and establishes only its accepted syntax. The adjustment
calculation returns a result conditional on the supplied graph and independent
sampling. The information-date check examines three constructed records:
one was available before the decision, one became available afterwards, and
one lacks an availability date. The latter two are flagged. Finally, changing
the sampling law to dependent months causes the identification request to be
reported as unsupported by that route.

An initial client attempt timed out during initialization after 20 seconds.
The retry used the established bounded environment with one numerical thread;
the cause of the first timeout was not conclusively isolated.
The saved retry responses agree exactly across all three interfaces for the four
cases. The local MCP negotiation uses protocol 2025-11-25 and the installed
1.27.0 SDK. This is a bounded observed result. It establishes neither general
protocol compatibility nor the scientific truth of the supplied assumptions.
An unsupported scientific request can be delivered successfully by the command
line and protocol: the economist must read the substantive disposition rather
than infer validity from a successful process exit.

The executable walkthrough is reproduced from the repository root by
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily
python3 tools/run\_banking\_walkthrough\_20261029.py
\end{quote}
It requires the locally installed research dependencies recorded with its
results. The numerical offer comparison is reproduced by
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily
python3 tools/run\_scientific\_synthesis\_20261029.py
\end{quote}
Both calculations use constructed inputs. Neither is a completed customer
policy analysis. A full study still needs observed assignment and outcome
information, a justified design, estimation and interpretation.

The separate sparse-support comparison can be reproduced with
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily
python3 tools/run\_sparse\_support\_20261029.py
\end{quote}
Its narrower and broader normal-model intervals make their additional
assumptions and loss of precision explicit.

The actual public-data timing comparison uses the retained UCI archive:
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily
python3 tools/run\_public\_timing\_20261029.py
\end{quote}
It fits the specified prediction models; it does not estimate a contact effect.

\section{How public evidence can support the proposal}
Public records and generated data serve different purposes. The executed UCI
comparison shows why a variable's availability can outweigh its apparent
predictive benefit. The retained UCI
Bank Marketing description supports a useful information-date example and
data-preparation exercise, but not an experimental effect of calling. FDIC
branch deposits and institutional histories are promising for observation and
panel construction; the documented branch outcomes do not make a merger or
closure exogenous. ACIC provides a route to comparing methods with generated
causal truth while retaining the distinction between real covariates and
simulated outcomes.
\citep{pd15_uci_bank,pd15_fdic_sod,pd15_fdic_api_spec,pd15_acic_pinned}

Use generated studies to test questions with known answers, then public data
to expose realistic observations, missingness and timing. The offer experiment
already changes a design requirement: outputs must distinguish projections
from population benefits and report sparse-support failures. The walkthrough
changes another: a study must preserve scientific meaning when passed between
interfaces. Neither result warrants spending on a broad bank trial yet. The
next public comparison should ask whether these protections materially improve
an analyst's completed study relative to ordinary practice.

The economic comparison of these workflows is developed in
Chapter~\ref{rewrite:investment-decision}. Its account includes unsuccessful
studies, correction, interpretation and maintenance, and distinguishes a
prototype comparison from a later bank-data pilot.

chapters.title: What the evidence changes about the proposed service

segments.text:
\chapter{What the evidence changes about the proposed service}
\label{rewrite:evidence-consequences}

The four journeys distinguish a wrong target, insufficient treatment support,
causal ambiguity and uncertain measurement. Those failures demand different
responses. A common service should make the distinctions visible while
reusing the appropriate statistical procedures. Its initial scope follows
from the evidence below; it does not require every possible capability to
be implemented at once.

\section{A result should change a design choice}
The existing 3,000-replication generated offer study is evidence about target
alignment. Under one specified design, the residual projection averages
26.447 when the equal-population benefit is 50. Its interval covers its own
target in 97.2\% of repetitions and the population target in none. At the
stipulated cost of 40, interpreting it as the population effect rejects the
beneficial offer in all 500 repetitions of that scenario. The design
consequence is to put the population weights and target in the result,
and to compare implementations only after aligning those quantities. A
more precise projection is not a repair for this interpretation error.

The separate 6,000-replication sparse-support study addresses inference
after the target is aligned. Pooling yields 94.7\% conditional coverage
under equal normal variances but 52.2\% under the tested unequal-variance
case. Cellwise Student intervals joined by a union bound preserve the
conditional coverage guarantee in the normal model at the cost of very
wide intervals. Thus the initial implementation should show cell support
and retain an unsupported or inconclusive result. If useful precision
requires unjustified pooling, the next expenditure should improve assignment
support or the information collected. These are existing generated
experiments, not evidence of superiority by a named external package.

The public UCI timing study answers a different question. On 41,188 archived
contact records, later-archive prediction has AUC 0.630 using the candidate
pre-call feature set and 0.793 when duration is added. The latter feature
is unavailable before the call, so its predictive gain cannot justify
pre-call targeting. Differences between early and late archive outcomes
also matter for evaluation. The correct service response is to preserve
availability dates and the evaluation period. Neither score estimates
the effect of making a call. Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} gives the
executed design, comparators, results and qualifications.

The retained public 401(k), monetary, panel and linked-record analyses
provide further empirical and methodological context. Their sampling,
instrument, design and observation restrictions remain attached to their
results in the detailed evidence part. A working independent-observation
covariance in a public application does not validate a bank's common-calendar
uncertainty. A successful finite construction does not settle the unrestricted
linked-history problem. The negative findings remain relevant because
they identify the information a future bank study must supply.

The new one-sample deposit calculation in Chapter~\ref{rewrite:deposit}
completes the numerical route from estimation to contribution. Its callable
and command-line agreement tests the delivery of that particular report.
The four existing library/CLI/MCP cases test semantic consistency for
their own operations, including unsupported dependence. They establish
complementary facts. The later public experiment also carries fitted effect and covariance
summaries through all three interfaces (Chapter~\ref{gap29:public}).
Raw-data fitting and final reporting remain local scripts. These executions
are not a matched analyst trial, a general estimation service or evidence
of improved bank outcomes.

\section{Choose the smallest comparison that can reverse the recommendation}
The first comparison should take the same fixed offer question through
expert composition and a minimal shared integration. The cases should
include correct assignment, heterogeneous effects, unequal treatment
support, unavailable predictors, misrecorded receipt and a dependent
sampling request outside the accepted route. The generated law supplies
truth where that is possible; a public case supplies realistic data handling
without pretending its causal truth is known. A valid refusal counts as
a completed scientific answer when the information is insufficient.

An independent evaluator should judge target correctness, assumption
visibility, uncertainty, interpretation and avoidable errors. Time must
include correction, interpretation and unsuccessful attempts. The estimate
itself is not a success metric when its target differs from the request.
The proposed comparison is not yet an executed analyst study; its purpose
is to discover whether the common representation is worth its expense.
If both workflows reach equivalent answers at equivalent cost, improve
the existing workflow. If the integration reduces consequential errors or
repeated work, a narrow bank-data pilot becomes a defensible next step.


\section{What the newer studies add to that choice}
The public earnings contrast tests the complete chain from observed rows to
uncertainty and an explicit spending hurdle. A positive contrast alone does
not establish that a cost is covered. The servicing comparisons show why a
fitted policy can offer narrow but misleading uncertainty when dropout or
state assumptions fail. The institutional panel separates persistent level
adjustment from a coherent economic unit; the linkage study makes the cost
of a justified error budget visible. These results explain which information
the proposed study description must carry, rather than establish the benefit
of buying the service.

Together they favour a comparison on completed scientific work: whether an
analyst identifies the right target, preserves uncertainty, recognizes an
unsupported premise and reaches the correct conditional decision. The
software choices in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software} and the investment account
in Chapter~\ref{rewrite:investment-decision} follow from that evidence.

chapters.title: What a shared service must preserve

segments.text:
\chapter{What a shared service must preserve}
\label{r3:software}

The preceding theory makes software selection more demanding than choosing
an estimator with an attractive name. A deposit-retention analysis may ask
for an average effect across customers, across branches, or across balances.
A collections analysis may ask for an effect of a fixed schedule, a rule
using available history, or a modification of the historical assignment
law. These distinctions change the estimand before any package is called.
The common product needs to preserve them as it moves between data engines,
identification libraries, statistical estimators and decision solvers.
Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software} gives the principal selection argument. Here the
comparison develops the conditions behind that choice: the population carried
by weights, the intervention represented by a policy, the information available
at each decision and the sampling unit carried into uncertainty. These are the
properties that the operations in Chapter~\ref{r3:product} must preserve.

This chapter uses the preserved primary documentation and selected source
interfaces of 44 projects. The scientific comparisons concern the inspected
versions, using 7 October 2026 as the publication/version cutoff where a
dated revision could be established. Mutable documentation accessed on
8 October has a separate access identity and does not establish its exact
contents at the cutoff. A documented interface, a successful
package execution and a validated banking analysis are different evidence.
The broad comparisons establish source/document evidence. Selected installed
DuckDB and Polars revision operations, scikit-learn Lasso normalization and
SciPy optimization now have executed reference comparisons, recorded
separately from the historical documentation snapshots. Their versions and
local source/license copies accompany the receipts; qualification applies
to those operations, not every feature of each package
\citep{runtime_duckdb,runtime_polars,runtime_scikit_learn,runtime_scipy,runtime_numpy}.
The selected DoubleML score and Tigramite temporal-search executions in
Sections~\ref{s5:composition} and~\ref{s5:discovery} add substantive causal
operations with matched references and preserved endpoint semantics
\citep{runtime_doubleml_scope,runtime_tigramite_scope}.
Published package versions, mutable documentation snapshots and
commit-pinned source files are kept distinct in the accompanying source
register. No speed ranking is inferred from repository activity or a
maintainer's benchmark.

\section{Changing software must preserve the economic quantity}
\label{r3:software-types}

Let a request contain a causal model class $\mathcal M$, observation operator
$K$, intervention $g$, target population $\nu$ and functional
$\theta(M;g,\nu)$. Let $P=K(M)$ denote the observed law. The first possible
output is an identification statement
\[
 \theta(M;g,\nu)=\Psi(K(M))\qquad\text{for all }M\in\mathcal M.
\]
An estimator is then a numerical map from the observed sample to
$\widehat\Psi$. An inference method is a further construction whose
validity depends on the sampling scheme and estimator remainder.
The input of a planner is different again: it requires an interventional
transition/observation/reward model, or an explicitly defined ambiguity set.
None of these objects can be substituted merely because its serialized
form is an array of numbers.

DoWhy exposes this separation in its interface. The inspected
\texttt{identify\_effect} selects its ID implementation when requested;
\texttt{estimate\_effect} separately takes an identified expression and
an estimator method \citep{sw_dowhy}. An expression produced by graphical
identification need not have a matching numerical estimator in the chosen
backend. Thus the product must distinguish three outcomes: a supported
identified functional, a valid identification result whose estimation is
not implemented, and nonidentification in the assumed model class.
The last requires a scientific witness such as the paired models of
Section~\ref{r3:nonidentification}; a missing Python method is not such a
witness.

There is a useful criterion for a data adapter. Suppose it transforms the
observation through $T$ and the backend estimates $\Psi_B$. Target
preservation requires
\begin{equation}
 \Psi(P)=\Psi_B(T_\#P)
 \quad\text{for every allowed observed law }P,
 \label{r3:adapter-identity}
\end{equation}
where $T_\#P$ is the distribution after transformation. Invertible relabeling
usually satisfies this with an appropriate inverse interpretation.
Demeaning, history truncation, averaging time bins, hard record linkage,
weight normalization and imputation generally require additional arguments.
Equation~\eqref{r3:adapter-identity} also shows why a common
\texttt{fit/predict} signature is insufficient: it says nothing about
which functional survives the conversion.

\section{Effects, projections and the population carried by weights}
\label{r3:software-effects}

EconML, DoubleML, causalml and grf provide useful but overlapping learning
components \citep{sw_econml,sw_doubleml,sw_causalml,sw_grf}. The relevant
comparison begins with the target. For binary treatment under adjustment,
the CATE is $\tau(x)=\E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]$. A partially linear residual
coefficient instead solves an unconditional moment and, with heterogeneous
effects, can weight $\tau(x)$ by residual treatment variation. The
R-learner calculation in Section~\ref{r3:heterogeneity} identifies that
difference. An IV learner introduces yet another moment and its exclusion,
relevance and effect-heterogeneity restrictions. A common effect-prediction
interface cannot turn these coefficients into a common CATE.

The inspected \texttt{grf::causal\_forest} documents the distinction
explicitly: for binary unconfounded treatment it targets a CATE; for
continuous treatment it uses
\[
 b(x)=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(Y,A\mid X=x)}
                 {\operatorname{Var}(A\mid X=x)}.
\]
This is a local linear projection in the treatment dimension. It is not
generally the dose-response derivative at a nominated action. For example,
if $A$ is uniform on $[-1,1]$, $Y(a)=a^3$, and no confounding is present,
then $b=\E[A^4]/\E[A^2]=3/5$, while the derivative at $a=0$ is zero.
Both quantities can be meaningful; an interface must name the requested one.

Population weighting is equally substantive. If branch $c$ contains $n_c$
customers with average effect $\tau_c$, then
\[
 \theta_{\rm customer}=
 \frac{\sum_c n_c\tau_c}{\sum_c n_c},
 \qquad
 \theta_{\rm branch}=\frac1C\sum_c\tau_c.
\]
For two branches with sizes $1$ and $9$ and effects $0$ and $10$, these
values are $9$ and $5$. The source of \texttt{causal\_forest} states that
\texttt{equalize.cluster.weights=TRUE} uses inverse cluster-size weights
when estimating average effects; it also requires
\texttt{sample.weights=NULL}. The default gives equal weight to units.
This option changes the population aggregation, not merely the reported
standard error \citep{sw_grf}.

A balance-weighted bank target needs a further definition. A weight
measured before treatment can define a baseline exposure-weighted average.
A balance measured after treatment may itself change under intervention;
using it as an ordinary sampling weight can select on a treatment
descendant. The product must carry the weight's time, role and normalization
with the target. Frequency weights, sampling weights, treatment-density
ratios, loss weights and numerical importance weights cannot share a
single undocumented field.

DoubleML's inspected data classes distinguish outcomes, treatments,
instruments, covariates and cluster columns. They do not make arbitrary
dependent records satisfy a cross-fitting theorem. causalml's documentation
supplies a CATE/uplift and benchmarking route; using its predictions for
contact allocation still requires the policy-value argument and independent
evaluation of Chapter~\ref{r3:decision-learning}. A package comparison should
therefore hold the estimand, population, nuisance information and evaluation
sample fixed before comparing bias, coverage, policy value or runtime.

\section{A panel identifier does not specify a panel model}
\label{r3:software-panels}

The same customer-period table can support a fixed-effect projection,
a staggered-adoption ATT, a dynamic GMM coefficient or a sequential blip.
Chapter~\ref{r3:panels} derives different assumptions for each. The software
mirrors this division. linearmodels supplies linear panel, IV and system
baselines; PyFixest and fixest supply formula-based fixed-effect, IV and
other regression operations; pydynpd explicitly constructs difference and
system GMM \citep{sw_linearmodels,sw_pyfixest,sw_fixest,sw_pydynpd}.
Absorbing many fixed effects quickly does not repair an invalid
heterogeneous-treatment TWFE estimand. Likewise, an automated search across
instrument lags cannot validate the orthogonality of those instruments.

For a branch rollout, \texttt{did::att\_gt} represents first-adoption
cohorts and group--time effects. Its inspected interface has important
implications for a shared service. Time-varying sampling weights are
handled differently in balanced panels and repeated cross sections or
unbalanced panels. Fixing weights at an anchor period can remove units
unobserved at that anchor. Beyond individual clustering, this snapshot
supports at most one additional coarser cluster variable. Uniform bands
require its bootstrap; setting \texttt{compute\_inffunc=FALSE} produces
point estimates without inference and prevents the documented aggregation
through \texttt{aggte} \citep{sw_did}. Saving memory by dropping influence
information therefore also removes downstream operations.

DoubleML's panel container is not a substitute for an arbitrary sequential
history object. Its default \texttt{static\_panel=False} interprets
treatment values as first-treatment timing, and the inspected constructor
permits only one treatment column \citep{sw_doubleml}. An array of monthly
credit-limit changes is not a cohort-date array. The conversion must be
rejected unless the requested analysis explicitly defines an appropriate
adoption representation.

DynamicDML illustrates the separate chronological contract. The inspected
EconML implementation requires equal group lengths and interprets each
group's occurrence order as its period order. Only first-period $X$
defines effect heterogeneity; later $X$ is a time-varying control. The
fit method warns that \texttt{sample\_weight} and \texttt{sample\_var}
are ignored and passes neither into fitting \citep{sw_econml}. A bank
adapter must therefore sort by a validated decision clock, check for
missing or duplicated periods, use a group-aware split, and reject a
weighted request this interface cannot honor. Padding a missing decision
with zeros changes the observation law and is not a general repair for
an unbalanced panel.

Alternatives change the identifying model rather than merely the optimizer.
synthdid's documented input requires simultaneous treatment with a block
adoption matrix. gsynth imputes untreated outcomes through interactive
fixed effects; its current README says that it wraps \texttt{fect} and is
maintained for backward compatibility, so that dependency needs its own
qualification \citep{sw_synthdid,sw_gsynth}. HonestDiD takes an estimated
event-study vector and covariance and adds an explicit class of possible
trend violations \citep{sw_honestdid}. That is a sensitivity operation on
an already defined contrast, not an automatic selection of a true trend
restriction.

CausalImpact and CausalPy provide further useful comparisons
\citep{sw_causalimpact,sw_causalpy}. CausalImpact's primary documentation
requires unaffected controls and a stable counterfactual relationship
after the intervention. CausalPy offers distinct quasi-experimental
designs with Bayesian or OLS estimation. The appropriate comparison with
a cohort estimator or factor model asks whether each model answers the
same bank intervention and whether its counterfactual restrictions are
credible. Comparing interval widths without those restrictions would
reward unwarranted certainty.

\section{Longitudinal libraries must preserve the intervention law}
\label{r3:software-longitudinal}

The longitudinal g-formula can be evaluated through fitted transition
distributions, backward outcome regressions or targeted/augmented
constructions. gfoRmula, ltmle, lmtp and zEpid expose different parts of
this space \citep{sw_gformula,sw_ltmle,sw_lmtp,sw_zepid}. They cannot be
made interchangeable by renaming their output \emph{policy effect}.
The treatment law, censoring intervention, endpoint and history are part
of the mathematical input.

gfoRmula's inspected interface takes person-period data, conditional models,
history functions and named interventions. It returns survival risks or
terminal means/probabilities. The number of simulated persons,
\texttt{nsimul}, controls Monte Carlo approximation; the number of
bootstrap samples, \texttt{nsamples}, concerns sampling uncertainty.
Increasing the former cannot compensate for a small observed cohort.
The interface also exposes competing-event treatment, visit processes and
prebaseline lag conventions. Its \texttt{sim\_trunc} option defaults to
true for specified continuous covariate families, restricting simulated
values to the observed range. Such a transformation must be part of the
reported simulation law. For a simple project example,
$P(L=-2,0,2)=(1/4,1/2,1/4)$ gives $\E[L^2]=2$; clipping to $[-1,1]$
gives $1/2$. The numeric range may look safer while the tail-sensitive
financial target changes.

ltmle represents chronology through column order in wide data. Its
treatment nodes must be binary, its survival indicators must remain one
after the event, and its probability bounds concern \emph{cumulative}
treatment/censoring factors. Its output retains influence values and
both bounded and unbounded cumulative probabilities. Continuous outcomes
can be scaled and, when \texttt{Yrange} is supplied, truncated. Some
robust-variance options are unavailable with nonbinary outcomes,
G-computation or other listed options \citep{sw_ltmle}. A sensible adapter
constructs columns from a separately validated clock and records each of
these choices. Renaming an arbitrary real-valued bank action as a binary
node would create a different intervention.

lmtp supplies targeted and sequentially doubly robust estimators for
modified treatment policies, with explicit ordered histories, censoring,
competing events, sampling weights and optional cluster identifiers.
Its finite-history parameter $k$ is a modeling restriction when the full
history is relevant. Its source also resolves a potentially serious
terminological ambiguity. The function \texttt{ipsi} implements a
stochastic retention-or-replacement rule. For
$e(h)=P(A=1\mid H=h)$, direct integration over the auxiliary uniform
random variable in the source gives
\begin{equation}
 q_\delta(1\mid h)=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta e(h),&0\leq\delta\leq1,\\
  1-\{1-e(h)\}/\delta,&\delta>1.
 \end{cases}
 \label{r3:software-ipsi}
\end{equation}
The downward branch scales exposure risk; the upward branch scales
nonexposure risk by $1/\delta$. This differs from the odds multiplier
$\delta e/(1-e+\delta e)$ in Section~\ref{r3:incremental}.
At $e=.2$, $\delta=.5$ produces $.1$ instead of $1/9$;
$\delta=2$ produces $.6$ instead of $1/3$. The corresponding policy means
and influence functions therefore cannot be interchanged. The comparison
is a derivation from inspected source, not a package execution.

The score difference can be made explicit. For a one-time binary action
and a differentiable probability transform $q=f(e)$, let
$m_a(h)=\E[Y\mid A=a,H=h]$ and
$\mu_f(h)=(1-f(e(h)))m_0(h)+f(e(h))m_1(h)$.
Differentiating the outcome regressions, the propensity and the marginal
history law separately, as in Section~\ref{r3:incremental}, gives
\begin{align*}
 \phi_f={}&\frac{Af(e)}{e}(Y-m_1)
       +\frac{(1-A)(1-f(e))}{1-e}(Y-m_0)\\
       &+f'(e)(m_1-m_0)(A-e)+\mu_f-\Psi_f .
\end{align*}
Here histories with $0<e<1$ are considered. For
Equation~\eqref{r3:software-ipsi}, $f'(e)$ is $\delta$ on the downward
branch and $1/\delta$ on the upward branch. For odds tilting it is
$\delta/\{1+(\delta-1)e\}^2$. At $\delta=1$ all reduce to the natural-course
mean and the score reduces to $Y-\E[Y]$. This limiting check and a finite-law
directional derivative are useful acceptance criteria for a policy adapter.

zEpid offers useful Python references for weighting, g-computation,
targeting and transport. Its documentation specifically limits its IPMW
description to monotone missingness and its SNMM g-estimation to a single
time point \citep{sw_zepid}. An umbrella description of \emph{g-methods}
must not be promoted to an implementation of every longitudinal method.
For collections, bankruptcy, settlement and exit should be represented
as the substantive events of Section~\ref{r3:competing-events}; a library's
censoring switch does not decide which event the bank intended to remove.

\section{A fitted state model is not yet a causal planner}
\label{r3:software-states}

Dynamax is a natural numerical comparator for conditional state-space
likelihoods. The inspected HMM abstraction builds initial, transition and
emission components, supplies \texttt{marginal\_log\_prob},
\texttt{filter}, \texttt{smoother}, and an EM E-step
\citep{sw_dynamax}. Its optional external inputs enter through those
components; the standard transition model can be a fixed transition
matrix. Thus an input argument does not prove that a selected subclass
has an action-dependent transition.

More fundamentally, the conditional emission likelihood does not
automatically contain a private action logger. Under the common law of
Section~\ref{r3:state-bridge}, observations of an action can alter the
posterior state through the factor $q_\eta(a_t\mid s_t,h_t)$. If logging is
independent of hidden state conditional on the recorded history, that
factor may cancel from the state update. Otherwise it must be represented
in the observational likelihood. Replacing it by a proposed intervention
then changes the experiment. A state-space adapter must establish this
factorization before fitting; optimizer convergence cannot repair an
omitted likelihood factor.

PyMC and NumPyro can express richer probabilistic models and estimate their
parameters \citep{sw_pymc,sw_numpyro}. They provide numerical inference,
not a general identification theorem. PyMC's inspected example distinguishes
model intervention and observation through \texttt{do} and
\texttt{observe}; their causal interpretation still depends on the supplied
model. NumPyro supports HMC/NUTS, mixed discrete/continuous methods and
variational alternatives. Marginalizing a finite hidden state is often
useful, but it is not the only documented approach to discrete variables.
Comparisons should hold the likelihood and prior fixed and separately
measure integration error, parameter uncertainty and sensitivity to
observationally equivalent causal completions.

POMDPs.jl and pomdp\_py solve another layer of the problem
\citep{sw_pomdps,sw_pomdp_py}. They provide problem representations,
planning and simulation interfaces. The Julia core interface, POMDPTools,
a solver and a Python bridge have separate versions and dependencies.
An adapter must state whether the observation occurs before or after the
transition, what information the policy receives and when reward is paid.
A smoothed state using future bank records cannot be used as an online
decision belief. Solver residuals and rollout error should be evaluated
against the model-conditional value, while the identification and model
error are assessed through Chapter~\ref{r3:controlled-identification}.

d3rlpy, SCOPE-RL and Open Bandit Pipeline offer policy-learning and
evaluation comparators \citep{sw_d3rlpy,sw_scope_rl,sw_obp}. Their natural
objects differ: a fitted policy, a sequential return estimate or return
distribution, and a contextual-bandit reward. A one-period contact reward
cannot represent a multimonth recovery path with carryover. Occupancy-ratio
OPE and trajectory-ratio OPE also require different sufficient-information
and coverage conditions. The rare-path construction in
Section~\ref{r3:ope-hardness} is a relevant stress case even when each
logged action has a positive probability.

\section{Discovery outputs must retain their unresolved information}
\label{r3:software-discovery}

The graph is a scientific output with a type. Tigramite's documentation
distinguishes PCMCI, PCMCI+, LPCMCI and other variants, and separately lists
the restrictions of conditional-independence tests \citep{sw_tigramite}.
Selecting a nonlinear test does not remove a stationarity assumption;
adding a missing-value mask does not identify an informative observation
process. A temporal discovery result must retain lag convention, window,
mask, background knowledge, test and model class.

The inspected causal-learn FCI interface returns a graph marked as a PAG
and edge-property objects. Its matrix distinguishes tails, arrowheads
and circles \citep{sw_causallearn}. Converting that matrix into Boolean
adjacency would erase precisely the information needed for
effect identification. A circle endpoint expresses unresolved ancestral
information; it is not a weakly weighted arrow. Bidirected edges are not
two ordinary causal arrows. The receiving effect operation must reason
over compatible graph completions or use a criterion valid for the
equivalence class, as in Chapter~\ref{r3:discovery}.

NOTEARS and DAGMA supply useful continuous-optimization constructions,
while gCastle collects several algorithm families and Tetrad offers a
separate Java ecosystem \citep{sw_notears,sw_dagma,sw_gcastle,sw_tetrad}.
For the optimization methods, the acyclicity constraint is a statement
about a fitted graph; it is not a proof that the observed law uniquely
identifies that graph. Search tolerances, thresholding and initialization
belong to the numerical output. For a toolbox, the assumptions belong to
the selected algorithm, not to the package name. gCastle's inspected
module distinguishes IID and event-sequence algorithms and marks HPCI
as under development. Tetrad's language bridge and runtime need separate
qualification from a particular search procedure.

Causica combines graph and neural-mechanism fitting within an additive-noise
structural model, then simulates interventions \citep{sw_causica}.
This is a useful comparison where the structural restrictions are justified.
A variational graph distribution conditional on that model is not a
frequentist graph-confidence set or a distribution-free certificate of
causal identification. The current README explicitly says Rhino and
DDECI were removed from the codebase and refers to an earlier release.
Their paper descriptions cannot establish the capability of the current
snapshot. The initial CausalNex repository retrieval failed; that historical
failure is not evidence that the project is abandoned \citep{sw_causalnex}.
The later pinned-source comparison recovers its StructureModel and selected
NOTEARS implementations. Default adoption remains deferred pending a justified
consumer, an isolated compatible environment and dependency qualification;
source retrieval itself is no longer the obstacle
\citep{exec13_pydisc_causalnex}.

\section{Data organization must preserve what was known}
\label{r3:software-data}

DuckDB and Polars provide relational and columnar execution paths;
Pandera supplies explicit schema and value checks
\citep{sw_duckdb,sw_polars,sw_pandera}. These are useful building blocks
for Chapter~\ref{r3:observation}, but type-correct data may still encode
the wrong decision history. An event dated before a credit-limit decision
may have reached the bank after it. A later corrected value can also
replace the value actually used. The history constructor must therefore
enforce event, availability and revision semantics before exporting
predictors to an estimator.

Feast's inspected historical-retrieval API makes the distinction concrete.
It uses event time and TTL, and offers
\texttt{filter\_by\_created\_timestamp}. The latter defaults to false;
when true it excludes later-created values only for feature views with
a configured creation-timestamp field \citep{sw_feast}. Hence it is
incorrect either to assume every point-in-time join captures actual
availability or to claim this capability is entirely absent. The bank
must map its availability semantics to the configured fields and test a
backfill whose event precedes, but creation follows, the decision.
TTL governs freshness and retrieval scope; it cannot establish that mapping.

DataHub and OpenMetadata can supply asset descriptions, ownership,
glossaries and lineage \citep{sw_datahub,sw_openmetadata}. Their graphs
record how data are described and produced; they are not causal graphs
of the customer or economy. A transform that computes arrears from
transactions produces a lineage edge, not evidence that editing the
arrears column would change past transactions. The product should reuse
the bank's catalog and attach the causal interpretation to its stable
asset identifiers. Broad catalog marketing that mixes open-source and
managed-cloud features is not evidence that a particular local deployment
has those features.

OpenLineage supplies an extensible run/job/dataset event model
\citep{sw_openlineage}. A causal-analysis extension should preserve the
target, data snapshot, observation clock, model/graph, split plan and
estimator identity. These are proposed scientific facets, not standard
causal semantics already supplied by OpenLineage. Splink addresses another
part of the observation operator: probabilistic linkage supplies pair
probabilities and estimated entity clusters \citep{sw_splink}. Their
uncertainty matters when a false household merge changes the unit of
treatment or uses post-treatment information. The linkage-variance
decomposition in Section~\ref{r3:entity-uncertainty} explains why a
thresholded ID alone is not a sufficient uncertainty record.

\section{Distributed execution must preserve the score experiment}
\label{r3:software-execution}

After identification and nuisance fitting, some estimates can be reduced
through additive scores. This creates an opportunity for local SQL,
columnar or distributed execution. Ray supplies tasks, actors and shared
objects, while Polars documents streaming and optional GPU execution
\citep{sw_ray,sw_polars}. Neither system specifies the independent
information in a causal analysis.

For a scalar estimating equation $\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_i(\widehat\theta)=0$,
write $\widehat J=n^{-1}\sum_i\partial_\theta\psi_i$.
If sampling clusters $c$ are independent, a basic cluster sandwich uses
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\widehat\theta)=
 \widehat J^{-2}\frac1{n^2}\sum_c
       \left(\sum_{i\in c}\psi_i\right)^2,
 \label{r3:software-cluster-reduction}
\end{equation}
before any stated finite-cluster correction. The reduction key is the
statistical cluster, not the worker partition. With score values
$(1,1,-1,-1)$ in two clusters $(1,1)$ and $(-1,-1)$, the cluster meat is
$8$; treating rows as independent gives $4$. Sharding each cluster across
workers and squaring partial sums before regrouping repeats that error.
Correct distributed execution first sums by stable cluster identity and
then forms the outer products. Multiway clustering and serial dependence
require their own covariance constructions.

Cross-fitting has the same constraint. A fold assignment must be a durable
function of the permitted sampling unit or time block, fixed before
worker scheduling. A retry must not duplicate a score contribution;
repartitioning must not move a household between training and evaluation.
Floating-point reductions may differ across orders, so a declared numerical
tolerance is appropriate, but the statistical partition must be exact.

The resulting qualification sequence is constructive. First verify a
small finite-law functional and its failure cases. Then compare the
adapter's actual target and outputs against a numerical reference.
Next evaluate sampling bias, coverage or policy regret under named
experiments. Finally measure the same scientifically valid computation
under larger loads, including memory, spill, retries and cost. A larger
row count is useful only after these identities are preserved.

\section{What the comparison assigns to the shared product}
\label{r3:software-composition}

The reusable layer should own the intervention and observation
representations, target-preserving transformations, identification evidence,
inference requirements and immutable execution records. Existing libraries
can then supply well-defined numerical operations. A bounded first set
includes adjustment-based effects, valid linear-IV moments, specified
panel/cohort contrasts, finite-horizon observed-history policies and
graph-equivalence discovery outputs. Controlled latent models require a
separate observational/interventional likelihood interface and evidence
for the requested value; supplying a planner alone cannot complete it.

This division also provides a substantive alternative to building the
product. An expert team can compose the same open-source libraries directly.
The shared product has value only if it preserves the scientific contracts
more reliably, reduces repeated data and validation work, and improves
decision throughput at a measured total cost. An estimator wrapper with
a common name adds little. The operations, invalid requests, numerical
obligations and reusable artifacts in Chapter~\ref{r3:product} make this
claim testable. The comparisons here explain why those requirements follow
from the economic question, rather than from a preference for a particular
software interface.

chapters.title: Choosing software by the economic question

segments.text:
\chapter{Choosing software by the economic question}
\label{exec13:survey}

\section{Start with the banking comparison}

A bank considering a causal library faces several different purchasing and
engineering decisions. It may need a defensible effect of an invitation, a
description of plausible causal directions among funding variables, or a
policy for repeated servicing decisions. A package that produces a directed
graph does not necessarily answer the first question. A package that estimates
an average treatment effect does not necessarily answer the third. The survey
therefore takes a scientific operation as its unit of comparison: an input
with a declared observation law, a causal target, assumptions connecting the
two, and an output whose meaning survives conversion into the bank's units.

This choice changes what counts as competitive capability. Consider a request
to increase deposit funding by changing the offered rate. A system that
returns several compatible effects has provided useful information if the
observations cannot distinguish their underlying mechanisms. A system that
returns one number after choosing a convenient graph may have answered a
more restrictive question. The comparison must expose the restriction before
comparing accuracy, speed or convenience. Similarly, a symbolic expression
for an effect and an estimate of that expression are different accomplishments.
The expression identifies what information is needed; its numerical evaluation
adds statistical and computational obligations.

The proposed common request is
\begin{equation}
 q=(\mathcal U,\mathcal T,\mathcal O,\mathcal A,\mathcal Y,
       \Psi,\mathcal G,\mathcal S),
 \label{exec13:request}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal U$ specifies the eligible population and sampling unit,
$\mathcal T$ the decision and measurement clocks, $\mathcal O$ the observed
variables and their units, and $\mathcal A$ the feasible intervention.
$\mathcal Y$ specifies the outcome and horizon. The functional $\Psi$ is the
requested causal quantity; $\mathcal G$ contains the graph or graph class and
its substantive restrictions; $\mathcal S$ describes sampling and uncertainty.
For example, one row may represent one independently sampled eligible
customer, the action may be a 25 basis point increase offered before account
opening, and the outcome may be net funding value over the next quarter.
These declarations are scientific inputs. A software interface cannot establish
them merely by accepting a table with suitable column names. The developed
comparison below follows five R discovery paths from their documented outputs
to the intervention question. It supplies the graph, effect and unit distinctions
behind the broader selection in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:software}; it does not
claim to exhaust the software landscape.

For an observational law $P$ and an admissible model class $\mathcal M$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal I_\Psi(P,\mathcal M)
 =\{\Psi(M):M\in\mathcal M,\ P_M^{\rm obs}=P\}.
 \label{exec13:identified-set}
\end{equation}
This is the collection of target values compatible with the same observations
and assumptions. It is a population object. A finite-sample graph estimate,
an estimated collection of effects, a Bayesian posterior and a confidence set
each add different operations to it. A common result schema must distinguish
these objects. Reducing all four to a scalar and two bounds would make the
schema convenient at the cost of its scientific meaning.

\section{The scope of the comparison}

The landscape has two dimensions that should be searched separately. The
method dimension includes observational, latent-variable and interventional
discovery; identification and counterfactuals; heterogeneous effects;
instrumental variables and discontinuities; longitudinal treatment and survival;
policy evaluation; panels and differences in differences; synthetic controls;
time series; interference; mediation and sensitivity; transport and missingness;
Bayesian structural models; observation construction; and computational
workflow. The implementation dimension distinguishes R, Python, Java,
C/C++, other language paths and commercial offerings. A language binding,
an underlying numerical engine and a commercial wrapper can occupy different
positions in that matrix without being three independent implementations.

The publication cutoff is 7 October 2026. Acquisition time, software revision,
manual generation date and scholarly publication date are retained separately.
This matters even for apparently simple documentation: the inspected pcalg
manual identifies version 2.7-12 and a package date in 2024, while the manual
itself was generated in May 2026. The bnlearn manual identifies version 5.2.1
dated 17 July 2026. BiDAG's inspected manual was generated in May 2026 but
describes a release dated May 2023
\citep{exec13_pcalg,exec13_bnlearn,exec13_bidag}. None of these dates alone
measures current support quality, future maintenance or compatibility with
the proposed product.

A reproducible search records the query, source, date filter, returned
identities, pagination and stopping rule. For the R observational-discovery
comparison developed here, the retained bibliographic query was ``R package
causal discovery constraint score continuous DAG.'' Its saved first page
contains ten records from a reported 1,648 matches. The primary comparison
starts from the inspected pcalg and bnlearn manuals, follows the BCDAG lead,
and then follows one package-reference step to BiDAG and mcmcabn. Those five
paths define the present comparison. Ten bibliographic results are not an
exhaustive R census. The remaining methodological leads do not establish
either the presence or the absence of an R implementation.

There are two useful stopping rules. A discovery pass can stop after a
declared search budget and report incomplete coverage. A capability decision
must instead stop when the evidence is sufficient for the particular claimed
operation, or report that the decision remains unresolved. The first rule
controls search cost; the second controls the strength of the conclusion.
Conflating them would allow an arbitrary search budget to become evidence
that a missing capability does not exist. Conversely, insisting on an
unbounded census before discussing any inspected package would prevent useful
comparisons indefinitely.

The comparisons use inspected original technical texts and the manuals or
source for the stated revisions. Their conclusions concern documented
behavior; discovery metadata alone supplies no algorithmic guarantee. An
unavailable original leaves the associated capability unresolved. The
accompanying source register records identities, rights, local copies,
digests and the technical anchors supporting each claim.

Conflicting evidence also requires a dated resolution. The authentic BCDAG
preprint from 2022 is useful for its Gaussian model and posterior construction.
Its contemporary package comparison cannot determine what bnlearn supports
in 2026. The inspected bnlearn manual now documents intervention and
counterfactual operations \citep{exec13_bcdag_paper,exec13_bnlearn}.
The sensible conclusion is that the comparison changed with the software.
This does not establish the validity of any particular causal use of bnlearn;
it corrects a capability description at a named version.

\section{What the five R paths actually return}

The five packages illustrate why language and algorithm labels are insufficient.
Table~\ref{exec13:r-comparison} compares their documented outputs. It is a
source-based comparison, not a benchmark of their implementations.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Selected R paths and the distinction their outputs require.}
\label{exec13:r-comparison}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}P{.15\linewidth}XX@{}}
\toprule
Path & Documented object & Decision-relevant restriction \\
\midrule
pcalg & Partial graph or graph class; IDA effect multiset & PC discovery,
latent-variable discovery and effect calculation have distinct assumptions. \\
bnlearn & Learned network; fitted parameters; causal queries & Score search,
functional discovery and intervention queries do not share one guarantee. \\
BCDAG & Graph and parameter draws; effect posterior & Gaussian model and
graph/parameter priors define the posterior; credible intervals retain that label. \\
BiDAG & MAP graph or sampled graphs & Score, admissible search space,
parent limits and sampling configuration constrain the answer. \\
mcmcabn & Score-cache graph samples and structural queries & Arc frequency
is a structural summary; outcome intervention effects require further modeling. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

In pcalg, the PC interface requires a conditional-independence test and its
significance level. Its stable skeleton option addresses ordering in the
skeleton search; it does not by itself settle all orientation conflicts.
Conservative and majority-rule variants treat ambiguous triples differently.
Some configurations can return a partial graph that is not extendable to a
DAG, and conflict-handling options can introduce bidirected marks with an
algorithmic meaning \citep{exec13_pcalg}. An importer must preserve that
meaning. Such a conflict is not automatically evidence of a latent common
cause, even though bidirected edges have a substantive interpretation in
other graphical formalisms.

A particularly consequential default is \texttt{NAdelete=TRUE}: a missing
independence-test result can cause an edge to be deleted. In the proposed
banking boundary, a failed statistical calculation should produce a diagnostic
response with its cause. It should not become evidence that two financial
variables are independent. Merely changing the option to false is also
insufficient if a failed test is then silently treated as dependence. The
wrapper must detect a missing or nonfinite result and stop that numerical
request. The package's documented flexibility and the product's selected
behavior are therefore different layers of the comparison.

The bnlearn family provides a different breadth. Its constraint-based defaults
depend on variable type, while its score-based and hybrid methods expose
different search controls. The inspected documentation gives an $\alpha$ of
0.05 for constraint procedures, locally complete observations for individual
tests with missing data, BIC defaults for common score searches, and no random
restarts by default for hill climbing. The MMHC and H2PC names denote
compositions of restriction and maximization procedures, rather than new
independent guarantees. DirectLiNGAM uses a separate functional-model route
with its own ordering and selection choices \citep{exec13_bnlearn}.
For a bank, this breadth supports useful baselines, but it also makes an
unqualified ``bnlearn result'' an inadequate description of an experiment.

BCDAG makes graph uncertainty explicit through a Gaussian DAG model and
posterior sampling. Its compatible DAG-Wishart construction is described in
the original preprint; the inspected version 1.1.4 manual distinguishes
structure-only sampling, joint graph/parameter sampling, effect summaries and
credible intervals \citep{exec13_bcdag_paper,exec13_bcdag}. The
\texttt{fast} option changes the proposal-ratio calculation through an
approximation; its default is false. A comparison must therefore specify
the graph prior, parameter hyperparameters, burn-in, retained draws, chain
configuration and approximation setting. A stable trace is useful diagnostic
evidence but is not a proof that a finite chain explored all consequential
graph regions.

BiDAG's order and partition samplers expose another tradeoff. A search space
can begin with a PC-derived skeleton and then be expanded. A MAP graph under
that space and a sample from a specified posterior serve different purposes.
Parent limits and the expansion strategy influence both computation and what
can be learned \citep{exec13_bidag}. If a true funding relationship was
excluded during search-space construction, a later apparently stable graph
sample cannot recover it without a mechanism that admits it. A benchmark
must consequently compare declared search procedures, not only the final
graphs after favorable tuning.

The mcmcabn documentation starts from a precomputed score cache, commonly
constructed with abn, and describes structural MCMC moves, priors and
structural queries \citep{exec13_mcmcabn}. This provides an alternative for
mixed node distributions and explicit structural prior beliefs. It also
introduces a scoring dependency whose assumptions and version belong to the
scientific input. The inspected documentation contains a conversion issue:
a named example places the Smoking-to-LungCancer prior at the row for the
child and column for the parent, while explanatory prose in the vignette
describes rows as parents and columns as children. A proposed integration
must resolve this discrepancy with named-node source and runtime checks.
Silently choosing one convention would be an avoidable scientific error.

These comparisons support a narrow initial choice: a pcalg route for explicitly
typed discovery and effect multisets, bnlearn as a method-specific alternative,
and Bayesian routes as separately configured sensitivity comparisons.
They do not justify porting every algorithm into a new library. The Bayesian
routes may be particularly informative when prior restrictions are part of
the scientific question; their value should be assessed by changing those
restrictions and reporting the resulting decision sensitivity.

\section{An exact funding example: identical observations, different actions}

Consider centered continuous variables $X$, $M$ and $Y$. In this constructed
example $X$ is an offered-rate margin measured in percentage points, $M$ is
a continuous funding-response index, and $Y$ is subsequent net funding value
in thousands of currency units. The index is not a binary take-up indicator.
For this first comparison, the admissible class uses the cross-sectional law
and acyclicity alone: assignment and temporal-order evidence have deliberately
been withheld. A verified banking clock would exclude any reverse model that
contradicts it. The example isolates what the observational law itself can
establish. Let the disturbances below be mutually independent standard Gaussians:
\begin{equation}
 X=\varepsilon_X,\qquad M=0.6X+\varepsilon_M,
 \qquad Y=0.8M+\varepsilon_Y.
 \label{exec13:forward}
\end{equation}
Under the causal interpretation of these equations, replacing the equation
for $X$ by a fixed assignment gives a total derivative of $0.6\times0.8=0.48$.
The observational covariance matrix, in the order $(X,M,Y)$, is
\begin{equation}
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0.6&0.48\\
 0.6&1.36&1.088\\
 0.48&1.088&1.8704
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \label{exec13:covariance}
\end{equation}
The partial covariance of $X$ and $Y$ given $M$ vanishes because
$0.48-0.6(1.088)/1.36=0$. For the Gaussian law this is the conditional
independence $X\perp Y\mid M$.

That same covariance admits the fork $X\leftarrow M\rightarrow Y$.
Take $\Var(M)=1.36$, regress $X$ on $M$ with coefficient $0.6/1.36$,
and retain the coefficient $0.8$ from $M$ to $Y$. Independent residual
variances are $1-0.6^2/1.36$ for $X$ and $1$ for $Y$. They are positive,
and the resulting covariance is exactly~\eqref{exec13:covariance}.
Intervening on $X$ now changes neither $M$ nor $Y$, so its total effect on
$Y$ is zero.

The reverse chain $X\leftarrow M\leftarrow Y$ provides a third representation.
Let $\Var(Y)=1.8704$, use coefficient $1.088/1.8704$ from $Y$ to $M$,
and $0.6/1.36$ from $M$ to $X$. The residual variance for $M$ is
$1.36-1.088^2/1.8704$, and that for $X$ is again $1-0.6^2/1.36$.
This gives the same observed law and again gives zero effect of $X$ on $Y$.
The distinct effect values across these three models are therefore
\begin{equation}
 \{0,\,0.48\}.
 \label{exec13:effect-set}
\end{equation}
The repeated zero matters if a procedure retains graph multiplicities; the
set of distinct values and a multiset must not be confused. All covariance
equalities and effects in this example have been checked with exact rational
arithmetic \citep{exec13_examples}. No discovery engine was run to obtain
them, and no finite-sample recovery rate is implied.

An observational search that preserves the undirected path $X-M-Y$ is
consistent with this ambiguity. A procedure that selects the forward chain
has supplied a graph choice in addition to the observational information.
This is precisely the distinction the IDA multiset makes useful in its
specified linear Gaussian setting \citep{exec13_pcalg}. Additional knowledge
can change the model class: a justified temporal ordering, an intervention
or a substantive structural restriction may exclude one of the alternative
graphs. Merely naming $X$ an ``offer'' does not document that restriction.
The bank must establish how the offer was assigned and when the relevant
variables were generated and observed.

The difference has an immediate monetary consequence. If $X_{\rm bp}=100X$
and $Y_{\rm currency}=1000Y$, then the forward-model derivative becomes
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\partial\E[Y_{\rm currency}\mid\doop(X_{\rm bp}=x)]}{\partial x}
 =\frac{1000}{100}\,0.48=4.8.
 \label{exec13:units}
\end{equation}
A 25 basis point change gives 120 currency units per eligible customer in
this linear construction, or 1.2 million over 10,000 such customers if the
same additive, noninterfering mechanism applies to each. The other two
compatible models give zero. These are conditional planning calculations,
not measured revenue or an investment recommendation. Aggregation and a
currency conversion cannot remove the underlying identification ambiguity.

\section{Keep graph ambiguity, statistical uncertainty and prior uncertainty apart}

The example separates uncertainties that are often compressed into one
picture. Even with the population covariance known exactly, the three causal
representations disagree about the intervention. Finite observations introduce
additional uncertainty about covariance and conditional independences.
If a graph is chosen from those observations, subsequent effect estimation
also depends on that choice. A graph-equivalence multiset is consequently
not a confidence interval with a nominal repeated-sampling coverage level.
Taking its convex hull may be useful for a conservative decision rule, but
the hull loses information about disconnected possibilities and multiplicity.

A Bayesian analysis describes another object. Write $G$ for a DAG and
$\vartheta_G$ for its parameters. The posterior distribution of an effect
can be expressed as
\begin{equation}
 \Pi(\theta\in B\mid D)
 =\sum_G \Pi(G\mid D)
   \int\ind\{\Psi(G,\vartheta_G)\in B\}
            \,d\Pi(\vartheta_G\mid G,D),
 \label{exec13:posterior}
\end{equation}
where $D$ denotes the observed data and $B$ a measurable set of effect values.
The graph prior, conditional parameter prior and likelihood jointly determine
this distribution. Compatible priors can assign the same marginal likelihood
to Markov-equivalent Gaussian DAGs, as described in the BCDAG construction
\citep{exec13_bcdag_paper}. Observational equivalence has not disappeared:
different graph weights can still reflect prior restrictions or different
admissible model classes.

The BCDAG method named \texttt{confint.bcdagCE} explicitly reports credible
intervals \citep{exec13_bcdag}. Its function name is not a reason to label
the output a frequentist confidence interval. The proposed result therefore
stores the uncertainty family, conditioning assumptions and computational
method alongside the numerical bounds. It also retains the prior and MCMC
configuration for posterior results. If a later simulation claims coverage,
that is a separate empirical statement about a specified repeated-sampling
experiment, with all failed and unavailable requests retained in its denominator.

The distinction is consequential for investment. A concentrated posterior
under a strong orientation prior can support a conditional decision while
still leaving the prior's banking justification unsettled. Conversely, an
effect collection containing zero can reveal that a proposed rate experiment
has informational value. The relevant question is then whether a feasible
experiment can distinguish the mechanisms sufficiently to change the action.
The product should make that unresolved decision visible rather than display
a more precise-looking number obtained by silently discarding alternatives.

\section{Targets must survive an identification or estimation boundary}

DoWhy provides a useful model of separating a supplied causal model,
identification and estimation. The inspected source revision is
\texttt{b06369ed} from 4 October 2026. Its graph-learning entry point is
deprecated, and its identification path operates on supplied graph,
treatment, outcome and observed-node information \citep{exec13_dowhy}.
The proposed reuse is therefore an optional identification service for an
explicit reviewed graph. It does not treat the package as an automatic
authority on the bank's diagram or as a universal discovery engine.

An exact second example shows why the target belongs to the interface.
Let $W$ be a baseline customer characteristic, $A$ a binary invitation and
$Y$ an outcome measured in thousands of currency units. Suppose
\begin{align}
 \Prob(W=1)&=\tfrac12, &
 e(W):=\Prob(A=1\mid W)&=0.2+0.6W,\\
 \E[Y(a)\mid W]&=3W+a(1+2W).&&
 \label{exec13:target-law}
\end{align}
Under consistency, exchangeability conditional on $W$, positivity and no
interference, the population average effect is
\begin{equation}
 \ATE=\sum_{w=0}^1
 \{\E[Y\mid A=1,w]-\E[Y\mid A=0,w]\}\Prob(W=w)=2.
 \label{exec13:ate}
\end{equation}
The treated group has $\Prob(W=1\mid A=1)=0.8$, while the untreated group
