and the outer wait is three seconds, the specified path takes \(24+6+3=33\) seconds. These values are exact
bookkeeping under the stated assumptions, not vendor prices or a measured service guarantee.~\citep{exec28_oa_reference}

The proposed admission layer should reserve a workflow-wide attempt and cost budget before issuing calls,
debit actual attempts, retain response identifiers and unknown outcomes, and distinguish cancellation requested
from cancellation observed. Public prototype tests should include an error after remote work may have begun,
an incomplete stream, a refusal, invalid tool arguments and a timeout during a tool result. The complete
denominator includes these cases. Financial value remains a separate assessment of decision quality and full
workflow costs; cheap valid JSON is not a monetary benefit by definition.

\subsection{Comparison and a bounded reuse choice}
The existing comparison treats Anthropic and Google client contracts, Ollama request and stream behavior,
and the parser, template and generation settings of vLLM and llama.cpp separately. The newly inspected OpenAI
originals add a sixth named provider/client family with explicit parsing, refusal, phase and retry rules.
Across these profiles, one adapter should preserve native status and error information before mapping it into
the common scientific envelope. Compatibility in endpoint spelling cannot prove equivalence in parsing,
model behavior, cancellation or cost.~\citep{exec24_backend_anthropic,exec24_backend_google,exec24_backend_ollama,exec24_backend_vllm,exec24_backend_llamacpp,exec28_oa_sdk}

The bounded proposal choice is conditional adoption of the original client behind a thin, versioned adapter,
rather than a wholesale port. The inspected SDK and cookbook carry Apache 2.0 and MIT notices respectively;
these notices concern those source artifacts. They do not establish service entitlement, model-weight rights,
data permissions or approved bank deployment. An implementation decision still requires the exact endpoint,
model, dependencies, configured retry policy and applicable service terms. The official live guide access
failure also remains an omission; the recovered repository originals establish their own narrower contracts.
No downloaded code or live model was executed in this review.~\citep{exec28_oa_sdk,exec28_oa_cookbook}

CLI and MCP should expose the same typed outcome, including nonidentification, scientific rejection, refusal,
incomplete output and transport uncertainty. Framework scheduling must consume this outcome rather than infer
success from text presence. This supplies a concrete route for a low-cost public prototype: freeze the client
and adapter identities, register adversarial response-state fixtures, verify the scientific envelope against
independent answers, and only then compare live backends under a declared budget. The source comparison reduces
an architectural uncertainty while leaving native performance, service terms and bank effectiveness open.
The banking decision remains admissible only when its scientific meaning survives the complete request lifecycle.

\section[Framework delegates and scientific completion]{When a completed software call leaves the research unfinished}
\label{sec:exec28-dl}
A causal workflow can finish its control flow without producing an admissible causal answer.
For a collections analyst, the distinction is practical. A reminder-policy analysis may return an
object after its structured-output step failed, repeat a tool after an interrupted response, or
accept a treatment identifier under a weakened constraint. Each event changes what the analyst can
infer from the result. A framework comparison must therefore follow the delegated implementation
of validation, stopping, retry and recovery, rather than infer these properties from a common API.
The following comparison concerns selected, pinned original source paths. It motivates product
contracts and public qualification experiments; it does not report executed vendor integrations.

\subsection{Validation must survive the complete calling path}
LangChain's inspected tool base distinguishes a dictionary schema from a Pydantic model. In the
dictionary branch of the input parser, the supplied input is returned; the Pydantic branch invokes
model validation and handles an injected tool-call identifier. This local branch difference does
not prove that no other layer validates a dictionary-schema request. It does show why the proposed
adapter cannot treat the presence of a schema as evidence that validation occurred at every entry
point. The same source can convert a handled validation or tool exception into an error-status tool
message. The consumer must preserve that status even when the returned content is readable text.
\citep{exec28_dl_langchain}

DSPy's inspected tool helper iterates over provided arguments, conditionally validates a field
against its schema when a qualifying type is present, then uses typed parsing for applicable
arguments. Its synchronous and asynchronous call paths also differ in coroutine handling. Google
GenAI's function-declaration helper builds a schema from a callable signature and type information,
including required fields and definitions; an inspected Vertex conversion branch supplies an
object type for an otherwise untyped union. These are useful mechanisms for translating interfaces.
They do not establish that a variable precedes treatment, that a graph encodes the business question,
or that omitted information is scientifically harmless. Conditional adoption should retain the
original helper while placing a common causal-request validator at the library boundary.
\citep{exec28_dl_dspy,exec28_dl_google}

Consider a request whose treatment identifier must contain a digit. Within the stipulated domain
\(D=\{\texttt{x},\texttt{7}\}\), the intended accepted set is
\(S=\{\texttt{7}\}\). If a conversion relaxes the restriction to any string, the accepted set becomes
\(\widetilde S=D\), so \(S\subsetneq\widetilde S\). The extra value is a false admission under the
original contract. This finite authored witness establishes the logical consequence of weakening;
it is not an observed generation or a measured package failure.~\citep{exec28_dl_reference}

The distinction matters for llama.cpp's inspected schema-to-grammar converter. An unsupported
regular-expression pattern can generate a warning and fall back to any string, whereas an invalid
pattern is recorded as an error. The converter subsequently raises recorded errors and prints
warnings. A separate build/configuration path can use LLGuidance; the warning behavior must not be
generalized to every backend. The selected chat-template path chooses schema-derived grammar or a
supplied grammar, while a separate argument parser can retain text when JSON parsing fails.
Consequently, grammar generation, parse success and validation against the original schema are
three distinct observations. The proposed library should retain conversion diagnostics and the
selected grammar backend, and validate the completed payload against the original request before
admitting an effect. Wholesale porting would inherit these semantic choices and add maintenance
cost without removing the need for this validation.~\citep{exec28_dl_llamacpp}

\subsection{A stop event is a control state, not a scientific certificate}
In LlamaIndex's inspected agent workflow, structured-response generation can raise an exception
that is converted to a warning before the workflow returns a stop event. Its early-stop generation
option can also make another model call to construct a final response. Thus, a terminal event alone
cannot certify a valid structured answer. In LangChain's classic agent, forced stopping returns a
limit response, while the generation option can request a final model answer. The synchronous loop
updates elapsed time between steps; that observation is narrower than a claim that all outstanding
remote operations are cancelled at a wall-clock limit.~\citep{exec28_dl_llama_index,exec28_dl_langchain}

Let \(T\) indicate terminal control flow, \(V\) validation of the scientific envelope, and \(I\)
admission of the requested effect under declared assumptions. The proposed scalar-effect gate is
\(T\land V\land I\). An exact four-case construction admits only the terminal, valid, identified
case. A completed nonidentification result remains a legitimate answer with a different disposition;
a terminal structured-output failure remains a failed representation; an incomplete stream remains
incomplete. The gate specifies responsibility, not the truth of a bank's assumptions. A framework
owns its execution state, the adapter checks representation and preserves errors, and the causal
library supplies the identification argument.~\citep{exec28_dl_reference}

Semantic Kernel's inspected chat agent combines arguments and execution settings before delegating
to a selected provider. Its function wrapper invokes filters, records errors and propagates
exceptions; the streaming path can yield partial results. These hooks are useful integration
locations, but the inspected wrapper does not establish a causal validator. Haystack validates
components, sockets and mandatory inputs; its execution wrapper checks the returned mapping and
output names, and a blocked queue can raise an error. Such checks protect pipeline structure.
They should be retained alongside a separate validation of the target, information clock, graph,
estimand and uncertainty claim. A proposed CLI command and MCP tool should return the same typed
scientific disposition even when their orchestration frameworks differ.
\citep{exec28_dl_semantic_kernel,exec28_dl_haystack}

\subsection{Budgets must count actual attempts and side effects}
LangChain recommends placing retries around the smallest operation that needs them. Its inspected
retry wrapper has configurable exception handling and backoff; the batch path retains successful
items and retries failed original indices. Suppose three independent items \(a,b,c\) run once,
only \(b\) fails, and \(b\) needs two further attempts. Selective retry makes \(1+3+1=5\) item
attempts, whereas repeating the whole three-item batch three times makes nine. At a stipulated
USD 0.25 per item attempt, the costs are USD 1.25 and USD 2.25. These exact accounting examples
are not vendor prices. They also assume that retained successes are valid and that the repeated
operation is safe to retry; neither property follows merely from an exception class.
\citep{exec28_dl_langchain,exec28_dl_reference}

Google GenAI's inspected HTTP path converts configured milliseconds into seconds and supports
request-specific retry settings in addition to client defaults. The inspected server-timeout header
rounds seconds upward. Haystack's visit limit applies to an individual component, while a workflow
can traverse several components. A business-request budget must therefore count HTTP attempts,
tool attempts, generation calls, waiting time and unresolved outcomes explicitly. A framework
iteration cap, a component visit cap and an HTTP timeout are different limits.
\citep{exec28_dl_google,exec28_dl_haystack}

Anthropic's pinned tool-runner documentation describes dispatch by native stop reason. Tool-use
responses trigger tools; paused turns and compaction can require continuation; other stop states
terminate the iterator after yielding the message. Its documented eager streaming mode can execute
a tool before the overall reply finishes. If that reply is interrupted, the tool's effect cannot be
undone merely by discarding the conversation, and the model may request the call again. The same
documentation describes compaction calls outside the ordinary iteration count and nested usage
accounting. Two ordinary turns plus one separate compaction make three calls in an authored counting
example. A top-level counter cannot be assumed to represent the complete cost denominator.
\citep{exec28_dl_anthropic,exec28_dl_reference}

For the reminder-policy workflow, graph inspection and effect calculation can be read-only tools;
dispatching an actual reminder is a different operation. The proposal should assign stable operation
identities, preserve pending results, and require a deduplication or reconciliation policy before
retrying actions with external effects. Cancellation requested and cancellation observed must be
separate states. A failed or unknown outcome remains in the denominator when comparing cost and
reliability. These are proposed architectural requirements, not a claim that any reviewed framework
already supplies end-to-end exactly-once execution.

\subsection{Recovery, native stop reasons and learned programs}
The inspected delegated workflow context describes a process-local store and serialization of
state, event queues, buffers and related execution metadata. Cancellation is delegated for an
external context, while other context states issue warnings. Serialization can support resumption,
but this source path alone cannot establish that a remote action and a local checkpoint commit
atomically. The proposed recovery record must therefore include both local state and unresolved
external-operation identities. Tests should interrupt immediately before and after issuing a tool,
receiving its result and recording the result.~\citep{exec28_dl_workflows}

Native stop reasons also need to survive compatibility adapters. Anthropic's selected type includes
refusal, pause, tool use, output limits and context exhaustion. In vLLM's inspected serving path,
parser selection depends on tool and reasoning settings, strictness, the model and tokenizer.
Its compatibility finish reason can depend on tool mode and generated tool content while retaining
the native stop reason. llama.cpp distinguishes native end-of-sequence, stop-word and limit states
before constructing compatibility fields; the task structure also retains cancellation targets and
parent-child identities. These source representations support a concrete preservation requirement.
They do not independently prove that cancellation has reached every child or that two servers with
similar response fields provide equivalent behavior.~\citep{exec28_dl_anthropic,exec28_dl_vllm,exec28_dl_llamacpp}

Optimization introduces another boundary. DSPy's inspected bootstrap procedure selects traces from
training examples. A variable called validation contains the unbootstrapped training subset, and
success depends on the configured metric; without a metric, the inspected branch accepts success.
The threshold branch also depends on its truth value. These are selected source semantics, not a
claim of a general empirical defect. A causal assistant still needs separately held-out tasks with
independent expected answers, including nonidentification, invalid adjustment and ambiguous graph
cases. Optimizing a demonstration-selection metric cannot by itself establish causal validity on
new banking questions.~\citep{exec28_dl_dspy}

\subsection{A bounded adoption and qualification decision}
The proposal favors thin adapters around selected original clients and orchestration components.
LangChain contributes composable calls and scoped retries; Semantic Kernel contributes provider and
function hooks; Haystack contributes explicit pipeline structure; LlamaIndex and its delegated
workflow package contribute orchestration and recovery representations; DSPy contributes a candidate
optimization layer subject to an independent evaluation contract. The decision is conditional
integration, with scientific validation owned by the causal library. It rejects automatic promotion
of terminal messages into effects, implicit schema weakening, unmeasured retry economics and
unqualified wholesale ports.~\citep{exec28_dl_langchain,exec28_dl_semantic_kernel,exec28_dl_haystack,exec28_dl_llama_index,exec28_dl_workflows,exec28_dl_dspy}

For hosted backends, client source inspection and service qualification remain separate. For local
backends, the exact server build, model, tokenizer, template, parser and grammar configuration are
part of the candidate. Ollama's selected README itself requires a separately running server and a
selected model; its client identity cannot substitute for those artifacts. README migration or
product-focus statements likewise supply leads, not inherited qualification: the Semantic Kernel
README names a successor framework, and the LlamaIndex README names parsing products and benchmarks.
Those separate products require their own primary-source comparison before adoption claims.
\citep{exec28_dl_ollama,exec28_dl_semantic_kernel,exec28_dl_llama_index}

A low-cost public qualification suite can now be specified precisely. It should present an invalid
original-schema value, a handled tool error, a structured-output failure followed by a terminal event,
a partly failed batch, an interrupted side-effecting call, a compaction call outside the ordinary
counter, and a limit stop containing a valid-looking prefix. Each fixture needs an independent expected
scientific disposition, attempt ledger and recovery outcome. Subsequent native trials require exact
artifacts, rights and declared budgets; bank effectiveness remains a later experiment. The comparison
supports these targeted experiments without converting static source inspection into measured merit.
The causal answer is trustworthy only when its meaning survives validation, scheduling, stopping and recovery.

\subsection{The component choice follows its scientific contract}

The complete comparison makes a conditional architecture possible without
assuming that every attractive component belongs in it. Typed representations
can preserve an effect set; source and state identities can expose stale work;
a deterministic controller can retain refusals and unknown outcomes. The
evaluation, memory, specialist-interface and code-generation studies show why
these properties still need task-specific tests, independent references and
complete cost accounting. Their distinct failure mechanisms determine what
should be checked before reuse.

The initial investment is therefore a bounded comparison against the existing
controller and a structured analyst workflow. A selected original client or
framework needs its own exact environment and behavioral qualification. No
source profile supplies causal truth, a universal performance ranking or bank
acceptance. The following synthesis draws together the assistance and
implementation choices while retaining those limits.

chapters.title: Assistance and implementation choices

segments.text:
\chapter{Assistance and implementation choices}
\label{sw:agents}

The preceding comparison establishes the component choices. This chapter
returns to the operation boundary that makes those choices useful: a
directional suggestion, a reviewed request and a qualified result are
different objects. The pairwise example makes the distinction concrete;
the remaining argument follows it through language boundaries, matched
qualification and commercial alternatives.


\section{A directional suggestion is a proposal}

Language assistance can help an analyst translate a business question into
variables, explain candidate diagrams, retrieve documentation and construct a
tool request. Those operations are useful even when a language model cannot
identify an effect from the available information. The software boundary should
make that distinction explicit: a model-generated proposition enters an evidence
and review process before it changes the graph used for causal inference.

The inspected pgmpy \texttt{LLMPairwise} implementation is an instructive
concrete example. It requires exactly two variables and builds its prompt from
their names and optional descriptions. Observed values are not used to orient
the edge. The prompt asks the model to choose one of two directions and the
result constructs a graph with one directed edge. There is no output choice
for no edge, a common cause, insufficient information or a retained graph
alternative. \cite{v12_sw_pgmpy}

This design may be suitable for collecting a narrowly defined directional
suggestion. It cannot by itself answer a broader question about whether two
bank variables are causally connected. ``Contact'' and ``distress'' may refer
to variables at different times, and a bank can contact distressed customers
while earlier contact also changes later distress. Names without clocks do
not determine the causal question. The project graph-equivalence example in
Chapter~\ref{sw:interfaces} also shows that observational ambiguity can remain
even with data; a forced linguistic choice does not resolve that mathematical
ambiguity.

Two implementation details strengthen the case for treating the output as a
proposal. The selected internal cache uses the unordered pair of names as its
key. Description, prompt, provider/model and sampling parameters are not part
of that key. If an instance retains this cache across calls, changed semantics
can therefore reuse an old orientation. This is a static conditional finding
about the cache path; the full estimator lifecycle has not been executed.
An integration test must establish when state is retained and verify
invalidation against the actual call contract. \cite{v12_sw_pgmpy}

The response parser searches first for a digit 1 or 2, then for an A/B token.
A sentence containing such a digit can be interpreted as an orientation even
when its meaning is a refusal. For example, the text ``neither option 1 nor
option 2 is justified'' contains a first matching digit. The proposed
integration should use a strict structured response with explicit abstention
and preserve the raw response. Parser acceptance is a syntactic property;
it cannot establish the truth of the extracted direction.

The decision for this inspected path is therefore to reject direct use of its
raw edge as a qualified discovery result. An exploratory assistant could still
use it after adding a complete request identity, structured abstention,
independent source checks and graph alternatives. Those changes would need
their own review and evaluation. They are proposed remedies, not already
verified upstream or project behavior.

\section{Evidence and authority must travel separately}

An assistant might accurately quote a package manual yet request an operation
that the organization has not approved. It might also request an approved
operation for a causally invalid target. Evidence, scientific applicability
and operational authority are separate inputs. A citation is evidence for a
claim in its scope; it is not authority to execute an action. A successful
schema check is evidence that a declaration has the expected shape; it is not
evidence that a business owner certified the declaration.

The proposed workflow binds a reviewed target and graph declaration to an
exact input identity. The selected operation consumes that declaration,
returns typed results and retains the chain from the question to the
assumptions, method and output. Changes to the treatment clock, target
population or diagram create a different scientific request. A cached
numeric result or prior approval should not silently follow those changes.

Retrieved documentation must be treated as source material. Text inside a
manual, repository or model response cannot grant itself permission to select
another tool, change the target or publish a decision. For the product user,
the meaningful consequence is a reviewable record of which evidence supported
which proposition and which person or authorized process accepted the
scientific declaration. Internal file names and routing details are not
substitutes for that explanation.

\section{One operation across library, CLI and MCP}

A reusable causal product can expose a library call, a command-line request
and an MCP tool for the same operation. Their success criterion is semantic
equivalence. Given the same complete request and execution policy, each should
preserve the target, graph endpoints, expression or set topology, numerical
units, missingness and refusal state. The transport should not narrow a PAG
to a DAG, replace a disconnected set with a pair of endpoints, or turn an
unsupported request into a zero effect.

This motivates a narrow integration boundary. A discovery operation returns
a graph object together with the test and search settings needed to interpret
it. An identification operation returns an expression or a typed failure in
the supplied model class. An estimation operation returns its target,
uncertainty and numerical diagnostics. A policy-value operation returns the
specified regime and horizon. A consumer can combine these operations only
when their contracts match; the mere availability of a tool name does not
establish that match.

For Tetrad, the initial bridge candidate is a Java process with explicit graph
serialization. This isolates runtime management but adds startup, transfer
and error-mapping costs. Its inspected root POM declares compiler release 21,
while the inspected README describes Java JDK 25+ for bridge use. These are
distinct source observations requiring an actual environment qualification;
choosing one by assumption would conceal a deployment uncertainty.
\cite{v12_sw_tetrad}

For the selected R estimators, a process boundary can preserve the native
method and dependencies. A direct Python interface can reduce translation
for causal-learn and selected pgmpy operations. For aGrUM, comparing the
existing wrapper with native C++ calls can clarify whether serialization or
binding overhead matters for the intended workload. These are candidate
routes. No downloaded package was executed for the inspections reported in
this reader.

Porting should be justified by a concrete advantage: unavailable deployment
environments, a measured bottleneck, a required result representation or a
maintenance constraint. It carries an obligation to reproduce the complete
procedure, including error behavior and uncertainty. Rewriting only a point
estimate while retaining a familiar method name would create a misleading
compatibility claim. Direct adoption also requires a dependency and license
review; a permissive root license does not settle every bundled component.

\section{A matched trial needs scientific and operational failures}

Qualification begins with an exact supported request and a suitable reference.
For a graph operation, independent endpoint fixtures and known graph classes
test representation and algorithm scope. For an estimator, analytically
tractable mechanisms or an independently reviewed implementation test the
target and numerical behavior. For a confidence set, evaluation must retain
empty, disconnected and unbounded outputs. For a longitudinal procedure, a
mechanism with action-dependent histories tests whether the intervention was
preserved. Ordinary and difficult cases belong in the same declared trial.

The measured workflow includes serialization, process startup, dependency
loading, fitting, uncertainty and result publication. A bridge that improves
fit time but dominates total latency with transfer costs may be a poor choice
for small requests. Conversely, an expensive startup may be acceptable for a
large repeated analysis if the process lifecycle is controlled. A comparison
should retain both outcomes rather than report only the most favorable
component timer.

Failure injection tests a different property from statistical calibration.
Interrupted input transfer, worker failure and interrupted publication should
not create a partly valid result. Replay needs immutable inputs and exact
predecessor artifacts. If a method uses randomness, its seed and configuration
belong in the request record, while nondeterministic numerical behavior needs
a stated tolerance. A recoverable execution record makes the calculation
auditable; it does not prove its causal assumptions.

No general preference for a process bridge, a native binding or a port can
be established without these measurements. The current source evidence does
support a narrower decision: evaluate existing implementations first where
their contracts fit, preserve distinct outputs and failures, and reject
interfaces that force unsupported scientific meaning without a reviewed
adaptation.

\section{Commercial comparison and the remaining evidence boundary}

The commercial comparison must operate at the same level of specificity.
For each vendor edition, the evidence should identify the estimator or graph
operation, its supported data and assumptions, uncertainty and diagnostic
outputs, automation interface, license boundary and dated cost information.
A product brochure can establish that a capability is advertised; it cannot
substitute for technical documentation of the method or an actual trial.

The selected community Stata package demonstrates why runtime and vendor
capability must be separated. It may extend an organization's Stata workflow,
but that observation does not establish what the vendor ships, licenses or
supports. Similarly, a graphical application component does not establish a
commercial causal-identification engine. Where essential vendor originals
remain unavailable, the capability comparison is unverified; it is not a
finding that the vendor lacks the feature.

The immediate engineering requirements are nevertheless concrete. Preserve
scientific targets and uncertainty objects, expose method-specific unsupported
states, qualify language boundaries, and evaluate whole workflows under
declared assumptions. These requirements address defects that would otherwise
be hidden by a superficially uniform API. Completing the wider software
survey, commercial comparison and bank qualification requires additional
primary sources and trials; this selected review supplies evidence and
testable integration choices for that work.

chapters.title: Reporting causal results and monitoring their continued applicability

segments.text:
\chapter{Reporting causal results and monitoring their continued applicability}
\label{exec16:reporting}

A servicing manager needs to know whether a contact policy improves thirty-day
net recovery, which accounts the conclusion concerns, and what could make it
inapplicable next month. A fluent explanation is useful only if it preserves the
answer supplied by the scientific analysis. A point estimate must not emerge
from a set of unresolved possibilities; a failed retrieval must not become
evidence that an assumption is false; and a successful replay must not certify
that a customer's information was available at the historical decision time.
The report brings together the economic question, the identification
argument, the estimate and the evidence needed to reproduce it. Monitoring asks which parts of that argument still apply after the
context changes.

\section{A banking report starts with a target and an information clock}

Let \(P\) be the eligible account population at the first servicing decision,
\(\pi\) a frozen contact policy, and \(\pi_0\) its comparator. Write
\(Y_{30}^{\pi}\) for thirty-day cash receipts and \(C^\pi\) for the associated
contact costs, both measured in USD per eligible account. The proposed target is
\[
 \theta(P,\pi,\pi_0)
   =\mathbb E_P[Y_{30}^{\pi}-Y_{30}^{\pi_0}]
     -\mathbb E_P[C^\pi-C^{\pi_0}].
\]
The report must bind the eligibility rule, treatment versions, outcome horizon,
currency and censoring convention. A later change of price can change the second
term without changing the already computed cash-receipt contrast. A change of
assignment or historical feature availability can instead undermine the
interpretation of that contrast itself.

At every action time, the available history contains only values whose
availability precedes the decision. Event time, availability time and reporting
time answer different questions. A recovered timestamp for a transaction does
not prove that the decision system could see it then. Consistency, an
appropriate sequential assignment assumption, policy support, and the declared
observation and dependence laws remain premises of the longitudinal analysis.
The language layer may explain those premises, organize their evidence and flag
contradictions. It cannot make them true by restating them. The policy
identification route in Chapter~\ref{ch:la04-workflow} supplies the baseline;
the present chapter carries its meaning into a decision report.

Consider a stipulated finite result object whose possible gross gains are
\(\{0,100\}\) USD per account and whose incremental cost is \(40\) USD.
Subtracting that cost gives the net set \(\{-40,60\}\). Neither a probability
distribution over the two cases nor a sampling confidence level has been
supplied. The midpoint is \(10\), which is not even a member of this set.
Reporting an expected gain of \(10\), or a \(95\%\) chance of benefit, introduces
information that the result object does not contain. The convex hull
\([-40,60]\) can be displayed as an explicitly labelled outer envelope, but it
also contains values absent from the original object. Under a stipulated
worst-case criterion relative to doing nothing, the minimum gain is negative;
under a probability-weighted criterion, further weights are needed. A useful
report explains this decision ambiguity and the information that would resolve
it. The exact calculation is a project reference, not a bank estimate.
\citep{exec16_report_oracle}

\section{Evidence-grounded auditing: useful questions and unfavorable answers}

ARGUS studies whether reported evidence supports identification assumptions in
climate-policy evaluations. Its construct is reported-evidence adequacy, not
causal validity. An auditor can locate an assignment description or an overlap
diagnostic without certifying the actual assignment mechanism or the unobserved
outcomes. In its eleven injected-flaw cases, the paper reports detection rates
of \(.182\) for a keyword method, \(.727\) for a two-stage pipeline, \(.818\)
for a single-pass variant and \(1.000\) for a per-dimension variant, with zero
synthetic false alarms in those headline rows. These are small, constructed
cases. Changes in evidence access and pipeline structure prevent attributing
the entire difference to one judging component.
\citep{v12_la_2609_30867}

The same paper's reconciled five-paper pilot is less reassuring. Of \(55\)
assumption cells, the human labels comprise seven low, forty-six medium and two
high cases. ARGUS abstains on \(22\); among the \(33\) answered cells, \(25\)
judgments are too severe. Both annotators find relevant reported evidence in
\(19\) of the \(22\) abstained cells, and at least one finds it in \(21\).
An abstention is consequently not interchangeable with a substantive high-risk
finding. A rule using retrieval quality and evidence status increases agreement
on answered cells from \(8/33\) to \(25/33\) in the same pilot. Always predicting
medium gives \(26/33\) on that selected subset. Weighted kappa increases from
\(.08\) to \(.23\), with an interval including zero. The alternative abstention
rule reduces answered coverage from \(33/55\) to \(13/55\). The improvement is
in-sample and does not qualify future bank monitoring.

These findings imply a practical remedy. A report should distinguish evidence
found and supportive, evidence found and adverse, inadequate retrieval,
conflicting evidence, and an assumption requiring external facts. Each judgment
needs the inspected passage, its source version, the claim being assessed and
the reason for the disposition. Missing retrieval should trigger a bounded
retrieval or human-review route. It should not increase a scientific risk score
by an undocumented convention. Calibration requires held-out examples, a
declared labeling protocol and a reported coverage--error tradeoff.

The observational causal inference workflow of Chou and colleagues offers a
different form of assistance: a human principal, actor and critic coordinate
analysis notebooks, diagnostics and versioned reports. The authors report
\(192\) satisfactory and \(39\) unsatisfactory critic judgments across \(231\)
ACIC datasets. Their smaller scaffolding comparison is favorable, but a
disguised LaLonde evaluation using twenty bootstrap replications has median
absolute percentage errors of \(52\%\) for PSID and \(19\%\) for CPS; the critic
declines the PSID result in all but one replication. These results motivate
both assistance and refusal. They do not make a critic's acceptance a new
confidence guarantee. Moreover, the inspected notebook's uniform average after
propensity trimming targets the retained population; calling it ATO does not
make it the conventional overlap-weighted estimand. A report must bind the
actual population and weighting, even when a package's label is familiar.
\citep{v12_la_2607_22443,v12_la_package_oci_agent}

For discovery, \emph{Causal Discovery in the Era of Agents} separates agent
suggestions, user decisions, algorithm settings and graph output. Its proposed
benchmarks for method selection, diagnosis and interpretation remain an
evaluation agenda. A reporting assistant should preserve CPDAG or PAG ambiguity
and the restrictions under which an effect query is answered. The medical
causal-copilot paper likewise proposes assistance with target specification and
study design while acknowledging contamination and inadequate study-design
benchmarks. Its discussion of missed or false post-market signals motivates
evaluation; it does not supply a validated alarm procedure. These are
substantive design contributions with different evidential status from
completed causal-effect studies.
\citep{v12_la_2606_23608,v12_la_2407_19118}

\section{What adjacent monitoring and repair literature contributes}

CausalPulse coordinates manufacturing diagnostics through agents, domain rules
and tools, including an MCP utility layer. Its inspected evaluation distinguishes
workflow completion from root-cause attribution: PSE planning and tool-use
success are reported at \(98.75\%\), while root-cause Hits@1 is \(.44\) and
F1 is \(.39\). The local hardware and workflow timings are author-reported
manufacturing evidence. A bank report should borrow the separation of stages
and their denominators. Reusing a cached graph also requires its contextual
applicability to be checked; cache availability alone does not settle that
question.
\citep{exec13_pulse}

FlowFixer makes workflow repair more concrete. It converts execution traces to
symbolic descriptions, infers behavioral assertions, attributes failures,
proposes edits and verifies candidates. The evaluated collection combines
\(307\) AgentFail logs with \(136\) n8n failure cases. The reported repair
success is \(71.3\%\), compared with \(59.4\%\) for ReCreat, an absolute
difference of \(11.9\) percentage points. Failure-attribution accuracy is
\(84.4\%\); the reported \(87.9\%\) root-cause accuracy is conditional on
correct failure attribution. These percentages do not share a denominator.
Repairs are repeated three times per case and assessed through dynamic
verification on the original inputs. Passing those inputs does not establish
generalization to an unseen incident or preservation of a causal estimand.
\citep{exec16_report_flowfixer}

The proposed reuse is methodological: make dependencies explicit, separate
symptoms from an attributed cause, and check an edit against an executable
contract. An inferred assertion that an itinerary respects a budget is not
the same kind of statement as sequential exchangeability. FlowFixer's
pre-execution filter reports \(99.7\%\) precision and \(84.6\%\) recall for
invalid workflows; some model and tool failures still appear only at execution.
For a causal report, a repair should preserve the frozen target, inputs and
uncertainty type, then be tested on separate adverse cases. Changing the target
or deleting failures to obtain a successful narrative is a scientific change
requiring a new analysis. The paper justifies studying this mechanism; its
distribution, dependency rights and actual integration remain to be reviewed.

PSEBench supplies an adjacent benchmark construction. Human-reviewed clause
cards factor policy conditions, facts, evidence anchors and constraints, then
generate complete, missing-information and uncertain cases. The cutoff-compatible
second version contains \(3{,}455\), \(1{,}362\) and \(257\) cases in these
groups. The authors compare fifteen models and report separate verdict,
evidence-citation, missing-information and uncertainty metrics. For example,
the paper reports \(90.2\%\) verdict accuracy and \(12.8\%\)
uncertainty-detection F1 for its GPT-5 configuration. This is a reported
configuration result, not a current model recommendation or our replication.
Its meaning is that classification success can coexist with a large weakness
in identifying cases that should remain unresolved.
\citep{exec16_report_psebench}

The benchmark reports expert review of ninety generated cases: agreement on
\(28/30\) complete verdicts, \(29/30\) missing-case indeterminacies and
\(30/30\) uncertain-case ambiguities. That supports a bounded quality check,
not universal correctness of generated labels. The narratives are synthetic,
the Ask tool idealizes retrieval, and the rules are tied to Minnesota's
framework. For banking, the transferable idea is to author explicit
result-and-evidence cards with separately known failure dispositions.
Medical reportability labels should not be imported as causal truth.
Generated cases can test faithful reporting now, while realistic retrieval
failures and different institutional meanings need distinct later evidence.

The NetOps/AIOps survey adds an operational perspective. Its inspected preprint
distinguishes freshness and provenance of logs, metrics, traces and change
records, and separates static questions, trace replay, sandbox execution, live
testbeds and canary evidence. It recommends scoring tool costs, abstention,
latency, drift and trace quality separately, with LLM judging as an auxiliary
signal. These are helpful contract categories. Proposed service invariants
written using probabilities do not themselves provide calibrated probability
models. The retrieved June preprint is not assumed identical to the journal
edition identified in the original search metadata.
\citep{exec16_report_netops}

An economic illustration supplies a caution closer to the application domain.
Kim presents ChatGPT-generated growth and stock-market diagrams and explicitly
says that the backdoor response needs confirmation and that the generated
figures should not all be believed correct. The paper can motivate checking the
distinction between a prediction and an intervention query. It cannot support
a claim of verified economic forecasts or calibrated causal alarms. This
negative interpretation is more informative than counting every paper with
causal terminology as affirmative evidence.
\citep{exec16_report_kimeconomy}

\section{The report object and the actual implementation gap}

The proposed report has three linked layers. Its scientific layer binds the
target, population, clocks, graph or graph class, assumptions and exact result
type. Its evidence layer binds the source data, code, environment, diagnostics,
source passages and review dispositions. Its decision layer states the monetary
conversion, loss criterion, alternatives and unresolved obligations. A sentence
asserting a number must point to a specific field or a separately checked
derivation. A sentence asserting a premise must identify whether it is
stipulated, supported, contradicted or unknown. These links distinguish faithful
transcription from scientific endorsement.
\citep{exec16_report_contract}

The current local report implementation provides a narrower foundation. It
accepts one to one hundred distinct authorized canonical-response artifacts,
checks their schema, binds input hashes and execution identity, and verifies a
completed checkpoint prefix before resumption. Its summaries retain declared
status, disposition, context hash, qualification and source reference. The
verification flag explicitly says that the check is schema-only and is neither
causal nor external review. The inspected worker does not yet copy the full
numerical result into a developed causal narrative or implement an
assumption-monitoring service. The agent workflow also preserves unresolved
obligations and denies authorization for a bank action.
\citep{exec16_report_sources,exec14_custody_implementation,exec14_failure_implementation}

OCI's pinned notebook runner checks interpreter identity and serializes
per-estimand estimates, intervals and diagnostics. It also accepts a selected
notebook and uses an unbounded notebook timeout. Its artifact concepts can
inform the proposed report boundary, but execution requires separate resource
and authority limits. The inspected CausalAgent output parser extracts text
between the first and last braces and returns an empty dictionary on a JSON
decoding error. A consumer must preserve that condition as a typed parse
failure; an empty object must not silently become successful analysis.
These are static source observations, with no new upstream execution.
\citep{v12_la_package_oci_agent,v12_la_package_causalagent,exec16_report_sources}

The proposed CLI and MCP operations should use the same scientific object as
the library. A report request selects immutable result references, an audience,
a template revision and a bounded presentation budget. It does not supply a
replacement estimate. The response includes generated prose, checked claim
links, unresolved statements and a reference to deterministic rendering.
A change-review request supplies a versioned event and returns affected
dependencies, reasons and proposed follow-up work. It does not mutate old
results. Both operations distinguish unsupported input, retrieval failure,
invalid result structure, unresolved science and completed presentation.
The new fields and monitor remain a proposed extension; the existing
schema-only report is not retroactively described as implementing them.

\section{Denominators and uncertainty after a critic selects reports}

Suppose a generated evaluation contains one hundred requests. Sixty produce
computed answers, of which forty-eight are correct; twenty are ambiguous,
ten are unsupported and ten fail retrieval. Conditional computed-answer
accuracy is \(48/60=.80\), whereas correct computed output per submitted
request is \(48/100=.48\). Neither fraction determines whether the ambiguous
or unsupported dispositions were appropriate. Those require independent
case-level labels, and correct refusals can be useful outcomes. A report
should show the full partition, the scientific status within each group and
the corresponding cost. Dropping an expensive failure changes both the quality
and economic comparison.
\citep{exec16_report_oracle}

Selection also changes uncertainty. Let \(C\) be the event that an estimated
interval covers the true effect and \(A\) the event that a critic accepts the
report. Then
\[
 \Pr(C\mid A)=\frac{\Pr(C\cap A)}{\Pr(A)}.
\]
Marginal coverage \(\Pr(C)=.95\) supplies no equality between this conditional
probability and \(.95\). In an exact constructed law with one hundred
equiprobable cases, ninety-five intervals cover. Let acceptance select five
covering and five noncovering cases. Acceptance is \(10\%\) and coverage among
accepted cases is \(5/10=.50\). The example does not assert that a particular
critic behaves this way. It disproves an unjustified inference.

A possible remedy is to qualify the complete selection-and-estimation rule,
including every refusal, under a declared joint experiment. Another is to
design an appropriate conditional inference procedure and establish its
assumptions. An independent acceptance event would preserve marginal
coverage, but the required independence often fails when a critic reads the
same data, intervals and diagnostics. Adding a second agent, or training the
critic elsewhere, does not establish independence of the acceptance event in
the current analysis.

\section{Monitoring requires a statistical design and an owner}

A service can monitor whether an artifact hash changed, whether a response
arrived, whether a measured distribution shifted, or whether a causal claim
remains applicable. These are different events. The first two admit direct
engineering checks. Distributional change can sometimes be tested under a
specified sampling law. Continued causal applicability depends also on
assignment, measurement, support and target population. The catalog example's
observationally equivalent worlds demonstrate why an unchanged observed
distribution need not settle an intervention contrast. Repeated queries to the
same observations cannot remove that ambiguity.
\citep{exec16_dh_exact}

Even a valid individual test needs a repeated-use design. For twelve independent
tests under their nulls, each with false-alarm probability \(.05\),
\[
 \Pr(\text{at least one false alarm})=1-.95^{12}
       \simeq .459640.
\]
Independence is required for this exact product formula. A simple alternative
allocates the total budget through
\[
 \alpha_t=\frac{.05}{t(t+1)},\qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}\alpha_t=.05\frac{T}{T+1}<.05.
\]
If each test has a valid null rejection probability bounded by its allocated
\(\alpha_t\), a union bound controls the probability of any false rejection;
independence is unnecessary for that bound. For adaptive choice of a test or
population, validity must survive that choice, for example through an
appropriate conditional guarantee. Four equally budgeted monitor families
would each receive \(.0125\), rather than independently spending the full
\(.05\). The allocation, tested family, restart policy and observation clock
must be explicit. An LLM's severity label is not a p-value.
\citep{exec16_report_oracle}

This spending construction is a transparent reference, not a recommended
high-power monitor for every dependent banking series. Late thresholds can
be stringent, repeated looks can reuse dependent observations, and weak support
can make effects uninformative before any test rejects. A proposed monitor
must state its null, unit, dependence assumptions, delay, false-alarm criterion,
detectable changes and response policy. A scientific owner decides whether the
signal warrants a new design or narrower claim; the data owner explains
availability and assignment changes; the operator owns delivery and recovery.
The agent may summarize signals and prepare the review. No bank-action
authority follows from its text.

\section{Version changes should invalidate the affected argument}

Let a dependency graph connect clocks and assignment to a design, the design
and cohort to an estimate, the estimate and prices to economics, and the
estimate and economics to the report. This graph describes provenance and
applicability, not causal relationships between customers. A change in price
reopens economics and the report while preserving the stored statistical
estimate. A change in the availability clock reopens the design, estimate,
economics and report. A change to an unrelated cohort reopens its own estimate
without invalidating this entire analysis. The exact reachability example
reproduces all three behaviors.
\citep{exec16_report_oracle}

Reachability identifies review obligations, not a verdict that every descendant
is wrong. A source correction may be editorial; an assignment correction may
be decisive. Each change carries its effective time, observation time, affected
field, old and new identity, evidence and responsible reviewer. Historical
artifacts stay immutable. A separate applicability state records current,
review-required, superseded, or unknown, with a reason. Revalidation creates a
new linked decision. This prevents an old report from being silently rewritten
while also preventing a stable byte hash from being mistaken for current
scientific validity.

\section{A public and generated prototype can settle the next engineering questions}

The immediate comparison can use frozen public source passages and authored
result cards. Begin with a deterministic renderer that carries all numbers,
units, result types and dispositions exactly. Add a constrained language
renderer that may explain those facts, and then an optional retrieval assistant.
The prototype case families should include the finite set and selection
examples above; a conflicting citation; an absent passage; a late feature;
a revised price; an unchanged observed law with unresolved causal meaning;
malformed output; a stale dependency; and an appropriate refusal. Withholding
a necessary fact differs from stipulating that two possibilities remain
observationally indistinguishable.
\citep{exec16_report_contract}

Before any optional live-model experiment, freeze the generator, truth fields,
source snapshots, split unit, budgets, prompts, model revision and evaluation
rules. Keep related variants on the same side of a split so that near-duplicate
cards do not masquerade as new evidence. Verify quantitative and structural
statements deterministically. Independently review scientific meaning and
explanation quality, with an adjudication rule for disagreement. Report coverage,
wrong numbers or units, lost ambiguity, unsupported claims, correct and incorrect
refusals, provenance defects, delay and full cost. Generation, retrieval, human
review, retries, storage and maintenance belong in that cost. A readability gain
is useful only alongside an explicitly acceptable semantic error profile.

The exact authored cases have been executed; this comparative model experiment
has not. A first finite conformance gate requires every declared number, unit,
result type and mandatory limitation to survive the selected reference cases.
Passing establishes those cases only. Generalization and alarm calibration
require fresh evaluations under their declared laws. Rights and complete
dependency review precede adoption of adjacent packages. A manual report
remains an alternative when automation saves too little review effort.

The bounded survey leaves three candidate areas outside its inspected evidence:
a broad safety review, marketing context graphs, and traceable agents in
bioinformatics. Their technical claims require original-text and version review.
The proposed public and generated comparison can nevertheless proceed. It can
establish faithful handling of declared evidence and known cases; bank assignment
truth, general causal identification, selective calibration and useful
institutional monitoring remain separate questions.
\citep{exec16_report_contract}
\label{exec16:reporting-end}

chapters.title: Evaluating causal assistance without changing the question

segments.text:
\chapter{Evaluating causal assistance without changing the question}
\label{la:evaluation}

The question throughout this chapter is whether assistance preserves a banking decision while improving its resolution at an acceptable cost. The opening defines the comparison; the coverage screen and prospective experiment then show what a finite evaluation could establish. The source studies test the reference answers, exposure history, adjudication and scoring rules on which that experiment would rely. Finally, the evaluator, memory and toolkit comparisons follow those requirements into a working interface. Their different failure mechanisms cannot be reduced to a single accuracy score.

\section{The benchmark unit is a causal problem}

An agent can produce a plausible report, execute valid code and still answer
the wrong causal question. Evaluation must follow the entire chain from
business meaning through assumptions and identification to uncertainty,
availability and decision loss. A benchmark of text fluency, graph edit
distance or successful tool calls measures only part of that chain.

CLadder demonstrates the value of formal questions with varied verbalizations,
including commonsense and deliberately unfamiliar or conflicting stories.
The inspected paper also identifies language-to-formal-tool formulation as
a continuing challenge. Its historical binary-answer accuracy is evidence
about those tasks and models; it is not a measurement of effect coverage,
decision loss or banking readiness. \cite{v12_la_2312_04350}

CausalDS expands the evaluation object to narrated synthetic mechanisms,
data and a separate observation model. Its inspected results show why
symbolic success, uncertainty quality, abstention and cost should be reported
separately. Its author-reported exam and repeated runs are useful design
evidence, not model evaluations conducted in this project. A generated world
with known truth also remains different from authentic bank data whose
semantic and assignment mechanisms must be established externally.
\cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

The proposed experimental unit is therefore an independently generated or
independently adjudicated causal mechanism and question. Several phrasings,
label conditions or stochastic model calls can be nested within that unit.
They do not create new independent worlds. Repeating one problem fifty times
can measure response variation for that problem; it does not provide fifty
independent demonstrations of general causal competence.

\section{Matched information and meaningful alternatives}

The prospective design compares a fixed numerical workflow, a language-only
workflow, retrieval assistance, a hybrid of numerical tools and typed model
proposals, and structured expert workflows with and without assistance.
Each arm needs a declared information budget. If one receives the true
causal graph and another must discover it, their effect-estimation scores
do not isolate the value of language assistance. If retrieval adds a valid
institutional fact, that information gain should be distinguished from a
better inference algorithm.

Eight strata are proposed: independent sufficient DAGs; latent-variable
graph classes; temporal data with known clocks; treatment-confounder
feedback; panel or quasi-experimental assignment; proxies, linkage and
selection; weak or nonidentifying effects; and ambiguous business targets
or monetary loss. Label and evidence conditions cross ordinary descriptions,
unfamiliar labels, misleading or irrelevant material, and conflict between
numerical evidence and text. These strata test different failure mechanisms
rather than treating all causal questions as interchangeable.

The current planning allocation is 400 mechanisms, with 50 per stratum and
three stochastic repetitions nested within each mechanism. This is an
allocation for developing the design, not a frozen final sample size or a
power calculation. For orientation, the worst-case normal approximation for
one Bernoulli proportion at 400 independent observations has half-width
\(1.96\sqrt{0.25/400}\), approximately 0.049. Paired differences, stratified
outcomes and rare severe errors require their own precision design. A
development pilot would inform that design and must be excluded from the
final test. The six task families developed in Section~\ref{exec13:live-design} describe workflow functions, whereas the eight strata here describe scientific conditions; they are different design dimensions. That later section uses additional sample sizes to illustrate error control, power and cost. Those calculations refine the choice of a trial rather than combine into an approved allocation.

Both natural-workflow and matched-budget comparisons can be useful. The
first asks what an analyst can achieve with a realistic workflow, including
review. The second asks what changes when information or computation is
controlled. Neither should hide extra expert time, repeated retrieval or
retry costs. The comparison must state which question it answers.

\section{A target error can survive perfect arithmetic}

An exact project IV construction illustrates a benchmark-label hazard.
Let a randomized binary instrument \(Z\) affect treatment for half the
population, the compliers; the other half never receives treatment. Set
\(Y(0)=0\) for everyone, \(Y(1)=1\) for compliers and \(Y(1)=3\) for
never-takers. Treatment equals \(Z\) for compliers and zero otherwise.
Randomization, exclusion and monotonicity hold in this construction.

The observed outcome difference across instrument values is \(0.5\) and
the treatment-probability difference is \(0.5\), so the Wald ratio is one.
The population ATE is two. Changing the never-takers' unobserved treated
outcome changes the population ATE without changing the observed law. A
scorer that calls the unrestricted Wald ratio the population ATE would
reward a target substitution. This is a finite counterexample supporting
review of generator assumptions, not a claim that every IV question in a
named benchmark uses this construction.

The same concern applies to trimming, overlap weighting and selected
populations. A language answer can reproduce the right formula for a
different target. Evaluation should therefore compare the population,
measure, action, comparator, horizon and units before comparing the numeric
answer. Critical semantic errors deserve their own count, even when a
numeric discrepancy happens to be small in the test mechanism.

\section{Graphs, sets and refusals need separate scores}

Graph evaluation should compare adjacency and endpoint statements against
the appropriate identifiable class. A justified circle or undirected edge
should not be penalized merely because a simulator internally selected one
fully directed graph. Orientation informativeness can be reported alongside
validity. This makes a method that preserves genuine ambiguity distinguishable
from one that returns little information and from one that confidently
overorients the graph.

Identification outcomes also need separate labels. Scientific
nonidentification, unsupported implementation, malformed output, explicit
abstention, timeout and missing input are not the same event. A well-designed
agent can correctly identify a missing premise without successfully computing
an effect. A backend can be unable to implement a valid functional. Combining
these into one ``incorrect'' or ``no answer'' category would obscure the
remedy.

For identified scalar targets, bias and error can be meaningful. For reported
sets, evaluate coverage, topology, finite availability and size. Whole-line
answers can have high coverage and little decision value. A method that
returns short intervals on a selected easy subset needs an all-request
availability denominator. Unbounded and disconnected sets must remain in the
evaluation rather than being replaced by finite plotting limits.

For an eligible finite interval \([l,u]\), one prospective score at nominal
level \(1-\alpha\) is
\[
 (u-l)+\frac{2}{\alpha}(l-\theta)1\{\theta<l\}
       +\frac{2}{\alpha}(\theta-u)1\{\theta>u\}.
\]
The formula balances length with penalties for missing the target. It is
not an instruction to compress a union of intervals into one interval. For
unions, coverage and total Lebesgue length can be reported while retaining
infinite lengths. Raw losses should not be capped simply to make a plot or
ranking convenient. The eligible target type must be stated before the
score is selected.

\section{Contamination, adaptation and selective reporting}

An exposed demonstration cannot become a held-out evaluation merely because
its variables are renamed. The local problem fixtures and replay examples
have already been used to develop and debug the prototype. They can continue
to test conformance, but they cannot provide independent estimates of a
language model's causal accuracy.

The final design needs a frozen development/test split, mechanism identities,
prompts, model/provider revisions, retrieval corpus and ranking rules, numerical
baselines, stopping rules and analysis code. Mechanism families should be
separated where family reuse would reveal the answer. Label novelty and
mechanism novelty should be varied independently. An unfamiliar name attached
to a memorized mechanism is not the same test as an unfamiliar mechanism.

Test outcomes cannot be used to tune prompt templates, choose the best
retriever, strengthen selected priors or discard difficult cells while
retaining a final-test interpretation. A changed method requires a new
reviewed evaluation revision. Failed and unavailable requests remain in the
record. Reporting only the critic-approved subset would confound answer
quality with selection by the critic.

The inspected OCI paper provides a useful refusal example: its critic
declines many replications when overlap is poor. That can be preferable
to an unsupported estimate, but it makes the denominator essential.
The reported successful answers, refused requests, review effort and
remaining target population must all be visible. The external results
are author reports, not a validation of this project's critic.
\cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

\section{Decision value and cost}

The ultimate question is whether assistance improves feasible decisions at
an acceptable total cost. In a known synthetic mechanism, a policy's expected
loss can be calculated under the mechanism and compared with the chosen
baseline. In a bank, the feasible policy, valuation model, risk limits,
operating costs and outcome truth need authentic inputs. Synthetic decision
loss does not establish institutional return on investment.

The prospective cost record includes model calls, input/output/cache tokens,
retrieval, numerical CPU time, wall time, memory, retries and human review
and rework. Actual dated prices are needed to turn these quantities into a
currency total. Unknown prices remain missing; zero live calls in an offline
prototype do not imply a free live workflow. A fast answer that requires
substantial correction can have a worse total cost than a slower transparent
analysis.

No final live-model experiment is reported by this chapter. Five prerequisite
classes remain: an exact live backend and custody terms; actual prices and
a bounded budget; independent held-out mechanisms and original benchmark
bytes; named business/diagram adjudicators and a rubric; and qualified
numerical baselines. These are missing program inputs. No credentials were
read and no provider endpoint was probed to infer that a service is unavailable.
The design provides a route to evaluation once those inputs are supplied;
it provides no current empirical model-performance claim. The remaining studies turn these requirements into inspectable tests: first the probability of passing a coverage rule, then a prospective comparison, and finally the reliability of its references, evaluators and numerical handoffs.

\section{The probability of passing a coverage screen}
\label{v13:la-screen}

Evaluating an agent that recommends inferential procedures requires a clear
distinction between nominal coverage, an argument for coverage and an empirical
qualification rule. Suppose a fixed procedure is tested in $n$ independently
generated replications of a declared mechanism. Let $K$ count requests whose
reported sets cover the truth; unavailable or failed requests remain in the
declared denominator. If the per-request coverage is $p$, then under these
simulation assumptions $K$ has a binomial law.

For a simultaneous family of $m$ cells and total error budget $\alpha$, consider
the one-sided exact lower bound
\[
 L(K,n)=\operatorname{BetaQuantile}
       (\alpha/m;K,n-K+1),\qquad K>0,
\]
with $L(0,n)=0$. A rule requiring $L\geq0.95$ certifies a minimum in this
specific finite experiment. At true $p=0.95$, its probability of passing one
cell is at most $\alpha/m$. This is how a lower-bound certification test behaves
at its boundary, not evidence that the procedure's true coverage is zero.

Before qualification, a designer can compute the smallest integer $k_*$ that
passes and the operating characteristic
\[
 \Pr_p(\hbox{pass})=\Pr_p(K\geq k_*).
\]
The project calculation evaluates this exactly for several replication counts,
family sizes and values of $p$, and independently checks the equivalent
binomial-tail threshold. It draws no random data and does not test a causal
estimator. Its purpose is to make the qualification design interpretable.
\cite{v13_project_exact}

Increasing replications can distinguish a genuine coverage margin above 95\%
more sharply. It cannot make a level-controlled test have high power at the
exact boundary. This does not justify lowering the required minimum after
seeing results. The analyst must state what guarantee is theoretically justified,
what empirical screen is being applied and what its power is. A method may
have a plausible asymptotic argument while failing this finite screen; that
should be reported as a qualification shortfall rather than silently recoded
as success.

An agent could otherwise exploit this distinction in two bad ways. It might
declare a method invalid merely because a low-powered boundary screen failed,
or widen intervals until they pass while ignoring decision usefulness. The
evaluation should penalize both. Coverage, finite availability and useful width
are separate dimensions. A whole-line interval covers every finite truth but
may support no action. Bank width and loss thresholds require actual decision
owners; synthetic thresholds should remain labeled as such.

\section{A live comparison needs independent mechanisms and complete costs}

An offline controller can demonstrate request validation, abstention, tool
dispatch and preservation of graph/set semantics. It cannot measure how a live
model translates a new banking problem, how often retrieval changes its graph,
or what the workflow costs. Zero model calls means those empirical quantities
are unmeasured; it does not mean accuracy is zero or costs are free.

A credible live comparison binds the exact backend/revision and inference
settings, data-custody arrangement, actual prices and approved budget, independent
held-out mechanisms or benchmark bytes, adjudicators and rubric, and qualified
numerical baselines. The final prompts, retrieval corpus, tools, retry rules,
token/time limits and numerical tolerances should be frozen before the first
final request. Development cases already exposed to the agent cannot become
held-out by receiving different filenames.

Compare data-only, model-only, retrieval-assisted, hybrid and expert-assisted
workflows under matched information and budgets. A hybrid receives additional
information when it uses a valid domain exclusion; its improvement should not
be attributed solely to reasoning. Conversely, a data-only baseline should not
be asked to identify an effect that the observed law cannot identify. The
equal-law counterexamples in Section~\ref{v13:la-equivalence} make this boundary
testable.

Metrics should include whether the translated intervention/population is valid,
whether graph output respects equivalence and latent ambiguity, whether the
downstream effect is scientifically supported, and whether abstention occurs
for the right reason. Repeated-run disagreement is relevant even when the
average score is favorable. Fluent explanations and exact string matches to
one graph are inadequate substitutes for these criteria.

Complete costs include unsuccessful calls, retries, retrieval, tool computation,
human review and operating overhead. If an agent frequently produces a request
that needs manual correction, its low token bill can conceal high workflow cost.
Decision value should be evaluated on feasible actions and held-out outcomes
or an explicitly justified reference, with uncertainty. A stipulated arithmetic
example explains the accounting but cannot establish provider pricing, model
calibration or bank ROI.

\section{Testing semantic failures before the expensive study}

Several low-cost deterministic cases can be exercised before live qualification.
A y0 nonidentification response must not become a zero effect. A continuous
density must not be interpreted as a binary probability. A grouped allocation
contrast must not become an individual direct effect. A statsmodels internal
covariance option must not be reported as final clustered uncertainty when the
inspected implementation supplies HC0. \cite{v13_sw_y0,v13_sw_causalgps,v13_sw_inferference,v13_sw_statsmodels}

These cases test the proposed interface and evaluation rubric. They are useful
development evidence, and their exposure should be recorded. Fresh independent
mechanisms are still necessary to evaluate generalization. Keeping those roles
separate allows an agentic workflow to improve through development while
retaining a meaningful final assessment.

\hypertarget{evaluate-the-claim-behind-the-benchmark-score}{%
\subsection{Evaluate the claim behind the benchmark
score}\label{evaluate-the-claim-behind-the-benchmark-score}}

\label{exec13:census-evaluation}

CausalEval places diverse language tasks in one comparative survey,
including commonsense cause selection, correlation-to-causation
questions, graph-based inference and judgments about described events.
This is useful navigation, but the common label ``causal reasoning''
does not make their outcomes interchangeable. Correctly classifying a
relation mentioned in a sentence, recovering a graph from observations
and identifying a policy value test different information and
