zero stage & 2000/2000 & 0.9525 & [0.9422, 0.9614] \\
false exclusion & 2000/2000 & 0.0000 & [0.0000, 0.0018] \\
observed sufficiency & 2000/2000 & 0.9540 & [0.9439, 0.9628] \\
nonlinear / action variance & 120/120 & 0.9583 & [0.9054, 0.9863] \\
nonlinear / omitted transition & 0/120 & 0.0000 & [0.0000, 0.0303] \\
learner / represented interaction & 300/300 & 0.9033 & [0.8641, 0.9343] \\
learner / omitted quadratic & 300/300 & 0.0000 & [0.0000, 0.0122] \\
larger learner / longer window & 300/300 & 0.9400 & [0.9068, 0.9641] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Selected graph, nonlinear and learner procedures. Coverage is over every requested draw; unqualified fits count as unavailable. Monte Carlo intervals describe simulation uncertainty, not bank validity.}
\label{r8:extension-table}
\end{table}

The first small joint-calendar design covers $553/600=.9217$, while pair-only
and calendar-only challengers cover $.8617$ and $.7017$. A fresh larger joint
design with 960 pairs, 720 dates and a separately registered longer window
covers $564/600=.94$, with Monte Carlo interval $[.9179,.9576]$. Keeping both
information dimensions improves the selected comparison, but the first design's
shortfall remains. Sample sizes and windows change between designs; matched
windows within the larger design assess one contribution without uniquely
explaining every finite-sample error. False inclusion and selected label errors
cover only $.7583$ and $.7983$. More data under a false scientific declaration
can make a wrong answer look precise.

Four pairs of complete fresh-process requests compare dense and chunked fitting
at 12,000 and 120,000 dates. Both include imports, immutable mapped-input
verification, fitting, prediction, inference, persistence and read-back of
public outputs and scores. Synthetic input acquisition is excluded equally.
Maximum score/output differences are below $1.2\times10^{-14}$, and result
identity, folds and inference descriptions agree. At the larger size, chunked
peak-process memory is approximately $.983$--$.985$ of dense memory; process-time
ratios are about $1.009$--$1.027$. These measured obligations do not demonstrate
large total-memory or speed gains. Avoiding one materialized design is a
specific algorithmic property, not proof of enterprise scalability.

\section{Evidence required before institutional use}
\label{r8:external}

Independent scientific review must reconstruct the target, assumptions,
identification, uncertainty and limitations, including negative comparisons.
Authentic bank validation then needs assignment and source-clock owners,
representative independent audit truth, known selection probabilities, a frozen
question and held-out evidence. An unknown-truth bank study cannot simply
reproduce synthetic truth-coverage counts. It needs assignment diagnostics,
placebos, audit sensitivity and financial reconciliation appropriate to its
design, together with a decision-relevant precision requirement.

Application acceptance requires consumer maintainers to preserve qualifications,
unbounded/disconnected sets and refusals under their actual interfaces. Workflow
economics require matched complete analyst tasks and quality, active labor,
rework, audits and infrastructure costs. Multi-host qualification requires the
target platform and declared fault/recovery and service objectives. Local
serialization, mapped-input fitting and restart checks do not supply these
external observations. The investment argument therefore continues with
bounded scientific capabilities and explicit dependencies, rather than an
assumption that completing the author program has completed adoption. The remaining funding question is especially instructive: expanding evaluation dates can leave pilot error and short-lag covariance error intact. The next chapter derives those contributions explicitly and compares the information and computational costs of proposed repairs.

chapters.title: Calibrating funding inference and accounting for its information cost

segments.text:
\chapter{Calibrating funding inference and accounting for its information cost}
\label{v9:chapter}

Increasing a study's size is useful only when its additional information addresses the error that matters. This chapter derives the shift induced by a fixed independent pilot, contrasts it with a joint fixed-regression construction, and identifies the assumptions behind a finite covariance horizon. Fresh comparisons retain the failures of both routes; the final implementation study asks which memory gains apply to which procedure. The cost of new history and audit information therefore enters alongside numerical efficiency.

\section{Why a larger evaluation sample can leave the wrong uncertainty}
\label{v9:target}

A treasury estimate can become more precise around the wrong population
quantity when its controls are learned from a fixed, imperfect pilot. The
funding construction supplies a useful setting in which to distinguish this
problem from audit inversion, covariance estimation and computational scale.
Keep the fixed one-month price intervention, balance-stock response horizon
$H$, financial weights $w_h$ and direct repricing cost $C$ of the earlier
funding example. Its target is
\[
 V=\sum_{h=0}^{H}w_h\beta\rho^h-C.
\]
This is the value of the specified intervention; neither the reporting horizon
nor the intervention is selected to improve its reported interval.

Consider the stationary mechanism
\begin{align}
 W_t&=rW_{t-1}+\sqrt{1-r^2}\,\xi_t,\qquad
 A_t=\tfrac12W_t+\tfrac15(W_t^2-1)+e_t, \label{v9:law}\\
 B_t&=\rho B_{t-1}+\beta A_t+1.2W_t+.4(W_t^2-1)+\nu_t.
\end{align}
Here $|r|,|\rho|<1$, the $\xi_t$ are independent standard Gaussian innovations,
the action innovation $e_t$ has variance one, and it is
independent of the complete driver path, other-date action innovations and
exogenous balance shocks. Future assignment remains natural under the
intervention. A companion portfolio has coefficient $\beta_d$ and shares the
exogenous shocks. Independent origin strata $S_t\in\{0,1\}$ and complete-horizon
swaps create the two candidate outcome vectors, with correct-map probability
$p_s$ in stratum $s$. Independent representative binomial audits estimate
$p_s$. This is an origin-swap experiment; it does not inherit the persistent
customer-map sampling law merely because both examples involve identity.

For the bank, the assumptions concern assignment and observation, not just
regression fit. A source owner must substantiate noninformative swaps, an
assignment owner must justify the innovation restriction, and an audit owner
must document representative independent labels. Good predictive accuracy
does not establish those statements.

\section{An exact account of independent-pilot error}
\label{v9:pilot}

Use the fixed dictionary $x_t=(1,W_t,W_t^2-1)'$, whose stationary second-moment
matrix is $Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,2)$. Let
$c_1=.5\beta+1.2$ and $c_2=.2\beta+.4$. The stationary conditional mean of
$B_t$ has coefficients
\[
 a_0=\frac{c_1}{1-\rho r},\qquad
 b_0=\frac{c_2}{1-\rho r^2},
\]
on $W_t$ and $W_t^2-1$. The geometric sums include balances accumulated before
the origin. Natural future assignment gives, for $h\geq1$,
\[
 a_h=\rho a_{h-1}+c_1r^h,\qquad
 b_h=\rho b_{h-1}+c_2r^{2h}.
\]
Mix these focal and companion means by $p_s$ to obtain each candidate's
conditional outcome mean. The action-mean coefficients are $(0,.5,.2)'$.
An independent infinite-past sum reproduces the recursions to numerical
precision. A literal 48-branch recursion also matches the aggregate simulator:
averaging independent Gaussian branch noise replaces its standard deviation
by $\sigma_{\rm branch}/\sqrt{48}$ while preserving the common shocks.
Stationary formulas describe the population; a finite burn approximates that law.

Condition on an independent pilot of size $M$. For one stratum and one
candidate horizon, write $\delta_a$ and $\delta_y$ for the pilot's action and
outcome coefficient errors. Let $\eta$ denote the desired candidate response.
Because $E[e_tx_t]=0$ and $E[e_t^2]=1$, the population residual-regression ratio
conditional on that pilot is
\begin{equation}
 \eta_M=\frac{\eta+\delta_a'Q\delta_y}
                    {1+\delta_a'Q\delta_a},\qquad
 \eta_M-\eta=
 \frac{\delta_a'Q(\delta_y-\eta\delta_a)}
      {1+\delta_a'Q\delta_a}. \label{v9:pilot-bias}
\end{equation}
Direct Gaussian quadrature of the residual products independently verifies
this identity. It is a population ratio conditional on the pilot, not an
assertion about the expectation of a finite-sample ratio or inverse audit map.
Correct action means remove this shift even when the outcome mean is
imperfect. Knowing only the outcome mean leaves the action-error square.

The orthogonal partialling-out score and its nuisance-product requirement are
inherited ideas \citep[Section 4.1, equation (4.4), Assumption 4.1]{dml2018};
equation~\eqref{v9:pilot-bias} is the present model's explicit calculation.
The cited iid theorem is not a dependent-calendar theorem. Under a fixed
dictionary, nonsingular moments, stable mixing and sufficiently high moments,
the pilot errors have order $M^{-1/2}$ with bounded ridge penalties. The target
remainder therefore has order $M^{-1}$. Root-$T$ inference for the desired
response requires
\[
 \frac{\sqrt T}{M}\longrightarrow0.
\]
A fixed pilot does not satisfy that requirement. For a growing Bartlett
window $L$, uniform score moment bounds give the additional sufficient control
$L/\sqrt M\to0$ for fitted-score covariance. These are sufficient rates for
the specified construction, not necessary rates for every learner.

The diagnostic experiment holds evaluation draws and audits fixed within each
$T$, uses nested prefixes of an independent pilot, and replaces action and
outcome means separately by their known values. At $T=4800$, the average
conditional shift decreases from about 42,452 currency units with $M=400$ to
9,049 with $M=1600$ and 616 with $M=19200$. Known action means remove that
conditional shift; finite-ratio and covariance errors remain.
Table~\ref{v9:diagnostic-table} separates the shift from empirical bias and
compares estimated standard errors with empirical dispersion. Known nuisance
and audit information diagnose this synthetic law; the bank cannot obtain
them by labeling an estimate an oracle.

\section{Joint fixed regression and the score's covariance horizon}
\label{v9:covariance}

A distinct practical procedure estimates the prespecified fixed regression
jointly on the evaluation sample. Within each stratum regress both candidate
outcome vectors on $(x_t',A_t)'$. Frisch--Waugh residualization recovers the
same action coefficient by projecting the action on $x_t$ and regressing the
outcomes on its residual. This is a fixed-dimensional joint estimating
equation. Its argument does not authorize selecting an adaptive dictionary
from evaluation outcomes and then treating that dictionary as fixed.

Let $e_t=A_t-x_t'\alpha$, let
$q_s=E[1\{S_t=s\}e_t^2]$, and let $\epsilon_{st}$ be the population joint
regression residual for a candidate horizon. The action-coefficient influence is
\[
 \psi_{st}=\frac{1\{S_t=s\}e_t\epsilon_{st}}{q_s}.
\]
Assume nonsingular regression moments, finite $4+\delta$ moments and stationary
mixing sufficient for a score central limit theorem. The stable Gaussian law
above satisfies these conditions away from persistence one. Estimated
fixed-dimensional regression residuals consistently recover this influence.
Additional predictable outcome structure need not bias the action coefficient
when the action mean and innovation moment remain correct.

There is a stronger property specific to this mechanism. Condition on the
complete exogenous driver path and all shocks strictly before $t$. Averaging
over $e_t$, the independent origin swap and shocks through $t+H$ makes
$\psi_{st}$ mean zero: its action-response component has already been removed
by the population coefficient. Its random action and balance inputs are
measurable through $t+H$. For $u>t+H$, the earlier score is measurable before
$u$, whereas the later score has conditional expectation zero. Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Cov}(\psi_t,\psi_{t+k})=0\quad(k>H),\qquad
 \Omega=\Gamma_0+\sum_{k=1}^{H}(\Gamma_k+\Gamma_k'). \label{v9:horizon}
\end{equation}
The score process need not itself be $H$-dependent. The argument requires
exogenous innovations, the correct action mean and noninformative swaps;
a finite reported horizon alone is insufficient.

For fixed $H$, untapered empirical lag products consistently estimate
\eqref{v9:horizon}; plugging in the consistent joint regression changes each
moment by $o_p(1)$. Bartlett weighting instead attenuates nonzero short-lag
covariances when its window is small. Its positive-semidefinite construction
is an inherited benefit \citep[printed p.4, Theorem 1]{newey1986}. The
untapered estimate has no such finite-sample guarantee. The implementation
qualifies only the prespecified scalar monetary contrast and returns an
unavailable result if its calendar variance is nonpositive. It does not clip
that variance or advertise a generally valid covariance matrix.

The mapping inverse remains a separate source of uncertainty. If
$\eta_{s1h},\eta_{s2h}$ are the candidate responses and each stratum has weight
one half, the monetary derivative with respect to $p_s$ is
\[
 d_s=\frac{1}{2}\sum_h w_h
       \frac{\eta_{s2h}-\eta_{s1h}}{(2p_s-1)^2}.
\]
Add $\sum_s d_s^2p_s(1-p_s)/n_s$ from the independent audits. Regular joint
asymptotics require $p_s$ away from $0,1,.5$ and finite limits for $T/n_s$.
The Wilson rank guard withholds a regular interval when an audit interval
crosses $.5$; empirical audit boundaries also remain unavailable. More dates
do not create strong identity information.

\section{What the fresh comparisons support}
\label{v9:results}

The first fresh comparison uses 600 requests in each of seven laws. Its
joint-regression horizon interval covers 550/600 at 720 dates, with Monte
Carlo interval $[.8916,.9375]$. This is a retained calibration failure.
At 1200 and 4800 dates coverage is .935 and .94; the persistent $\rho=.96$
case gives .9467. Changing the covariance does not remove all finite-regression
error. In the weak-audit law only 127/600 requests yield intervals, of which
121 cover; conditional coverage is about .953, but all-request coverage is
.202. Reporting only the conditional fraction would hide the information
shortfall. Omitting the quadratic action-mean term gives .2633 coverage;
correlating the action innovation with the structural disturbance gives zero.
These are false scientific declarations that a numerical API cannot detect.

The exact pilot calculation suggests another route: retain an independent
pilot but let $M=4T$. This satisfies the selected sufficient rate and avoids
claiming that the small joint-regression failure has been repaired.
A separately frozen fresh study compares the inherited pilot, a fourfold
pilot with Bartlett covariance and a fourfold pilot with horizon covariance.
For the latter, the fitted score converges in mean square to the true-nuisance
score, so each of its fixed-$H$ lag moments converges to the moment in
\eqref{v9:horizon}. The vanishing pilot remainder supplies the required
centering at the desired target. An imperfect pilot held fixed need not have
zero score covariance beyond $H$; the growing-pilot argument is asymptotic.
The last procedure has coverage .9600, .9417 and .9333 across the three
designs in Table~\ref{v9:followup-table}. Each Monte Carlo interval includes
.95, but the largest point estimate remains below nominal. Its mean SE is
64,431 compared with empirical SD 65,867. Relative to the same-draw inherited
baseline, the coverage changes are $4/600$, $0/600$ and $1/600$; descriptive
paired Monte Carlo intervals include zero. Clear superiority is not established.

At 720 dates the old pilot was already fourfold; only covariance differs.
The 1200/4800 designs require three/twelve times the inherited pilot history.
Mean fit-and-inference time for the horizon route is about 1.35/1.57 times the
baseline in those two cases, excluding acquisition. Thus a justified
information rate has a real requirement even where nominal calibration is
statistically compatible. The independent pilot must also represent the same
economic law. A long history drawn from a different assignment regime does not
satisfy that requirement.

\section{Fitting and covariance without retaining all scores}
\label{v9:execution}

The joint-regression route permits a stronger memory construction than merely
reducing the fitting matrix. Form each stratum's block of $[x,A,Y]$, take its QR
factor and combine the small retained triangular factor with the next block.
The final factor supplies the action projection, full regression coefficients
and residual-action sum of squares. A second pass forms the monetary score
directly. It need not materialize the horizon score matrix or retain all $T$
scalar scores.

For lag $k$, store the raw cross-product sum $R_k$, total score $S$, count $T$,
and first and last $H$ scores. If $\bar\psi=S/T$, the centered lag sum is
\[
 R_k-\bar\psi\{2S-S_{{\rm first},k}-S_{{\rm last},k}\}
       +(T-k)\bar\psi^2.
\]
Keeping the final $H$ scores of one block supplies its cross-boundary pairs
with the next. Independent dense SVD and direct centered lag calculations
agree for awkward block sizes, including blocks shorter than $H$. The
working state is bounded by block size, fixed dictionary/outcome width and
$H$; raw input storage and resident mapped pages remain real costs.

Complete fresh-process requests at 120,000 and 1,200,000 dates include imports,
immutable-input checks, fitting, prediction, inference, serialization and
read-back. At the larger size, chunked peak memory is .434--.435 of dense
memory, and elapsed time is .831--.841 of dense time. Maximum relative
output differences are below $6.0\,10^{-15}$. At the smaller size time ratios
straddle one. These measurements concern the joint-regression procedure whose
small-sample calibration failure remains visible. The growing-pilot
implementation still stores its arrays; it does not inherit these memory gains.
Neither procedure has demonstrated bank-platform service levels or analyst
labor savings.

\section{From a qualified request to an institutional decision}
\label{v9:external}

The public request names the procedure, financial target, covariance rule,
audit counts and scientific declarations. Its identity binds evaluation and
pilot bytes as well as those choices. Two local consumer examples preserve
the status, qualifications, monetary units and interval through serialization.
Unavailable results withhold monetary estimates and intervals rather than
becoming a confident zero. Interrupted unfinished fits can be retried from
immutable inputs; no partial-fit checkpoint or distributed recovery is implied.

Independent review must reconstruct the nuisance-bias and filtration arguments
and challenge the retained small-sample failure. Bank validation requires
authentic assignment, source-clock and audit evidence, an independently
invariant pilot when that route is used, and a decision-relevant precision
target. Consumer maintainers must accept the real interface; platform operators
must measure complete workloads under intended storage and faults. Workflow
evaluation must price pilot/audit acquisition, active labor and rework at matched
output quality. These are additional observations, not consequences of an
author having obtained a passing calculation or a useful local memory ratio. The comparison supports a conditional procedure choice rather than a universal repair: growing the independent pilot addresses its selected remainder, joint regression changes how the nuisance is fitted, and streaming changes storage for the procedure actually implemented. The following precision study asks how these choices behave when useful financial width, small audits and complete workflow cost are considered together.

chapters.title: Pilot information, calibration precision and complete streaming inference

segments.text:
\chapter{Pilot information, calibration precision and complete streaming inference}
\label{ch:precision-streaming}

The funding desk's question remains the value of a one-month price intervention
over a fixed balance-response horizon. Chapter~\ref{v9:chapter} shows why a
fixed imperfect pilot can move the target of a residual regression. Increasing
pilot information and reducing working memory address different obstacles.
More independent history can reduce nuisance error, but does not create identity
truth or remove finite-sample covariance error. Streaming makes a specified
calculation feasible with less working storage, but leaves its statistical
assumptions intact. This chapter gives an equivalent streaming construction and
compares fixed procedures with enough repetitions to resolve larger calibration
shortfalls. The banking consequences include the extra history required, the
financial width retained, and the cases in which inference remains unavailable.

\section{Preserving the pilot's learning objective}
\label{v10:pilot}

Let a pilot independent of evaluation supply $M$ dates, the six-column design
$X$ of the preceding chapter and the $K=1+2(H+1)$ targets $Z$: the action
followed by the two candidate response curves. The design contains the intercept, driver,
centered driver square and their stratum interactions. Divide the dates
chronologically into $m_1=\lfloor M/2\rfloor$ training dates and $m_2=M-m_1$
validation dates. For each prespecified penalty $\lambda$ the original pilot
computes
\begin{align}
 B_\lambda&=\arg\min_B\{\|Z_1-X_1B\|_F^2+
                              \lambda\|DB\|_F^2\},\\
 \ell_\lambda&=\frac{1}{m_2K}\sum_{j=1}^K
                 \frac{\|(Z_2-X_2B_\lambda)_{\cdot j}\|^2}{s_j^2},
 \qquad s_j^2=\frac1{m_1}\sum_{t\leq m_1}(Z_{tj}-\bar Z_{1j})^2,
\end{align}
where $D=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,1,1,1,1)$. Only the global intercept is
unpenalized, exactly as in the inherited pilot. The first minimizing penalty
in the supplied list is selected, then refitted using all $M$ pilot dates.
This finite-dictionary construction is a particular nuisance estimator for the
inherited partialling-out score \citep{dml2018}; neither its tuning rule nor
the dependent funding inference is an iid theorem from that source.

For either half, successive QR reductions of $[X_b\;Z_b]$ retain an upper
factor $R_b=[R_{Xb}\;R_{Zb}]$. Orthogonality yields, for every coefficient
matrix $B$,
\begin{equation}
 \|Z_b-X_bB\|_F^2=\|R_{Zb}-R_{Xb}B\|_F^2.
 \label{eq:v10:qr-loss}
\end{equation}
Rows removed in a thin factorization contribute zero because all columns of
$[X_b\;Z_b]$ lie in its retained column space. Stacking a preceding factor
above the next data block and reducing again preserves the same norm identity.
Appending the rows $\sqrt\lambda D$ to $R_{X1}$, with zero target rows,
therefore solves the identical training problem. The validation factor gives
the identical standardized loss without storing all predictions. Stacking the
two factors gives the full-pilot refit. These are exact real-arithmetic
identities, independent of the stochastic dependence within a pilot half.

Training variances are accumulated from centered block moments. If two blocks
have sizes $a,b$, means $u,v$ and centered sums $S_a,S_b$, their combined sum is
\begin{equation}
 S_{a+b}=S_a+S_b+\frac{ab}{a+b}(u-v)^2,
 \qquad \bar Z=\frac{au+bv}{a+b},
\end{equation}
componentwise. This avoids cancellation from subtracting two large raw second
moments. Positive target variances and full design rank in each half are checked.
No holdout outcome from the evaluation sample enters pilot tuning.

Floating-point equivalence additionally requires a stable problem. If each
computed validation loss is within $\epsilon$ of its exact value, a unique
minimum separated by more than $2\epsilon$ has the same selected penalty.
This implication is an algebraic diagnostic, not a global error certificate
for every input. The reference exposes all validation losses and their gap;
identical repeated penalties retain the first occurrence. Near ties, ill
conditioning and arbitrary high-dimensional learners require further numerical
or statistical qualification. In the selected independent dense comparisons,
coefficients, loss ordering, financial results and both covariance choices agree
within the reported numerical tolerance, including chunks of one row and
boundaries shorter than the response horizon.

\section{Streaming evaluation preserves the monetary score}
\label{v10:execution}

After the pilot is fixed, write $v_t=A_t-X_t\widehat B_A$ and
$r_t=Y_t-X_t\widehat B_Y$. A first evaluation pass stores, for each stratum
$s\in\{0,1\}$,
\begin{equation}
 Q_s=\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_t^2,\qquad
 P_s=\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_t r_t,\qquad
 \widehat\eta_s=P_s/Q_s.
\end{equation}
The regular audited inverse supplies the monetary multiplier $c_s$ of the
preceding chapter. A second pass computes the scalar score
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\psi_t=
 \frac{T v_t}{Q_{S_t}}\,(r_t-v_t\widehat\eta_{S_t})^\top c_{S_t}.
\end{equation}
Raw lag products, the global sum, and the first and last $L$ scores recover
globally centered lag covariance across all chunk boundaries. The independent
binomial audit contribution is then added without changing the derivative or
rank guard. Both the horizon rule and Bartlett comparator preserve their
earlier meaning \citep{newey1986}; equivalence of two implementations proves
neither a covariance theorem under another law nor finite-sample calibration.

For block size $b$, design dimension $p$, target dimension $K$ and lag $L$,
working storage is $O(b(p+K)+(p+K)^2+L)$ rather than retaining every pilot
prediction and evaluation score. The input files still occupy $O(M+T)$ rows,
and mapped pages remain part of resident-memory measurements. At fixed
dimension and horizon, the factor size is independent of $M$ and $T$.
Bartlett's growing window gives an additional growing $L$ buffer. The selected
benchmark below uses fixed-horizon covariance; it does not claim constant
total storage or arbitrary-learner streaming.

\section{A more precise comparison of fixed information designs}
\label{v10:precision}

The comparison uses joint regression, a fourfold pilot $M=4T$, and an eightfold
pilot $M=8T$, all with the previously specified horizon covariance. Each
request shares evaluation histories and audit counts; the pilots are nested
prefixes of a separate independent realization. Both growing-pilot sizes
satisfy the sufficient rate of Chapter~\ref{v9:chapter} under its fixed
dictionary and stable-law premises. The number of pilot rows doubles between
the two pilot arms; this information cannot be obtained merely by repartitioning
the same shorter history.

Eight selected designs vary evaluation dates, audit information, persistence
and proximity to singular mapping, and include false exogeneity. The grid is
a structured comparison, not a full factorial or an authentic bank population.
Each design has 2,000 independent requests. Near coverage .95, the approximate
ordinary Monte Carlo half-width is
$1.96\sqrt{.95(.05)/2000}=.00955$; its worst-case value is .02192. Ordinary
Wilson intervals are descriptive. The retained exact binomial inversions use
Bonferroni adjustment across the 24 marginal coverage cells; they give a
simultaneous Monte Carlo bound for those fixed simulation designs, not a
guarantee of causal coverage under another data law. Paired differences use
the observed gain/loss discordances and report their sampling uncertainty.
There is no final-result selection of penalties, covariance, sample size or
favorable design. Unavailable requests remain in all-request coverage; bias,
empirical SD, mean SE and finite width describe the available requests.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
\toprule
Design & $T$ & Audit & Joint & $4T$ & $8T$ & Available\\
\midrule
Original & 720 & 200 & 0.9340 & 0.9400 & 0.9405 & 2000/2000\\
Baseline & 1200 & 1600 & 0.9360 & 0.9470 & 0.9485 & 2000/2000\\
Longer history & 4800 & 1600 & 0.9495 & 0.9520 & 0.9520 & 2000/2000\\
Small audit & 1200 & 200 & 0.9270 & 0.9330 & 0.9340 & 2000/2000\\
Large audit & 1200 & 6400 & 0.9380 & 0.9435 & 0.9420 & 2000/2000\\
Persistent & 1200 & 1600 & 0.9325 & 0.9400 & 0.9395 & 2000/2000\\
Near rank & 1200 & 1600 & 0.2205 & 0.2210 & 0.2210 & 451/2000\\
False exogeneity & 1200 & 1600 & 0.2290 & 0.2055 & 0.2085 & 2000/2000\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{All-request coverage in 2,000 fresh requests per design. Audit is the independent count per stratum. The persistent case has $\rho=.96$; near-rank probabilities are .55 and .515. Pilot arms use nested independent histories; unavailable requests count as noncoverage. These are synthetic selected-law results.}
\label{tab:v10:coverage}
\end{table}
At 720 dates the joint procedure covers .9340 and the pilot procedures
cover .9400 and .9405. The ordinary exact binomial interval for .9400 only
slightly excludes .95; the adjusted interval includes it. With 200 audit
observations per stratum at 1200 dates, coverage is .9270/.9330/.9340. All
three exact simultaneous intervals end below .95 (upper endpoints
.94372/.94900/.94988), so the small-audit shortfall persists after accounting
for all 24 marginal comparisons. The last endpoint is close to .95; its
significance should not be enlarged into a large economic distinction.
Mean SE divided by empirical SD in that design is about .939--.944.

At 4800 dates, coverage is .9495/.9520/.9520, with all ordinary and adjusted
intervals containing .95. This is evidence for this selected design, not a
uniform theorem. The high-persistence case remains .9325/.9400/.9395; the
joint procedure's exact adjusted upper endpoint is .94856. In the near-rank
case only 451 of 2,000 requests return intervals. The pilot arms cover 442
of those available requests, yet all-request coverage is only .2210. The
conditional figure .9800 does not qualify a broadly available operation.
False exogeneity gives coverage .2290/.2055/.2085 despite all requests being
numerically available.

Paired pilot-minus-joint coverage differences at the baseline are .0110 and
.0125. An exact conditional binomial test of equal coverage gives Bonferroni
adjusted two-sided $p$ values .0394 and .00408 across the 24 paired tests.
Thus there is selected-design evidence favoring the pilots over joint
regression. The conservative simultaneous intervals for the difference,
constructed by separate gain/loss bounds, still include zero; these bounds
are looser than the exact conditional test and are not its inversion.
Neither result establishes general superiority. Every conservative interval
for eightfold minus fourfold pilot coverage includes zero. Even at 4800 dates
the two pilot arms have identical covering counts; doubling pilot history
has no demonstrated coverage advantage here.

The initial normal approximation gives a zero-width paired interval when
both discordance counts are zero. That is not population certainty. Exact
binomial inversion for gain and loss probabilities, followed by a union
bound, gives a conservative difference interval $[L_g-U_l,U_g-L_l]$.
For the near-rank pilot comparison with no observed discordance, the ordinary
conservative interval is $[-.00219,.00219]$, and the simultaneous interval
is $[-.00377,.00377]$. This reporting repair leaves the procedures and draws
unchanged and retains the original approximations. Exact marginal simultaneous
intervals use error .05/24 per cell. Paired simultaneous bounds use .05/48
for each of the two binomial proportions in 24 comparisons. Each family is
controlled separately; no combined .95 guarantee across both families is
claimed. The binomial count inversion is the elementary construction in
Section~\ref{s61:binomial-inversion} applied to independent simulation requests.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{rrrrr}
\toprule
Evaluation dates & Pilot dates & Repeat & Memory ratio & Time ratio\\
\midrule
12,000 & 48,000 & 1 & 0.921 & 0.992\\
12,000 & 48,000 & 2 & 0.937 & 0.989\\
120,000 & 480,000 & 1 & 0.544 & 0.906\\
120,000 & 480,000 & 2 & 0.599 & 1.071\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Streaming/dense ratios for complete local pilot tuning, refit and inference. Each route includes imports, input hashing, output persistence and read-back. Input acquisition is excluded equally; resident mapped pages count in peak memory. Order reverses between repeats.}
\label{tab:v10:workload}
\end{table}
Independent dense numerical comparisons cover both covariance choices,
chronological split boundaries and chunks of 1, 5, 37 and 4096 rows. The
largest scaled difference is $1.6\times10^{-14}$ in those checks and
$3.3\times10^{-14}$ in the complete workloads. Audit rank/boundary refusals
and invalid histories retain their meaning. At 120,000 evaluation dates and
480,000 pilot dates, memory ratios are .544 and .599. Elapsed ratios .906 and
1.071 show no consistent speed advantage. The smaller case has only modest
memory differences, because imports and other fixed costs matter. These
four paired comparisons (eight fresh worker runs) establish a local selected memory benefit;
two repeats are too few to characterize a broad performance distribution.
No partial-fit recovery or bank-platform service level follows.

The financial precision account remains material. At the baseline the
fourfold pilot's median interval width is about USD\,498,000; at 4800 dates
it is about USD\,252,000. These values belong to the stipulated 48-branch
synthetic population. They are neither bank estimates nor a stated acceptable
decision width. Extra audit information cannot be assigned a causal cost benefit
from these unpaired design cells; the comparative pilot arms are paired within
each cell. A bank precision target and prices for independent histories and
gold audits are still needed before claiming economic advantage.

\section{Information and adoption boundaries}
\label{v10:limits}

The extra pilot must be independent of evaluation under an invariant relevant
law. A bank cannot replace that condition with arbitrary historical volume;
regime changes or overlapping histories require a different separation and
influence argument. Likewise, more nuisance history cannot create representative
identity truth. Near-singular audit information can still require refusal, and
false scientific declarations can yield precise but invalid financial answers.
Earlier omitted-feature and endogenous-map counterexamples remain relevant.

The selected implementation supplies a bounded scientific operation. It does
not identify a general nonlinear private-state model, retain the true class in
arbitrary latent-graph discovery, or establish rates for an arbitrary learner.
Independent review, authentic bank assignment and source clocks, audit truth,
target storage and concurrency, adopted interfaces and measured analyst costs
remain distinct inputs to product qualification. These distinctions determine
which evidence the funding desk can act on and which claims still need testing. The comparisons separate three investments: pilot history addresses the specified nuisance error, representative audits inform the assignment inverse, and streaming reduces working storage for the same calculation. None substitutes for the others. The next chapter replaces a near-rank refusal with a projected uncertainty set and asks whether its financial width is useful.

chapters.title: Funding value when customer identity is uncertain

segments.text:
\chapter{Funding value when customer identity is uncertain}
\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection}


\begin{quote}\small
The regular funding interval cannot support inference when a representative identity
audit cannot distinguish two candidate portfolio assignments. An alternative reporting design uses simultaneous bands for the four observable
candidate monetary responses, exact binomial audit intervals, and projection
through the assignment inverse without dividing by a nearly zero estimated
rank. In 3,000 fresh paired synthetic requests, the resulting set has high
all-request coverage but markedly worse financial precision. At the near-rank
design, 546 of 600 sets equal the whole real line. Exact audit inversion does
not make the response bands finite-sample exact, verify causal exogeneity, or
provide a bank decision threshold. These findings concern constructed funding studies; their usefulness for a
bank depends on the validity of the assumptions and the precision it needs.
\end{quote}

\section{The bank's target and the rank-one obstruction}

The target remains the value of a one-month 10-basis-point price intervention
over a fixed balance-stock response horizon $H=6$, summed across 48 branches:
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:target}
 V=\sum_{h=0}^{H}w_h\beta\rho^h-C.
\end{equation}
The monetary weights $w_h$ include branch scale, margin, discounting and the
first-month repricing interaction; $C$ is the direct repricing cost. The
intervention, weights and horizon were fixed before this experiment. A funding
desk needs both an interval/set that covers under defensible assumptions and
a width small enough to distinguish a worthwhile price change. These are
separate requirements.

For identity-audit stratum $s\in\{0,1\}$, let $\theta_s$ be the focal
portfolio's weighted response before $C$, $\delta_s$ the companion's weighted
response, and $p_s$ the probability that the first candidate is correctly
assigned. Noninformative whole-horizon swaps give observable candidate
responses
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:mixture}
 \mu_{s1}=p_s\theta_s+(1-p_s)\delta_s,\qquad
 \mu_{s2}=(1-p_s)\theta_s+p_s\delta_s.
\end{equation}
For $p_s\ne 1/2$, inversion yields
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}
 \theta_s=\frac{p_s\mu_{s1}-(1-p_s)\mu_{s2}}{2p_s-1},\qquad
 V=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C.
\end{equation}
At $p_s=1/2$, the two observable responses both equal
$(\theta_s+\delta_s)/2$. If the companion response is unrestricted,
$\theta_s$ is then unrestricted. A finite interval obtained by substituting
$\widehat p_s\approx1/2$ would conceal this identification failure. The
preserved V10 procedure instead uses a Wilson rank guard and returns
``unavailable'' when its audit interval crosses $1/2$. The new design reports
the full set of values compatible with primitive response and audit bands.

\section{Primitive inference before inversion}

The nuisance pilot is independent of evaluation and has $M=4T$ dates. It
retains the fixed six-column dictionary, chronological half-split ridge
selection and full-pilot refit of V10. Dependence within the pilot is allowed;
independence from evaluation and a stable relevant law are required. For each
evaluation date, let $v_t$ be the residualized action and $u_{tj}$ the
residualized, financially weighted candidate outcome for $j=1,2$. Write
\begin{equation}
 Q_s=\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_t^2,\qquad
 \widehat\mu_{sj}=Q_s^{-1}\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_tu_{tj}.
\end{equation}
Crucially, these are \emph{observable mixed-candidate} responses. Neither
an estimated audit probability nor the unstable inverse enters their score.
The scalar influence estimate is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:score}
 \widehat\phi_{tsj}=\frac{T1\{S_t=s\}v_t
 (u_{tj}-v_t\widehat\mu_{sj})}{Q_s}.
\end{equation}
For each of four coordinates separately, center the score over all $T$ dates
and sum lag products through the prespecified response horizon $H$. The
variance of the sample mean is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac}
 \widehat V_{sj}=T^{-2}\left\{\sum_t\widetilde\phi_{tsj}^2+
 2\sum_{k=1}^{H}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}
 \widetilde\phi_{tsj}\widetilde\phi_{t-k,sj}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Only positive finite estimates qualify. This untapered fixed-horizon formula
uses the V9 innovation-filtration argument under correct action-mean and
exogeneity premises. Newey and West's positive-semidefinite Bartlett
construction is a distinct inherited alternative, not a proof that
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac} is finite-sample positive or correctly calibrated under a
different law \cite{newey1986}. The orthogonal partialling-out score and
nuisance-product logic trace to the inspected primary DML text
\cite{dml2018}; its iid theorem does not supply this dependent-calendar
inference. The fixed-dictionary $M=4T$ centering rate is a project derivation
in the preserved V9 chapter.

Allocate $\alpha_R=.025$ among four two-sided normal response bands:
\begin{equation}
 B_{sj}=\left[\widehat\mu_{sj}\pm
 z_{1-\alpha_R/8}\sqrt{\widehat V_{sj}}\right].
\end{equation}
For independent representative binomial audits $(K_s,n_s)$, allocate
$\alpha_A=.025$ among two exact equal-tail binomial inversions $P_s$. Each
audit interval has error allocation $\alpha_A/2=.0125$ and tails of .00625.
The implementation computes beta-quantile endpoints rounded outwards; exact
binomial coverage was enumerated for sizes 1--15 on a probability grid and
compared to the existing inversion. This exact statement concerns only the
audit component. The response bands are normal/dependent-calendar
approximations, not exact finite-sample intervals.

Let $f(B_{s1},B_{s2},P_s)$ be the exact image of the rectangle under
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}, retaining disconnected and infinite components. The
reported financial set is the Minkowski sum
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:set}
 \mathcal V=\tfrac12 f(B_{01},B_{02},P_0)
 +\tfrac12 f(B_{11},B_{12},P_1)-C.
\end{equation}
On the event that all six primitive intervals cover their truths, $V\in
\mathcal V$ regardless of the rank of the audit matrix. For each fixed law
under the stated nuisance rate and response-score central limit theorem,
Bonferroni therefore gives $\Pr(V\in\mathcal V)\geq .95-o(1)$.
No uniform near-rank, false-law or finite-sample response guarantee is
claimed. At exact rank one, a compatible primitive region may project to the
whole real line; that is honest identification uncertainty, not a precise
answer. An empty projection is recorded as noncoverage, not replaced by an
unbounded set.

\section{Registered comparison and independent numerical challenge}

The design and author challenge were recorded before new draws. Five selected
stress cases each use 600 fresh paired requests: the 1,200-date baseline,
small audit, near-rank audit, persistent response and false exogeneity. The
same evaluation histories, fourfold pilot and audit counts feed both the
inherited regular pilot interval and the new projection. Pilot/evaluation/audit
seeds are disjoint from V10. The final journal records every request and
reconstructs all five summaries exactly. At 600 repetitions, the ordinary
Monte Carlo half-width near .95 is about .0174; the worst-case value is about
.0400. Exact-binomial Monte Carlo intervals and a five-cell Bonferroni family
are retained in the machine result. They describe these fixed synthetic laws,
not bank-population coverage.

Before the final draws, eight numerical challenges passed: small-count audit
coverage enumeration and comparison with the inherited inversion; whole-line
and disconnected rank-one sets; dense candidate-slope and horizon-covariance
arithmetic for baseline and near-rank fixtures; and rejection of invalid
counts, declarations, dimensions and nonfinite histories. These are author
checks, not independent scientific review. The streaming implementation keeps
fixed-dimensional pilot factors and four scalar lag accumulators, without
storing all evaluation scores.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Fresh paired funding inference: all-request coverage and useful precision. Each row has 600 independent synthetic requests. A whole-line set counts as coverage if it contains the fixed truth, but has no finite decision width. Finite median widths are in thousands of USD, conditional on a finite set.}
\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:tab:weak-audit-results}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
\toprule
Design & Regular cover & Set cover & Finite set & Whole line & Regular width & Set width \\
\midrule
Baseline & 567/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 499 & 1231 \\
Small audit & 571/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 499 & 1406 \\
Near rank & 130/600 & 600/600 & 54/600 & 546/600 & 1907 & 63712 \\
Persistent & 555/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 1341 & 3426 \\
False exogeneity & 122/600 & 591/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 565 & 1367 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


The baseline regular interval covered 567/600 requests; the projection set
covered 600/600. The respective median finite widths were approximately
USD 499,000 and USD 1.231 million. In the small-audit design the figures were
571/600 versus 600/600, with median widths USD 499,000 and USD 1.406 million.
The selected persistent design had 555/600 versus 600/600, at approximately
USD 1.341 million and USD 3.426 million median widths. These are wide
selected-law sets, not evidence that a bank would accept their precision.

Near rank, the regular procedure returned a finite interval in only 132/600
requests and covered on 130/600 all requests. The projection produced 546/600
whole-line sets; only 54 were finite. Their conditional median finite width
was about USD 63.7 million, versus USD 1.91 million among the regular
procedure's 132 available intervals. All 600 projected sets covered, mainly
because most contained every real value. Reporting only ``100\% coverage''
would invert the practical conclusion.

In the false-exogeneity design, regular coverage was 122/600 and projection
coverage was 591/600. The latter had median width about USD 1.367 million,
roughly 2.4 times the regular width. This high selected-law coverage does not
validate the false declaration. The method has no causal guarantee there;
a different violation magnitude or economic threshold can expose the bias.
No method was chosen after observing this cell, and no universal correction
is established.

\section{Financial interpretation and the information still needed}

Projection can trade noncoverage or refusal for width. That trade is not
automatically useful. A funding decision based on the sign of $V$ would need
the entire defensible set on one side of the bank's specified decision
threshold. A whole-line set can never meet that rule. Even the baseline median
set width exceeds the synthetic target value (about USD 375,000) by more than
a factor of three. The exercise does not provide a bank threshold, the price
of representative audit labels, or the cost and availability of independent
pilot history. Width conditional on a finite set cannot substitute for
all-request coverage and finite-set availability.

The inherited regular inverse is tighter in selected cases but can refuse
near rank and undercovers under some finite designs. A sharper transformed
average/difference confidence region or candidate-specific covariance
inversion is a substantive alternative; it would need its own simultaneous
dependent-score argument and numerical qualification. More representative
audit labels can shrink $P_s$ but cannot cure a false origin-swap or
exogeneity premise. New outcome-linked information may identify targets that
counts and candidate responses cannot. These alternatives require separate evaluation.

Chapter~\ref{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening} develops the transformed average/difference alternative and evaluates it on fresh paired requests, including weak audits, persistence and false exogeneity. That comparison addresses precision under the same target; it does not acquire the new causal information required to rule out confounding. Bank use would also require
credible histories and audit labels, an economically meaningful precision
threshold, measured costs and operating evidence. The local experiment
establishes neither an adopted service nor institutional savings.

\section*{Evidence and source scope}

The projection formula, bounded-memory implementation and synthetic
findings are project work. The cited sources support the specific technical
steps identified in the text; neither is presented as proving the new
construction. The study specification, code and complete results are retained
with the research materials. The literature cutoff is 7 October 2026.

chapters.title: Using shared information to narrow uncertainty

segments.text:
\chapter{Using shared information to narrow uncertainty}
\label{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening}

\begin{quote}\small
Separate response bands retain uncertainty about customer identity but can
produce broad funding-value sets. Shared information in the two observed
candidate responses can narrow those sets by forming average and difference
scores before covariance estimation. A repaired 3,600-request study finds narrower transformed sets in
all 2,937 paired finite cases of six selected designs, without a general
dominance theorem. Weak audit information remains the limiting factor: 558/600
near-rank outputs are whole-line; even with eight times as many audit labels,
105/600 are whole-line and the finite transformed median width is about
USD 15.4 million. A pathwise observational-equivalence construction shows that
false exogeneity cannot be solved by interval algebra alone. The study uses synthetic populations; performance for a particular bank
requires evidence about its assignment and observation processes.
\end{quote}

\section{A sharper primitive region, with the same target}

The financial target, independent fourfold nuisance pilot, fixed monetary
weights, exact independent-binomial audit inversion and two-candidate origin
mixture are those in Chapter~\ref{integrated:weak_audit_projection}. Write the two observable
candidate monetary responses in stratum $s$ as $\mu_{s1},\mu_{s2}$, the
correct-assignment probability as $p_s$, and the focal/companion responses as
$\theta_s,\delta_s$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening:eq:transform}
 A_s=\tfrac12(\mu_{s1}+\mu_{s2})=\tfrac12(\theta_s+\delta_s),\quad
 D_s=\tfrac12(\mu_{s1}-\mu_{s2})=
     \tfrac12(2p_s-1)(\theta_s-\delta_s),\quad
 \theta_s=A_s+\frac{D_s}{2p_s-1}.
\end{equation}
The value remains $V=(\theta_0+\theta_1)/2-C$. At $p_s=1/2$, $D_s=0$ in
the observational law but the focal response is not identified separately
from its companion. Projecting a region for $(A_s,D_s,p_s)$ must retain this
structural ambiguity; no transformation creates audit truth.

The separate-band method constructed four bands for the candidate
responses. Those bands can discard shared candidate noise. The alternative transforms the two financially weighted residual outcomes to their half-sum
and half-difference \emph{before} estimating the four corresponding action
slopes and fixed-horizon calendar score variances. Equivalently, if
$\widehat\phi_{s1},\widehat\phi_{s2}$ are the observable influence scores,
the new scores are $(\widehat\phi_{s1}\pm\widehat\phi_{s2})/2$. Their marginal
variances therefore include the candidate cross-covariance. Four two-sided
normal bands share response error .025 by Bonferroni; two exact equal-tail
binomial audit intervals share audit error .025. The reported set is the exact
image of the resulting $(A_s,D_s,p_s)$ rectangles under
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening:eq:transform}, combined with fixed half-stratum weights and direct
repricing cost. A valid joint primitive region still contains $V$ after
projection, but the new rectangle is not nested in the old candidate
rectangle. Neither finite-sample response coverage nor pointwise width
dominance is a theorem.

The normal/dependent-calendar bands inherit the conditional growing-pilot
rate and score assumptions from the preserved monograph. The inspected
primary DML paper establishes the orthogonal-score/rate premise in its own
iid setting, not this project's dependent result \cite{dml2018}. The
inspected Newey--West 1986 working paper supports a Bartlett covariance
alternative, not finite-sample validity of this untapered fixed-horizon
scalar score \cite{newey1986}. Exactness applies only to the binomial audit
component. Numerical qualification refuses nonpositive/nonfinite response
variance and a difference-score variance at most
$(8\epsilon_{\rm machine})^2$ times its positive average-score variance.
That last guard prevents floating-point roundoff from turning a deterministic
zero difference into a falsely precise normal band.

\section{Registration, preserved failure and fresh comparison}

The original set's large widths motivated this separate plan, which was
registered before the follow-up's final draws. Its first 3,600 requests are
retained as \emph{exploratory and not qualified}. An adversarial fixture with
identical candidate outcomes exposed an inadequate zero-variance guard: the
fitted difference-score variance was numerically positive, roughly
$2\times10^{-33}$ of the average-score variance. The initial check had
exercised an exactly zero accumulator but failed to require refusal for this
fitted fixture. The complete initial code, specification, check receipt,
journal and summary were archived and read back before repair. The scale-aware
guard and a strengthened refusal check were registered before a new 3,600-draw
comparison with a fresh seed. The initial results were not promoted or
quietly hash-replaced.

The qualified comparison holds each evaluation history, 4,800-date independent
pilot and audit counts fixed across two methods: the candidate-response
rectangle and the transformed average/difference rectangle. Five 1,200-date
stress laws are inherited; a sixth keeps the near-rank law but uses 12,800
instead of 1,600 representative audit labels \emph{per stratum}. All have
600 fresh requests, no early stopping, the same fourfold pilot training and
the same error allocation. Numerical checks compare transformed slopes and
lag covariance with an independent dense four-coordinate calculation; its
maximum scaled variance difference was $1.65\times10^{-15}$. Whole-line,
disconnected and empty rank-one geometry, the repaired degenerate fixture and
a pathwise causal counterexample were checked separately. A read-only journal
reconstruction verifies all 3,600 request identities, both primitive bands,
audit intervals, financial sets, coverage counts and paired finite widths.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\caption{Fresh 600-request matched designs. C is the candidate rectangle and A/D the transformed average/difference rectangle. Finite median widths are thousands of USD and are descriptive only on the paired finite subset. Whole-line outputs have no finite decision width.}
\label{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening:tab:sharpening}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
\toprule
Design & C cover & A/D cover & Both finite & Whole A/D & C width & A/D width \\
\midrule
Baseline & 600/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 1229 & 1096 \\
Small audit & 600/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 1410 & 1178 \\
Near rank & 600/600 & 600/600 & 42/600 & 558/600 & 51990 & 16208 \\
Persistent & 600/600 & 600/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 3387 & 2889 \\
False exog. & 597/600 & 561/600 & 600/600 & 0/600 & 1375 & 1181 \\
Near rank, 8x audit & 600/600 & 600/600 & 495/600 & 105/600 & 47823 & 15437 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


Across the six selected designs, the transformed set was narrower in all
2,937 requests where \emph{both} sets were finite. This is a paired descriptive
result under the registered laws, not a width theorem or an economic
qualification. Baseline median finite width fell from about USD 1.229 million
to USD 1.096 million; small-audit width fell from USD 1.410 million to
USD 1.178 million. Both still exceed the approximately USD 375,000 synthetic
baseline target by a wide margin. Under persistent responses, median width
fell from USD 3.387 million to USD 2.889 million. All four selected valid-law
cells and the higher-audit cell showed 600/600 synthetic coverage for both
sets; six-cell simultaneous Monte Carlo intervals and individual counts are
saved. This is evidence about fixed simulators, not a bank coverage guarantee.

At the original near-rank audit size, each method returned 558/600 whole-line
sets. Only 42 were finite; their respective median widths were roughly
USD 52.0 million and USD 16.2 million. Increasing audits eightfold raised
finite availability to 495/600, but 105/600 sets still spanned the whole line.
Among the 495 paired finite cases, transformed median width was about
USD 15.4 million, versus USD 47.8 million for the candidate rectangle. Audit
information can improve availability without producing an actionable bank
interval; its acquisition cost and decision threshold are unknown.

Under false exogeneity, candidate and transformed sets covered respectively
597/600 and 561/600 of the original causal target. Tightening lost coverage
in 36 paired requests and gained none. The second fraction is 0.935, but no
coverage theorem applies when the action innovation restriction is false.
The high first fraction is equally incapable of verifying that restriction.

\section{Why exogeneity is an information problem}

The failure is not merely an interval formula. Let
$m(W_t)=.5W_t+.2(W_t^2-1)$, $A_t=m(W_t)+e_t$, and let $g(W_t)$ be an
otherwise unknown baseline balance response. Consider the structural law
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening:eq:confounded}
 B_t=\rho B_{t-1}+\beta A_t+g(W_t)
      +\sigma\{c e_t+\sqrt{1-c^2}\,z_t\}+\xi_t,
\end{equation}
with independent centered $e_t,z_t,\xi_t$ before the displayed shared term.
Define a second law with independent structural error but
\begin{equation}
 \beta'=\beta+\sigma c,\qquad
 g'(W)=g(W)-\sigma c\,m(W),\qquad
 B'_t=\rho B'_{t-1}+\beta'A_t+g'(W_t)
       +\sigma\sqrt{1-c^2}\,z_t+\xi_t.
\end{equation}
Because $A_t-m(W_t)=e_t$, the two observed balance recursions are
identical path by path for the same initial balance and exogenous draws.
The candidate swaps, independent audit labels and any statistic of the
observed histories are therefore identical as well. Yet under a one-month
intervention on $A_t$, the first law has response $\beta\rho^h$ and the
second $(\beta+\sigma c)\rho^h$. At the registered false-law values
$\sigma=2$, $c=.5$, their one-unit response coefficients differ by 1 and
the fixed financial target differs by about USD 387,575. A direct coupled
numerical witness reproduced identical observed paths to floating precision.

This is an identification counterexample for a class permitting the adjusted
nuisance mean $g'$. An externally known $g$, randomized action variation,
valid instrument or other justified scientific restriction could separate
the laws. More audit labels about candidate identity or a narrower confidence
box alone cannot. Numeric declarations of exogeneity are assertions to be
validated by assignment and source owners, not tests performed by the API.

\section{Decision and delivery boundaries}

The transformed region is a locally reproducible way to use covariance that
the first box omitted. Its precision may still be inadequate for a financial decision: whole-line
sets and multi-million-dollar finite widths remain under weak audit rank,
even in the higher-audit cell. The observational counterexample isolates a separate identification limit that requires new causal information. Any next
statistical refinement must be derived, preregistered and tested on fresh
adverse laws, reporting all-request coverage and finite decision precision.

The bank has not supplied an acceptable value-width threshold, representative
history/audit prices, authentic assignment truth, independent reviewers,
target-platform service evidence or an adopted interface. Bank use still requires independent review and evidence that the
method applies to the institution and decision being considered. The next chapter changes the observation itself: selected audits reveal the focal outcome history rather than only whether a candidate assignment is correct. This can resolve the identity ambiguity, while the exogeneity counterexample continues to apply. Its benefit must therefore be compared with both the new label requirements and the remaining uncertainty.

\section*{Sources and reproducibility}

The transformation, repaired numerical check, observational example,
registered study and financial interpretation are project contributions.
The cited sources support only the technical results attributed to them.
The original failed run and the repaired comparison remain available with
the specification and code. The literature cutoff is 7 October 2026.

chapters.title: Learning funding responses from verified histories

segments.text:
\chapter{Learning funding responses from verified histories}
\label{integrated:linked_funding}

\begin{quote}\small
Correctness counts can leave an individual funding response unidentified when
two candidate histories mix equally. An audit that resolves the actual focal
history supplies a different observation. We derive a sampled-outcome score
for the existing continuous-action, common-calendar funding target, including
its additional audit variance and independent nuisance pilot. A registered
4,800-request comparison finds finite intervals in every linked-outcome
request. At exact identity rank one, the augmented method has median width
about USD 527,000, while the count-based set is whole-line in all 600 requests.
Its coverage there is 559/600, so finite availability is not general
calibration. False exogeneity, incorrect inclusion probabilities and noisy
truth labels produce severe failures. The result identifies useful new
information to seek from a bank; its authenticity, price and acceptable
decision precision remain external requirements.
\end{quote}

\section{The same bank decision, with a richer observation}

A deposit team considers a one-month increase of ten basis points in its
offered rate. Let $F_t=(F_{t0},\ldots,F_{tH})'$ denote the focal portfolio's
balance response history at origin $t$, with $H=6$. Two candidate vectors
$Y_{t1},Y_{t2}$ contain the focal and companion histories in an uncertain
order. An origin's assignment applies to all seven horizons. The two strata
$S_t\in\{0,1\}$ each have fixed target weight one half. If $\beta_{sh}$ is
the focal balance response to the rate intervention, define
\begin{equation}
 \theta_s=\sum_{h=0}^{H}w_h\beta_{sh},\qquad
 V=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C.\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:value}
\end{equation}
The inherited synthetic account has 48 branches, USD one million per balance
unit, monthly margin .002 and discount .99. Its weights are
$w_h=48\times10^6\{.002(.99)^h-(.001/12)1\{h=0\}\}$ and
$C=48\times100\times10^6(.001/12)=400{,}000$ USD. The immediate induced
balance also pays the increased rate; future margins are discounted once.
With focal response $2(.82)^h$, the target is USD 375,149, or USD 751,749
when persistence is .96. These are reproducible synthetic accounts, not
measured bank profits.

Chapters~\ref{integrated:weak_audit_projection} and~\ref{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening} infer $V$ from candidate responses and independent correctness counts. If the probability $p_s$ of the first candidate being
focal equals one half, the mean mixing equations cannot separate focal and
companion effects. Better interval algebra retains that ambiguity. Consider
instead an audit indicator $R_t$ with known probability $q_t>0$ that, when
selected, reveals \emph{which stored candidate history is focal}. The bank
must provide this information in both evaluation and independent pilot
histories. One audit resolves an origin's vector, not seven independent
audits. Unselected labels are unavailable to the estimator.

This is an extension of the monograph's independent-pair audit argument to
the selected dependent funding calendar. It does not identify persistent
maps across arbitrary customer pairs, arbitrary shared audit errors or
many-to-many ownership. Here the inherited candidate swaps are independent
by origin and the new audit draws are conditionally independent across
origins given the complete histories and their supplied probabilities.

\section{Identification from sampled linked outcomes}

Let $B_t=(Y_{t1}+Y_{t2})/2$ be the observed candidate average and let
$\mathcal H$ contain all complete focal/companion histories, assignments and
actions before audit randomization. Define the vector pseudo-outcome
\begin{equation}
 Z_t=B_t+\frac{R_t}{q_t}(F_t-B_t),\qquad
 \E[R_t\mid\mathcal H]=q_t.\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:pseudo}
\end{equation}
Only the selected term requires the focal identity. Conditional expectation
gives $\E[Z_t\mid\mathcal H]=F_t$ exactly. No inverse $1/(2p_s-1)$ appears;
indeed swapping the candidate names and complementing the selected audit
labels leaves $Z_t$ unchanged. The alternative $Z_t^{I}=R_tF_t/q_t$ has the
same conditional expectation, but uses no observed average as augmentation.
There is no unconditional theorem that either has lower variance for every
possible outcome law.

Write $A_t=m_s(X_t)+v_t$ for the observed action, where $X_t$ contains the
fixed driver dictionary and stratum. Let
$\ell_s(X_t)=\E[w'Z_t\mid X_t,S_t=s]$.
Under the inherited exogenous-innovation response law,
\begin{equation}
 \E\!\left[1\{S_t=s\}v_t
   \{w'Z_t-\ell_s(X_t)-\theta_sv_t\}\right]=0,
 \qquad Q_s=\E[1\{S_t=s\}v_t^2]>0.\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:score}
\end{equation}
Equation~\eqref{integrated:linked_funding:eq:pseudo} reduces this observed moment to the corresponding
focal-outcome moment. Thus the same intervention target is identified even
at $p_s=1/2$, provided the new audit law and the causal action restriction
are true. The conditional expectation identity does not establish exogeneity.

An independent 4,800-origin pilot selects among the fixed penalties
$0,1,10,100$ using first-half fitting and second-half standardized prediction
loss, then refits on its whole history. Its outcomes are the same audited
pseudo-outcomes, so its labels are part of the information bill. On the
1,200 evaluation origins, set $\widehat v_t=A_t-\widehat m_s(X_t)$ and
$\widehat u_t=w'Z_t-\widehat\ell_s(X_t)$. The estimator is
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\theta_s=
 \frac{\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}\widehat v_t\widehat u_t}
      {\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}\widehat v_t^2},\qquad
 \widehat V=\tfrac12(\widehat\theta_0+\widehat\theta_1)-C.
 \label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:estimate}
\end{equation}
The partialling-out orthogonality and joint nuisance-product/action-square
rate premise appear in the inspected DML original \cite{dml2018}.
That paper's iid result does not by itself prove the dependent result here.
For this fixed stable Gaussian dictionary, fixed $q\ge q_{\min}>0$ and
independent invariant pilot, coefficient errors of order $M^{-1/2}$ give
product remainders $O_p(M^{-1})=o_p(T^{-1/2})$ when $M=4T$. This is a
pointwise growing-history statement, not a uniform guarantee when audit
probability tends to zero or persistence tends to one. A falsely supplied
probability changes the population moment before any rate argument applies.

\section{Audit variance on a shared calendar}

Define the oracle scalar influence for $V$ using focal outcomes as $\psi_t^F$.
With $c_t=\tfrac12\sum_s1\{S_t=s\}v_t/Q_s$, the pseudo-outcome influence is
\begin{equation}
 \psi_t^Z=\psi_t^F+a_t,
 \qquad a_t=c_t(R_t/q_t-1)w'(F_t-B_t).\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:decompose}
\end{equation}
Conditionally on $\mathcal H$, $\E a_t=0$. Independent audit randomization
also gives $\E[a_ta_u\mid\mathcal H]=0$ for $u\ne t$, and every $a_t$ is
uncorrelated with any complete-history score $\psi_u^F$. Its variance is
\begin{equation}
 \E a_t^2=\E\!\left[c_t^2(1/q_t-1)\{w'(F_t-B_t)\}^2\right].
 \label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:auditvar}
\end{equation}
The added audit term therefore changes lag zero only. This conclusion uses
independent audit draws \emph{conditional on the complete histories}; a
persistent audit mechanism or correlated label errors needs a new argument.

For the latent focal score, the monograph's innovation filtration condition
averages the current exogenous action innovation and shocks through $t+H$
to zero, conditional on the full exogenous driver path and shocks before $t$.
The score is measurable through $t+H$. A later score more than $H$ dates away
has conditional mean zero given the earlier one, giving zero covariance
beyond $H$. The scores need not be $H$-dependent. Stable roots, finite higher
moments and stationary mixing supply the score CLT; the finite horizon by
itself is insufficient. This condition fails under the deliberately endogenous
innovation law.

Using the fitted scalar score
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\psi_t=\frac{T}{2}
 \sum_s\frac{1\{S_t=s\}\widehat v_t
   (\widehat u_t-\widehat\theta_s\widehat v_t)}
  {\sum_j1\{S_j=s\}\widehat v_j^2},
\end{equation}
center it by its sample mean and write the centered scores as $d_t$.
The selected variance estimate and normal interval are
\begin{equation}
 \widehat s^2=T^{-2}\!\left\{\sum_t d_t^2+
       2\sum_{k=1}^{H}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}d_td_{t-k}\right\},
 \qquad \widehat V\pm z_{.975}\widehat s.\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:variance}
\end{equation}
The empirical scores include audit noise, so adding a second independent
``audit variance'' would double count it. We refuse nonpositive/nonfinite
variance, absent sampled strata and deterministic scores at the numerical
roundoff floor. We do not clip a negative estimate into an interval.
The inspected Newey--West original proves positive semidefiniteness for its
Bartlett weighting \cite{newey1986}; this untapered, fixed-horizon scalar
construction is different and inherits no such guarantee. Its advantage
within the stated filtration law is avoiding attenuation of nonzero short-lag
covariances.

\section{Fresh comparison and retained adverse evidence}

The eight designs and three procedures were fixed before their final draws.
Each design has 600 independent requests, the same evaluation/pilot histories
across methods, and distinct random streams for count audits and outcome-linked
audits. The count method uses 1,600 correctness labels per stratum and the
previous half-sum/half-difference rectangular projection. The linked methods
use $q=.25$ in both histories, except the $q=.10$ low-audit cell. Near rank
means $(p_0,p_1)=(.55,.515)$; exact rank means $(.5,.5)$; the baseline is
$(.9,.85)$. The persistent cell changes the balance root from .82 to .96.
Three adverse cells separately violate exogeneity, actual inclusion or
label truth. Neither the reported probabilities nor the declarations test
their own truth.

All 4,800 requests produced computed sets for all three procedures. The
linked intervals were finite in every request. Table~\ref{integrated:linked_funding:tab:coverage}
reports all-request coverage and availability, and
Table~\ref{integrated:linked_funding:tab:diagnostics} retains bias, empirical dispersion and labels.
Exact-binomial Monte Carlo intervals are saved for each coverage frequency,
with Bonferroni simultaneous control across all 24 design/method combinations.
They describe Monte Carlo uncertainty under these selected laws only.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\caption{Fresh 600-request cells. C uses count-audit transformed sets; A uses augmented linked outcomes; I uses inverse audit weighting. Widths are conditional finite medians in thousands of USD.}

Design & C cover & A cover & I cover & C finite & A finite & A width & I width\\\midrule
Baseline & 600 & 564 & 572 & 600 & 600 & 524 & 1091\\

Low linked audit & 600 & 572 & 568 & 51 & 600 & 599 & 1762\\
