In the near-rank cell, the count set was whole-line in 552/600 requests;
its 48 finite sets had median width USD 17.396 million. The augmented
interval was finite in all 600 with median width USD 528,513 and coverage
572/600. In all 48 paired finite requests it was narrower. At exact rank,
the count set was whole-line in all 600 requests, while the augmented median
width was USD 526,663. This is new outcome information resolving an old
mean ambiguity; it is not an improvement obtained from the old count data
alone. There is no paired finite width ratio at exact rank because the
baseline has no finite set there.

Finite precision does not establish 95\% calibration. Exact-rank augmented
coverage is $559/600=.9317$, with mean SE/empirical SD .943. Its individual
Monte Carlo interval is approximately $[.9084,.9505]$ and simultaneous
interval $[.8942,.9593]$. Baseline augmented coverage is \mbox{$564/600=.94$}.
These finite samples neither prove a general failure nor qualify uniform
nominal coverage. Under the persistent law, augmented median width is USD
1.413 million against synthetic value USD .752 million. The low-audit
design uses about 601 linked labels across both histories and has median
width USD 599,027. The ordinary $q=.25$ designs use about 1,500 labels.
Neither label count is an observed market price.

The augmented interval was narrower than inverse weighting in 4,793 of
4,800 matched requests and wider in seven wrong-inclusion requests. This
descriptive result includes invalid-law cells and has no universal ordering
interpretation. Even on the valid laws, reducing the augmented width relative
to the count box trades the box's strong conservatism for a normal-approximation
interval; one must assess coverage and precision together.

\section{Why truthful audits and exogeneity remain essential}

The false-exogeneity cell has innovation correlation .5 with a balance shock
of scale 2. The inherited observational-equivalence argument shifts the
observed action coefficient by one. The financial shift is therefore
$\sum_h w_h(.82)^h=387{,}575$ USD. The observed augmented bias is USD 388,119,
and coverage is only 148/600. Resolving focal identity does not resolve action
confounding; the wide count set's 600/600 coverage in this cell supplies no
causal validation.

If actual inclusion is $q_a$ but the caller supplies $q_d$, then
\begin{equation}
 \E[Z_t\mid\mathcal H]
  =B_t+\frac{q_a}{q_d}(F_t-B_t).\label{integrated:linked_funding:eq:wrongq}
\end{equation}
With $q_a=.10$, $q_d=.25$, focal coefficient 2 and companion .5, the
augmented coefficient is 1.55, not 2. Its population monetary bias is about
USD $-174{,}409$, compared with the saved bias USD $-179{,}157$. Coverage
is 378/600. Pure inverse weighting instead targets coefficient .8, explaining
its larger negative bias and 159/600 coverage. This failure happens even
with independent selection; more complicated unknown selection laws add
further obligations.

If selected labels independently flip with probability $e$, the apparent
focal mean becomes $(1-e)F_t+eG_t$, where $G_t$ is the companion. For $e=.15$
the coefficient shifts by $.15(.5-2)=-.225$, producing population monetary
bias about USD $-87{,}204$. The augmented observed bias is USD $-84{,}726$
and coverage 528/600. Label-error correction would need external gold truth
and its sampling uncertainty; pretending that the label is exact has not
performed such a correction. These population identities and the numerical
audit-variance decomposition are project checks, not source-derived bank
guarantees.

\section{A design calculation before buying labels}

For a constant, truthful $q$, write
$K=\E[c_t^2\{w'(F_t-B_t)\}^2]$ and let $\Omega_F$ be the latent focal
long-run variance. Equation~\eqref{integrated:linked_funding:eq:auditvar} gives
$\Omega_Z=\Omega_F+(1/q-1)K$. If an external bank decision specifies a
maximum interval width $w_\star$, its first-order planning inequality is
\begin{equation}
 \Omega_F+(1/q-1)K\le
 L,\qquad L=T\left(\frac{w_\star}{2z_{.975}}\right)^2.
\end{equation}
When $K>0$ and $L\ge\Omega_F$, this gives
$q\ge K/(L-\Omega_F+K)$; if $L<\Omega_F$, even complete audit cannot meet
the width target at that calendar size. If $K=0$, audits add no variance in
this specific moment, but the caller still needs a valid information law.
This algebra is a planning approximation, not a finite-sample coverage
certificate. Values of $K$ and $\Omega_F$ used for a new design must come from
an independent design pilot and include their estimation uncertainty.

For the registered $M=4T$ pilot, expected linked-label demand is $q(T+M)=5qT$.
An economic comparison also needs history acquisition, truthful resolution,
pilot fitting, complete evaluation and review costs. Count labels and linked
histories are different services; 1,500 linked histories cannot be declared
cheaper than 3,200 correctness labels without actual prices. The bank has
supplied neither those prices nor $w_\star$. A fixed precision target and
authentic audit design are the next inputs required to turn this construction
into an investment or deployment decision.

\section*{Evidence, scope and continuation}

Independent enumeration checks the audit expectation and added diagonal
variance. Dense fitting and direct lag products agree with the implementation
across chunk boundaries to about $1.9\times10^{-14}$ relative error. Complete
audits reduce to observed focal histories; unsampled labels, invalid
probabilities and degenerate variance are rejected. The first 600 raw requests
were preserved as unqualified after an interval-serialization mismatch stopped
summary generation. The shared-format repair and round-trip check preceded a
fresh registered seed; none of those first requests is part of the 4,800 final
comparison. The saved journal reconstructs every summary and interval; eight
fixed requests were separately regenerated. These are author checks, not an
independent scientific review.

Resolving the actual customer history supplies information that
correctness counts alone can miss. Finite intervals at exact identity rank
one are demonstrated for the specified funding model; their calibration and
useful precision for a bank remain uncertain. Valid assignment, known audit
inclusion and accurate labels are essential. Independent origin audits do
not establish inference under arbitrary persistence of customer identity and
calendar shocks. Nonlinear policies, temporal graphs and other learners
require their own arguments. Bank adoption also needs independent review,
relevant operating trials and measured costs. The following comparison asks what stronger assignment and sampling information can achieve across funding, servicing, discovery and learning. It retains this chapter's distinction between finite availability, calibrated uncertainty and worthwhile financial precision; the stronger information has its own acquisition and feasibility costs.

The experiment preserves its specification, code, completed results
and the failed partial run. These records distinguish the reported evidence
from unperformed work. The literature cutoff remains 7 October 2026. No new exhaustive source search
was performed; the two inherited primary copies were reinspected for the
limited roles cited above.

chapters.title: What additional information buys

segments.text:
\chapter{What additional information buys}
\label{integrated:master_execution}

\begin{quote}\small
A causal banking service must return a decision quantity together with the information and uncertainty that make it defensible. Funding responses, sequential servicing, temporal relationships and verified customer histories reveal different limits on that information. A funding experiment uses supplied action randomization and independent calendars to remove a fitted-ratio mean shift. A nonlinear servicing extension evaluates a fixed observable policy using truthful state audits and supplied action probabilities. Both meet a preregistered minimum-coverage screen on selected synthetic grids with conservative 99\% critical values. A joint pair/calendar/gold-label experiment still fails finite calibration in important regimes. A corrected temporal graph union retains effects but can return the whole real line. A corrected sparse learner fails qualification at higher dimension or support. Full linked-outcome streaming agrees with its dense reference and survives real local process failures, without a consistent measured performance gain. These are research findings from specified experiments. Their use in a bank requires independent review, credible assignment and observation information, suitable operating performance and a defensible economic case.
\end{quote}

\section{One decision, several kinds of evidence}
A bank deciding whether to raise a deposit rate, change a collections policy or act on a discovered relationship needs a target with units and timing. It also needs an observation model: a row may not identify the customer whose balance matters; a public signal may omit the private state used by a historical decision maker; an apparent edge may permit several intervention effects. Computation cannot supply missing identity, assignment or exclusion information.

The experiments ask whether changing the available information improves
a stated banking comparison. A negative result can explain which information
is missing. An uncertainty set can be statistically defensible yet too wide
to distinguish a profitable action from a loss. Scientific validity and
useful precision therefore need separate attention.

Every table cell has 512 fresh Monte Carlo requests. Covers uses all requests, including refusals. MC lower is a simultaneous one-sided exact-binomial 95\% lower bound, Bonferroni-adjusted over all method/cell comparisons in the study. The minimum screen is .95. These screens do not prove uniform coverage or validate supplied scientific assumptions. Primary methods use frozen 99\% critical values or covariance regions; some challengers use 95\% critical values. Width and coverage have a disclosed tradeoff.

\section{Funding: change information to remove an error}
\subsection{Target, linked audits and pilot bias}
The target is a one-month ten-basis-point increase over $H=6$ future months. With two equally weighted strata,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V&=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C,\qquad \theta_s=w'\beta_s,\\
 w_h&=48\cdot10^6\{.002(.99)^h-(.001/12)1\{h=0\}\},\quad C=400{,}000.
\end{aligned}
\]
A balance unit is USD one million and the synthetic account has 48 branches. Future margin is discounted once. Response $2(.82)^h$ gives approximately USD 375,149; persistence .96 gives USD 751,749. These are reproducible accounts, not bank profits.

Let $F_t$ be the focal response and $Y_{t1},Y_{t2}$ candidate histories. A truthful identity audit $R_t$ has known inclusion $q_t>0$. Conditional on complete histories $\mathcal H$, assume $\E[R_t\mid\mathcal H]=q_t$ and set
\[
 B_t=(Y_{t1}+Y_{t2})/2,\qquad Z_t=B_t+R_t(F_t-B_t)/q_t.
\]
Then $\E[Z_t\mid\mathcal H]=F_t$, without division by identity rank $2p_s-1$. Each origin audit resolves a horizon vector, not seven independent labels. Truthful links are additional information beyond correctness counts.

For the inherited independent-pilot ratio, define $d_m=\widehat m-m$ and $d_\ell=\widehat\ell-\ell$. With innovation variance one, the conditional population slope is
\[
 \frac{\theta_s+\E[d_md_\ell\mid P]}{1+\E[d_m^2\mid P]}.
\]
A residual calendar variance does not estimate this pilot-dependent mean shift. Orthogonal-score product conditions support a growing-pilot argument \cite{dml2018}; the cited iid result does not prove finite dependent-calendar calibration here.

\subsection{Known randomization and independent calendars}
Suppose the true assignment is supplied as $A=m(X)+v$, with $\E[v\mid X]=0$ and $\E[v^2\mid X]=1$. The synthetic law uses $m(W)=.5W+.2(W^2-1)$. An independent pilot produces an outcome prediction $\widehat\ell$ and scalar control $\widehat b$. Define
\[
 G_t=v_t\{w'Z_t-\widehat\ell(X_t)\}-\widehat b(v_t^2-1).
\]
Conditional on the pilot, $\E[v\widehat\ell(X)]=0$ and $\E[v^2-1]=0$. Exogeneity and truthful inclusion give $\E[G_t\mid P]=\theta$. The pilot affects variance, but not the mean. The fitted-action error and ratio denominator disappear because assignment information is supplied. The study has equally sampled strata and a common response; unequal sampling would need explicit weights.

With $K$ independent calendars and $L$ consecutive origins each, let $U_k=L^{-1}\sum_tG_{kt}$. Then
\[
 \widehat V=K^{-1}\sum_k U_k-C,\qquad
 \widehat s^2=\frac1{K(K-1)}\sum_k(U_k-\overline U)^2.
\]
The variance contains all within-calendar covariance. Its conditional mean is constant, so no pilot-dependent mean variance is omitted. An iid-calendar CLT as $K\to\infty$ justifies the limit; Student critical values are asymptotically equivalent, not exact pivots for these non-Gaussian means.

The frozen design has $K=24$, $L=50$ (12 for the short cell), a fourfold pilot and 99\% Student intervals. Adjacent blocks of one bank series are not independent calendars, nor are branches sharing a national shock. This requirement has real feasibility and cost implications.

Table widths are USD. The challenger is the inherited stacked-calendar ratio using a 95\% interval.

\begin{center}\footnotesize\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}\toprule
Scenario & Covers & MC lower & Finite & Median width & Challenger\\
\midrule
baseline & 506/512 & 0.968 & 512/512 & 747,858 & 484/512 \\
small T & 501/512 & 0.954 & 512/512 & 1,457,144 & 466/512 \\
low q & 505/512 & 0.965 & 512/512 & 850,455 & 489/512 \\

All six valid cells pass the lower-bound screen and always return finite intervals. Persistence has median width USD 1.975 million against value USD .752 million. Passing coverage does not establish useful precision. Ordinary requests need about 1,500 linked labels; low audit about 600. The paired inherited ratio sees the same rows but stacks independent calendars; artificial boundaries mean this is not a new qualification of its original uninterrupted-calendar argument. That older study remains separate.

False exogeneity, wrong inclusion and label errors fail visibly. Wider critical values cannot repair those population errors. This is a scoped added-information route, not a universal correction or evidence that the bank can acquire independent economic calendars.

\section{Persistent maps, common dates and imperfect gold truth}
\subsection{One joint sampling law}
After multiplying outcomes by randomized signed actions, let focal and companion responses be
\[
 F_{it}=\beta+U_i+C_t+E_{it},\qquad D_{it}=\delta+V_i+C_t+J_{it}.
\]
Pair effects are iid across pairs; $C_t$ is an independent stationary Gaussian AR(1); cell disturbances are independent. Candidate order persists within a pair. A Bernoulli pair audit $R_i$ has known $q$, and its label independently flips with probability $e<1/2$. An independent representative sample of $M$ gold labels estimates $e$. This is a specific experiment, not arbitrary multiway dependence.

Let $\xi_i=1$ for a correct audit label and $-1$ for a flipped label. At the true $e$, $W_i=R_i\xi_i/[q(1-2e)]$ has mean one and second moment $a=1/[q(1-2e)^2]$. For $d=(\beta-\delta)/2$, the corrected score has decomposition
\begin{align*}
 Z_{it}&=\beta+P_i+C_t+H_{it},\\
 P_i&=(U_i+V_i)/2+W_i(U_i-V_i)/2+d(W_i-1),\\
 H_{it}&=(E_{it}+J_{it})/2+W_i(E_{it}-J_{it})/2.
\end{align*}
Pair and cell projections are uncorrelated. With pair variance $\sigma_p^2$ and cell variance $\sigma_e^2$,
\[
 \Var(P)=\sigma_p^2(1+a)/2+d^2(a-1),\quad
 \Var(H)=\sigma_e^2(1+a)/2.
\]
Thus the known-error variance of the mean is
\[
 \frac{\Var(P)}N+\frac{\sigma_c^2}{T^2}\left[T+2\sum_{k=1}^{T-1}(T-k)\rho^k\right]+\frac{\Var(H)}{NT}.
\]
Gold estimation adds $g^2e(1-e)/M$ at first order, $g=(\beta-\delta)/(1-2e)$. Curvature and random-derivative terms require a fixed rank margin and comparable pair/date/gold growth; their constants diverge near $e=.5$.

Persistent audits contribute to pair variance and cannot be averaged away merely by adding dates. Independent origin audits instead add a diagonal cell component. At $q=1,e=0$ the expression reduces to complete truth. Binary enumeration and direct Toeplitz covariance sums independently check the limits.

\subsection{Feasible precision still fails}
Row-mean variance and date HAC each count cell interaction. Subtracting its double-demeaned estimate once addresses that duplication under this law. It is not a generic dependent-panel repair. Rank uncertainty can cause refusal; Bartlett calendar variance remains biased at high finite persistence.

The reported monetary target is $1000\beta$ USD; interval widths are USD. The challenger retains the inherited double-counted interaction and a 95\% critical value.

\begin{center}\footnotesize\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}\toprule
Scenario & Covers & MC lower & Finite & Median width & Challenger\\
\midrule
balanced & 508/512 & 0.972 & 512/512 & 931 & 498/512 \\
pair scarce & 498/512 & 0.944 & 512/512 & 1,525 & 481/512 \\
date scarce & 498/512 & 0.944 & 512/512 & 815 & 461/512 \\
low audit & 489/512 & 0.921 & 512/512 & 1,749 & 462/512 \\
exact identity rank & 506/512 & 0.966 & 512/512 & 923 & 478/512 \\
persistent calendar & 442/512 & 0.813 & 512/512 & 987 & 379/512 \\
weak gold rank & 248/512 & 0.418 & 251/512 & 2,850 & 230/512 \\
long window & 472/512 & 0.880 & 512/512 & 1,167 & 413/512 \\
shared audits & 430/512 & 0.787 & 512/512 & 919 & 383/512 \\
wrong inclusion & 151/512 & 0.237 & 512/512 & 703 & 85/512 \\
endogenous label error & 482/512 & 0.904 & 512/512 & 899 & 426/512 \\
\bottomrule\end{tabular}\end{center}


The adjusted balanced and exact-identity cells pass, but scarce pairs/dates, low audit and persistence do not. Persistence covers 442/512 with lower bound .813. A longer window does not qualify it. A separate true-variance oracle covers 505/512 there, locating part of the feasible covariance difficulty; that oracle is not deployable bank information. Shared pair audits, false inclusion and state-dependent labels remain adverse laws.

A successor needs a justified stronger variance law, independent calendar information or enough pair/date/gold growth to control finite errors. Choosing a new window after observing results would not complete the frozen study. The negative finding specifies what further information and theory must address. Chapter~\ref{exec13:persistent-region} develops a finite confidence region under explicit variance and persistence bounds, and shows why unrestricted persistence prevents a uniform precision promise. That derivation changes the assumptions behind inference; it does not retrospectively qualify these failed requests.

\section{Nonlinear servicing with a supplied private logger}
\subsection{State, signal, action and reward}
The selected17 extension adds a nonlinear action reward to the inherited action-variance family:
\begin{align*}
 S_{t+1}&=\rho S_t+\gamma\tanh(S_t)+bA_t+\sqrt{q_{A_t}}\epsilon_{t+1},\\
 O_t&=S_t+\sqrt{v_o}\nu_t,\\
 p_t(1\mid S_t,O_t)&=.05+.9\operatorname{logistic}(\lambda_0+\lambda_sS_t+\lambda_oO_t),\\
 R_t&=\eta_0+\eta_sS_t+\eta_aA_t+\eta_{sa}S_tA_t+
 \eta_{\tanh}A_t\tanh(S_t)+\sqrt{v_R}\zeta_t.
\end{align*}
The private state precedes signal, historical action and reward. A deployed policy observes $O_t$, not $S_t$. Representative truthful full-state audits fix state scale/orientation; logger probabilities are actual supplied records. With full support and positive action probabilities, the transition/reward regressors are linearly independent and their Gaussian conditional laws identify this finite family. A noisy audit or guessed logger is a different experiment.

The complete likelihood multiplies initial, observation, Bernoulli action, reward and transition densities. Hidden-state likelihood fitting remains an efficiency alternative; this estimator uses extra logger information instead. Mechanism replacement supplies the intervention interpretation \cite{pearl2009}; the new numerical/inferential composition is project work.

\subsection{Sequential weighting and uncertainty}
For a policy chosen independently of evaluation,
\[
 W_t=\prod_{j\le t}\frac{1\{A_j=\pi_j(O_j)\}}{p_j(A_j\mid S_j,O_j)},\qquad
 V(\pi)=1000\E\left[\sum_{t=0}^2.97^t W_tR_t\right].
\]
Integrating each historical action cancels its denominator and replaces that action by the policy. This sequential change of measure covers the nonlinear transition and reward under the supplied true logger. It remains valid with a misspecified parametric transition if logger and audit truth remain correct.

One trajectory contributes one discounted weighted reward. Its sample variance retains within-path dependence. The fixed horizon and probability floor bound weights by $.05^{-3}$; Gaussian moments give finite variance. The trajectory CLT motivates 99\% Student intervals, not an exact finite $t$ law. Poor overlap can still make convergence slow. Thresholds $(0,.2,.4)$ are independently frozen; no unknown optimal value is inferred.

Widths are USD per trajectory. The challenger is the same weighting estimator with a 95\%, rather than 99\%, interval.

The five valid information cells and the transition-misspecification robustness cell pass the screen. Scarce audits have median width USD 2,339 per trajectory, versus baseline USD 735, against a common synthetic policy value about USD 1,174. Wrong logger probabilities cover 1/512. Declared leakage refuses all requests. A flag cannot detect concealed evaluation-data reuse, so provenance remains necessary.

Direct weighting has no filter or optimizer approximation. Synthetic targets are numerical references: a subsequent audit independently reconstructs complete likelihood with scalar densities, compares complex-step and finite-difference scores to $2.9\times10^{-9}$, and compares nested Gaussian quadrature with a refined grid to less than USD $4.8\times10^{-5}$. These checks occurred after evaluation; the earlier record overstated their pre-evaluation availability. They corroborate saved targets without changing methods or requests, but are not uniform numerical certificates or independent review.

Fixed-policy confidence does not imply uniform confidence over policies or optimal-value/regret bounds. Estimated logger probabilities would introduce additional nuisance uncertainty. Chapter~\ref{exec13:servicing-observed} develops one estimated-probability route for sufficient finite observed histories, bounded rewards and independent cohorts. Those restrictions differ from the nonlinear private-state experiment here; its guarantee cannot be transferred by substituting fitted logger probabilities into these saved requests. General policy optimization remains a separate research obligation.

\section{Temporal discovery: retain the class before answering}
\subsection{A stationary finite temporal law}
Let $X_t=(Z_t,A_t,Y_t)'$ satisfy
\[
 X_t=rX_{t-1}+\epsilon_t,\qquad r\in\{0,.4,.8\},
\]
with invariant Gaussian initialization and iid innovations. Innovation structure is
\[
 z=e_z,\qquad a=kz+l_au+e_a,\qquad y=\tau a+cz+l_yu+e_y.
\]
The latent root and errors are independent. The instantaneous intervention coefficient is $\tau$. In structural form the lag matrix is $r(I-B)$: a real restriction, not an arbitrary VAR. Unknown continuous lag and long-run interventions are different questions.

For every candidate $r$, form $E_t(r)=X_t-rX_{t-1}$. At the true candidate these are iid Gaussian innovations. Nine simultaneous variance bands---three coordinate variances and six signed pair sums/differences---give covariance inclusion by chi-square inversion and Bonferroni. Propagate each covariance box through all compatible graphs and union over all lag candidates.

Only inclusion at the true candidate is needed. Wrong-lag data need not be iid, and no selected lag is falsely treated as fixed. The finite innovation classes contain the inherited 40 broad latent structures or eight encouragement/sufficiency structures per lag. Graphs are removed only when necessary restrictions cannot intersect their covariance region. On true-law inclusion the true graph and effect survive.

With valid encouragement exclusion, $c=0$ and the latent root does not cause $Z$, so $\Cov(Z,Y)/\Cov(Z,A)=\tau$. Interval ratio propagation imposes no positive first-stage floor and preserves disconnected or unbounded sets. Broad latent models admit equal-covariance witnesses with arbitrary effect, giving $\R$. Extra scientific information must exclude those alternatives; selecting a convenient graph does not.

Widths are outcome/action units, conditional on finite returned sets. The challenger selects one lag before propagating its graph class.

The true graph and effect survive every valid request. Strong encouragement has median width 3.930 outcome/action units. Weak relevance and unrestricted latent observation return whole-line answers every time; persistence has five whole-line answers. The overall finite-availability screen fails because the weak-relevance and unrestricted latent cells never return finite sets. The persistent cell itself passes its original raw-fraction rule: $507/512=.990234375$ exceeds $.99$. Its five whole-line outcomes remain visible, and none of these availability counts establishes decision-useful precision or a confidence lower bound of $.99$. Section~\ref{exec13:temporal-design-review} explains the distinction and the successor design requirements \cite{exec13_temporal_design}.

False exclusion retains the true graph in zero requests even though broad effect intervals cover all targets. Numerical coverage cannot validate a false class. Hidden-history and selection labels likewise do not establish membership of their invalid observation laws. Independent symbolic covariance formulas and arbitrary-effect witnesses verify small-class reductions. Endpoint calculations have checked rounding behavior, not a full formal floating-point certificate. Arbitrary learned PAGs and richer hidden histories remain unqualified.

\section{A learner whose code matches its argument}
The residualized IV score is
\[
 \E[(Z-m_Z(X))\{Y-m_Y(X)-\theta(A-m_A(X))\}]=0.
\]
Independent-training nuisance errors shift the conditional moment by $\E[\delta_Z(\delta_Y-\theta\delta_A)]$. This is the inherited orthogonal-score principle \cite{dml2018}; dependent separation and actual selection need their own proof.

The corrected procedure has two outer calendar blocks separated by a gap. Inside each training block a further separated split selects a shrinking lasso grid. Inner training controls standardization; selected models are refit using only outer training data. Evaluation labels never tune penalties. Bartlett products stay within evaluation folds, never across the omitted gap. Actual feature/support overrides are honored.

For fixed dimension, a correct linear nuisance, positive Gram eigenvalues and fixed geometric mixing give root-sample moment/coefficient rates. A finite shrinking grid preserves that rate, including at selection boundaries. Products are then second order. A sufficiently increasing gap and growing covariance window supply a conditional asymptotic route. Growing dimension additionally needs restricted-eigenvalue and approximation/product-rate control. Prediction accuracy alone proves none of these. The grid has 20 or 60 controls, support three or eight, 640 origins and ordinarily a 40-origin gap.

Widths are outcome/action units. The challenger fits an unpenalized dense reference on the same permitted training folds.

Scenario & Covers & MC lower & Finite & Median width & Challenger\\
\midrule

high dimension & 499/512 & 0.949 & 512/512 & 0.245 & 468/512 \\
larger support & 493/512 & 0.934 & 512/512 & 0.250 & 490/512 \\
long gap & 504/512 & 0.963 & 512/512 & 0.261 & 495/512 \\
persistent & 501/512 & 0.954 & 512/512 & 0.250 & 489/512 \\
inadequate gap & 504/512 & 0.963 & 512/512 & 0.243 & 488/512 \\
nonlinear misspecification & 0/512 & 0.000 & 512/512 & 0.331 & 0/512 \\

Baseline, long gap and persistence pass. Higher dimension (.9491) and larger support (.9339) miss the .95 lower-bound rule. A failed screen prevents qualification but is not a universal undercoverage theorem. Nonlinear omitted nuisances cover zero targets. Weak IV gives median width 3.836 against true effect 1.2; a small-denominator guard is not weak-IV inference.

An independent constrained convex solver checks lasso, exact soft thresholding checks a selection boundary, and separate matrix algebra checks dense fitted-score covariance. Earlier evaluation-tuned requests remain preserved as exploratory and do not support this corrected argument. Next routes are independent-pilot covariance control, high-dimensional rates, richer prespecified nuisance bases and weak-IV test inversion. Chapter~\ref{exec13:dependent-pilot} develops explicit pilot-error and weak-instrument bounds for a different bounded, finite-dependent law, then assesses their precision before a larger experiment. The selected Gaussian failures here retain their original scope and outcomes.

\section{Keeping uncertainty visible in the reported result}
Each A-D result carries actual bounds or a refusal reason, units, assumptions and capability disposition. Finite intervals, disconnected sets, whole lines, empty sets and unavailable computations remain distinct. Computed sets without bounds reject. Null endpoints denote infinity only in the explicit extended-real schema, never zero or absent evidence.

The full linked method streams both pilot and evaluation pseudo-outcomes. Chronological pilot halves are compressed into augmented QR factors and online target moments. Validation uses the same fixed penalty losses, followed by full-pilot refit; bounded passes then compute estimates and covariance. Twelve dense-equivalence cases span chunks 1/37/257, low audit, identity rank and persistence. Relative tolerance $10^{-9}$ and absolute USD $10^{-6}$ assess numerical equivalence, not bank usefulness.

Complete workloads include input generation, tuning/refit, inference, serialization and total process memory. At 120,000 evaluation and 480,000 pilot origins, dense and streamed runs take about 1.08 and 1.71 seconds, with roughly 409 MiB peak RSS each. The streaming fit is slower. Input generation dominates memory; reduced auxiliary storage does not imply a large total RSS reduction. No consistent performance advantage is claimed, and a dense fallback is retained.

Recovery binds code/input hashes, seed and request count. Local locking, fsync, atomic record rename and a final manifest prevent partial publication. Real process deaths during fitting, a partially written checkpoint and final publication recover the same 12 requests on restart, replay without duplication and reject changed identities. This is local single-process evidence; multi-host coordination and bank service levels need their platform operators.

\section{Financial value and unresolved evidence}
If $\Delta L$ is held-out improvement in bank decision loss over an accepted workflow, then
\[
 \mathrm{Net\ value}=\Delta L-C_{\rm audit}-C_{\rm calendar}-C_{\rm integration}
 -C_{\rm compute}-C_{\rm review}-C_{\rm operation}.
\]
The research supplies synthetic precision and local computing measurements, not bank values for these costs. Linked histories, correctness labels and full-state audits are different services. A label count is not a market price; a faster fit is not ROI. Width, availability and decision loss need matched information and actual prices.

Verified customer histories provide a restricted way to learn funding
responses, and the nonlinear servicing study supports one specified policy
comparison. Several causal graphs can still fit the same observations.
Assignment, audit inclusion and label accuracy require substantive evidence.
Joint dependence and high-dimensional learning retain adverse findings, while
local computing results do not establish bank operating performance. Useful
precision and the full financial case depend on the institution and decision.

A bank study would need the relevant decision makers and data owners
to establish assignment rules, observation quality, required precision and
costs. The information requested should be specific to the proposed study.

\section*{Evidence and reading guide}
The five current studies contain 22,528 final requests: 4,608 funding, 5,632 joint dependence and 4,096 each for servicing, corrected graph inference and corrected learning. Another 4,096 earlier learner requests remain exploratory. Complete journals reconstruct saved summaries; 15 first/middle/last representative requests are regenerated. Twenty-five master-control tests pass.

Primary texts support only stated inherited roles. New derivations, fixtures, synthetic outcomes and engineering measurements remain project evidence. Genuine local PDFs, source versions/hashes, inspected anchors and claim limits are recorded in the release audit. Literature coverage retains the 7 October 2026 cutoff; no exhaustive new search is claimed. Process corrections and exact continuation steps are in the companion review.

The selected experiments establish both useful information designs
and adverse findings. They motivate a restricted prototype; they do not
establish performance or financial returns for an adopting bank.

\section*{From research output to a bounded bank decision}
A deployment question must first specify the unit, decision time, available records and loss from a wrong action. The funding construction requires certified randomization and link inclusion, plus independent calendars whose economic shocks do not overlap. If those inputs cannot be supplied, its calibrated synthetic interval is not a substitute for a bank answer. The servicing construction requires a frozen observable policy, truthful representative state audits and the actual historical action probabilities; otherwise the reported fixed-policy value has a different target or can be severely biased.

For discovery, a bank must specify the scientific restrictions that remove observationally equivalent intervention effects. If its accepted restrictions still permit the whole real line, the service should return that set and withhold a directional recommendation. For shared calendars and dependent learning, the present finite failures require a new variance design or stronger information before qualification. A platform may transmit these limitations faithfully, but cannot turn them into positive scientific evidence.

Finally, independent reviewers must reconstruct each claimed regime and bank owners must measure useful precision, decision loss and complete acquisition and operating costs. Only a bounded release meeting those conditions should enter an institutional acceptance and investment decision. An adverse scientific or economic conclusion is a legitimate output of this program.

segments.text:
\chapter{Persistent audit information and finite calendar
uncertainty}\label{persistent-audit-information-and-finite-calendar-uncertainty}}

\label{exec13:persistent-region}

A bank can increase its account count without acquiring an independent
observation of a common calendar shock. It can also add monthly
observations without redrawing a persistent identity audit. These two
limitations affect different parts of funding uncertainty. A useful
analysis must first state the joint observation law, then determine
which uncertainty can be bounded from its actual information.

The construction below is a project derivation for the additive
experiment. It gives a finite-sample confidence set when variance and
persistence bounds are supplied, together with an information
counterexample to a uniform precision claim when persistence is
unrestricted. The exact multiplier moments, covariance references and
numerical illustrations are reproducible project calculations; no new
random evaluation sample or empirical qualification is used.
\citep{exec13_persistent_derivation,exec13_persistent_examples}

\hypertarget{the-observation-law-and-the-banking-target}{%
\section{The observation law and the banking
target}\label{the-observation-law-and-the-banking-target}}

Retain the previously studied independent persistent pairs, common
calendar and separate gold experiment. For pair \(i=1,\ldots,N\) and
date \(t=1,\ldots,T\), the signed focal and companion responses are

\[
 F_{it}=\beta+U_i+C_t+E_{it},\qquad
 D_{it}=\delta+V_i+C_t+J_{it}.
\]

The pair effects \(U_i,V_i\) are mutually independent centered Gaussians
with variance \(v_p\). The cell errors \(E_{it},J_{it}\) are mutually
independent centered Gaussians with variance \(v_e\). The independent
calendar is stationary Gaussian AR(1) with variance \(v_c\), correlation
\(\rho^{|t-s|}\), and \(|\rho|<1\). Candidate order is fixed within a
pair and exogenous. Its sign \(K_i\in\{-1,1\}\) states whether the first
candidate is focal. Randomized observed action signs multiply both
recorded candidate histories; undoing those known signs yields the two
candidate responses \(X_{i1t},X_{i2t}\).

An audit \(R_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), with known constant
\(q>0\), selects a whole pair history. On selected pairs the reported
order is \(L_i=K_i\xi_i\), where \(\xi_i\) has probability \(e<1/2\) of
being \(-1\). The error is symmetric, independent of pair outcomes and
audits, and persistent across dates. An independent representative gold
sample contains \(M\) Bernoulli error indicators with the same \(e\).
Unobserved audit labels remain missing; multiplication by \(R_i\) below
means their contribution is zero without imputing an observed label.
Endogenous selection, asymmetric error, shared pair audits and
nonrepresentative gold labels violate this law.

The target is \(1000\beta\) currency units per focal unit under the
previously studied signed-action response convention. This causal
interpretation is stipulated in the generated experiment; multiplying an
arbitrary bank outcome by an action sign would not establish it. Let
\(b=(\beta+\delta)/2\), \(d=(\beta-\delta)/2\), and \(r=1-2e>0\). Then
\(\beta=b+d\).

The two observed summaries are

\[
 \widehat B=\frac1{NT}\sum_{it}\frac{X_{i1t}+X_{i2t}}2,
 \qquad
 \widehat H=\frac1N\sum_i H_i,
 \quad
 H_i=\frac{R_iL_i}{2qT}\sum_t(X_{i1t}-X_{i2t}).
\]

The common calendar cancels from every candidate difference. Since the
same \(K_i\) appears in the difference and the audited order,
\(K_i^2=1\) removes ordering from \(H_i\). Hence

\[
 H_i=W_i\left(d+\frac{U_i-V_i}{2}
                    +\frac1T\sum_t\frac{E_{it}-J_{it}}2\right),
 \qquad W_i=R_i\xi_i/q,
\]

with \(E W_i=r\) and \(E W_i^2=1/q\). The independent-pair and Gaussian
assumptions give

\[
 E\widehat B=b,\qquad E\widehat H=rd,
\]

\[
 V_B=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat B)
   =\frac{v_p}{2N}+\frac{v_e}{2NT}+v_c k_T(\rho),
 \quad
 k_T(\rho)=\frac{T+2\sum_{k=1}^{T-1}(T-k)\rho^k}{T^2},
\]

\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat H)
 =\frac1N\left\{\frac{v_p}{2q}+\frac{v_e}{2qT}
                       +(q^{-1}-r^2)d^2\right\}.
\]

These formulas do not divide by an estimated rank. The first summary is
Gaussian. The second is a persistent-audit mixture, so a Gaussian
approximation to it is an additional step, not an exact consequence of
Gaussian outcomes. The coefficient of \(d^2\) retains the audit
uncertainty that more dates cannot remove. The variances are nonnegative
under \(q\leq1\) and \(0<r\leq1\).

\hypertarget{a-finite-construction-with-explicit-unknown-nuisance-bounds}{%
\section{A finite construction with explicit unknown-nuisance
bounds}\label{a-finite-construction-with-explicit-unknown-nuisance-bounds}}

Suppose the admissible model supplies finite bounds \(v_p\leq\bar v_p\),
\(v_e\leq\bar v_e\), \(v_c\leq\bar v_c\) and
\(|\rho|\leq\bar\rho\leq1\). The values inside these bounds are unknown.
Taking \(\bar\rho=1\) is allowed as a conservative envelope for the
stationary models, although it sacrifices calendar shrinkage. Since the
lag coefficients in \(k_T\) are positive,

\[
 V_B\leq \bar V_B:=\frac{\bar v_p}{2N}
            +\frac{\bar v_e}{2NT}+\bar v_c k_T(\bar\rho).
\]

Choose error budgets \(\alpha_B,\alpha_H,\alpha_e>0\) whose sum is at
most \(\alpha\). The normal interval

\[
 C_B=[\widehat B-z_{1-\alpha_B/2}\sqrt{\bar V_B},
      \widehat B+z_{1-\alpha_B/2}\sqrt{\bar V_B}]
\]

has coverage at least \(1-\alpha_B\), because \(\widehat B-b\) is normal
with variance no larger than \(\bar V_B\). Degenerate zero variance is
handled by the point interval, not by dividing by zero.

Obtain a two-sided exact binomial interval \(C_e\) by inverting the gold
count \(S\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(M,e)\), allocating \(\alpha_e/2\)
to each tail. For an interior count \(s\), its lower endpoint solves
\(P_{e_L}(S\geq s)=\alpha_e/2\) and its upper endpoint solves
\(P_{e_U}(S\leq s)=\alpha_e/2\), with endpoints zero/one for the
boundary counts. Binomial tail monotonicity shows that excluding the
true \(e\) through either tail has probability at most its allocated
error. Intersect with the model's \([0,1/2)\) to obtain
\(C_r=\{1-2e:e\in C_e\cap[0,1/2)\}\). This intersection preserves
coverage under the model, but can yield ranks arbitrarily close to zero.
It does not justify silently imposing a positive lower rank.

Define the observed-data confidence set

\[
 C=\left\{(b,d,r): b\in C_B,\ r\in C_r,
 (\widehat H-rd)^2\leq
 \frac{\bar v_p/(2q)+\bar v_e/(2qT)+(q^{-1}-r^2)d^2}
      {N\alpha_H}\right\}.
\]

At the true \((d,r)\), Chebyshev's inequality bounds the probability of
violating the displayed quadratic inequality by \(\alpha_H\), using the
variance derived above and its nuisance envelope. This follows directly
by applying Markov's inequality to \((\widehat H-rd)^2\): its
expectation is the variance and is no larger than the numerator divided
by \(N\). No independence between the confidence components is needed.
The union bound therefore proves

\[
 P\{(b,d,r)\in C\}\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 P\{1000\beta\in\mathcal S\}\geq1-\alpha,
 \quad \mathcal S=\{1000(b+d):(b,d,r)\in C\}.
\]

This is a finite-sample statement, uniform over the specified nuisance
envelope and the declared observation law. It estimates the gold-error
rank through a confidence set and bounds unknown calendar/pair/cell
variances; it does not treat those unknown values as known oracle
constants. The construction is feasible in the mathematical sense that
all inputs to the inequalities are observed summaries or declared
bounds. A numerically certified implementation must still project over a
continuum of \(r\); a grid that misses a feasible component would not
inherit the theorem. Analytic quadratic roots or interval outer bounds,
including empty, disconnected and unbounded sets, are suitable
implementation routes. A raw point estimator is optional.

If independent pilot data supply simultaneous upper confidence bounds on
the variances or persistence instead of deterministic bounds, their
joint failure probability must receive an additional budget. Coverage
follows on the event that the bounds are valid, with that event's
failure probability added by the union bound. Independence is not
required for this composition argument, although it can simplify the
pilot proof. Supplying bounds calculated from the same data without a
validity argument would merely move the missing uncertainty problem into
another function.

\hypertarget{why-validity-need-not-produce-a-useful-finite-interval}{%
\section{Why validity need not produce a useful finite
interval}\label{why-validity-need-not-produce-a-useful-finite-interval}}

For fixed candidate rank \(r\), multiply the numerator inequality by
\(\alpha_H\) and collect powers of \(d\). The leading quadratic
coefficient is

\[
 a(r)=r^2(\alpha_H+N^{-1})-(qN)^{-1}.
\]

If \(a(r)<0\), sufficiently large positive and negative \(d\) satisfy
the inequality. If \(a(r)=0\), the inequality is linear or constant and
can produce a half-line, the whole line or an empty set. If \(a(r)>0\),
it gives a bounded interval or an empty set at that rank. A sufficient
uniform condition for bounded numerator projection is that every
feasible rank exceed

\[
 r_{\min}^2>\frac1{q(N\alpha_H+1)}.
\]

Merely checking a positive leading coefficient at the estimated rank is
insufficient when smaller ranks remain in \(C_r\). Even when each
individual rank gives a finite interval, approaching a zero leading
coefficient can make their union unbounded. A strict common margin is
what supplies the useful bound.

For illustration, take the previously studied error probability
\(e=.08\), so \(r=.84\), and allocate \(\alpha_H=.02\). At
\(N=100,q=.4\), the leading coefficient is \(-479/125000\); this
construction has unbounded tails even if the rank were known exactly. At
\(N=320,q=.4\), it is \(17009/2000000>0\) at that rank. With
\(N=100,q=.1\), the threshold exceeds one, so no allowable rank can
supply a positive leading coefficient. Exact rational arithmetic
reproduces these facts. This is a limitation of the conservative
Chebyshev construction, not an impossibility theorem for every sharper
mixture or randomization method. A bounded interval obtained by clipping
its tails would abandon the proved coverage statement.

Calendar uncertainty has a different dimension. With \(\rho=.95\),
stationary calendar standard deviation .6, and \(T=40\), the standard
deviation of the calendar average is about .4494; at \(T=160\) it is
.2776. Increasing \(N\) does not change either number. An assumed
persistence cap may improve a bound, and genuinely independent calendars
may supply new information. Neither benefit follows from creating more
account-date rows within the same calendar.

\hypertarget{an-information-counterexample-for-unrestricted-persistence}{%
\section{An information counterexample for unrestricted
persistence}\label{an-information-counterexample-for-unrestricted-persistence}}

Consider the favorable submodel with exact audits, no pair or cell
noise, and \(\beta=\delta=b\). Every signed focal and companion history
equals the same \(b+C_t\). Thus even infinitely many observed pairs
leave only one Gaussian calendar path. Let the calendar variance
\(v_c=\sigma^2>0\) and correlation \(\rho\) be known in this submodel,
making inference easier than in the intended unknown-nuisance problem.
For \(T\geq2\), the precision matrix of a stationary AR(1) correlation
matrix is tridiagonal. Summing its entries gives the mean information

\[
 I_T=\mathbf1^\top\Sigma_T^{-1}\mathbf1
   =\frac{T(1-\rho)+2\rho}{\sigma^2(1+\rho)}.
\]

The matrix identity is independently checked by exact rational inversion
for small \(T\), and the general formula follows by summing its two
endpoint diagonals, \(T-2\) interior diagonals and \(2(T-1)\)
off-diagonal entries. For fixed \(|\rho|<1\), \(I_T\) grows with \(T\).
But along the admissible stationary sequence \(\rho_T=1-T^{-2}\), it
converges to \(\sigma^{-2}\). Thus no increasing information about the
common mean is guaranteed uniformly over all persistence values below
one.

The limitation is not confined to unbiased estimators. Compare the laws
with means zero and \(\Delta\), the same known covariance, and
\(\Delta=\sigma\). Their total variation distance is

\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_\Delta)
 =2\Phi\left(\frac{|\Delta|\sqrt{I_T}}2\right)-1.
\]

To see this, whiten the two Gaussian laws and project onto their
mean-difference direction. The likelihood-ratio threshold lies halfway
between the two projected means, leaving the stated difference of normal
tail probabilities. Along \(\rho_T\), the distance tends to
\(2\Phi(1/2)-1\simeq.3829\).

For any confidence set \(S_T\) with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) at
both means, the definition of total variation gives

\[
 P_0(\Delta\in S_T)\geq1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_\Delta).
\]

Combining this with \(P_0(0\in S_T)\geq1-\alpha\) shows

\[
 P_0\{\operatorname{diam}(S_T)\geq|\Delta|\}
 \geq1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_\Delta).
\]

At 95\% coverage the lower bound tends to about .5171. An honest
confidence set therefore cannot have uniformly vanishing diameter over
this persistence sequence, even with known covariance and exact
identity. This counterexample does not contradict pointwise asymptotic
normality for a fixed correlation, and it does not prove impossibility
at the previously studied specific fixed value .95. It rules out a
stronger uniform precision promise that lacks a persistence margin or
independent calendar information. In the monetary target, the diameter
scales by 1000 with no additional information gained.

\hypertarget{what-additional-information-would-change-the-decision}{%
\section{What additional information would change the
decision}\label{what-additional-information-would-change-the-decision}}

The finite region separates valid uncertainty from useful precision.
Bounds on unknown variances and persistence supply a model under which
the probability statement is established, but the resulting set can
still be unbounded. For a generated prototype those bounds may be
stipulated and tested as assumptions. For a later bank claim their
scientific origin must be established, or their estimation must receive
its own valid uncertainty budget. A successful calculation cannot
certify them.

The earlier 5,632-request study of the additive pair/calendar/gold law
found finite undercoverage in scarce-information and persistent-calendar
regimes despite favorable balanced-case results. Those fixed findings
motivate this alternative construction; they do not validate it. The
same study's wrong-inclusion, shared-audit and endogenous-label cases
remain outside the law used here. A valid set under independent
symmetric audits cannot be transported to those mechanisms by changing a
covariance estimator. \citep{exec13_persistent_predecessor}

There are three distinct next routes. A conservative region can serve as
a transparent reference in a generated prototype, with exact quadratic
and set-projection checks. A sharper mixture-likelihood or
test-inversion method might retain validity with less conservative
bounds, but it must account for the unknown variances and dependence
parameters. A changed information design can add independently audited
pairs, independent representative gold labels or genuinely independent
calendar clusters. Each addresses a different part of the uncertainty.
More gold labels alone cannot remove a shared-calendar obstruction,
while more dates alone do not make a persistent audit independent.

A prototype should preserve unbounded and disconnected results, measure
the cost of certified projection, and compare these information choices
under the same scientific target. The comparison can initially use
generated mechanisms without costly bank data. A later bank experiment
is justified when its information could narrow a decision-relevant
ambiguity enough to change an action. The present argument supports that
conditional choice; it does not promise a universally precise funding
estimate. The next servicing argument confronts a different information cost: learning action and observation probabilities while preserving the original eligible population. Both constructions budget uncertainty from information that a large row count alone cannot supply. \label{exec13:persistent-region-end}
\hypertarget{servicing-policies-with-estimated-action-and-observation-probabilities}{%

chapters.title:
Servicing policies with estimated action and observation
probabilities

segments.text:
\chapter{Servicing policies with estimated action and observation
probabilities}\label{servicing-policies-with-estimated-action-and-observation-probabilities}}

\label{exec13:servicing-observed}

A servicing team wants to compare an assistance rule with ordinary
collection. Its historical action probabilities may not have been
retained, and some customers disappear from the analytical records
before their next repayment is measured. These are two estimation
problems only after a more basic scientific question has been answered:
did the recorded history include enough information to remove action and
observation selection? A highly accurate model of recorded actions
cannot answer that question on its own.

This chapter develops a restricted route with estimated probabilities, a
policy selected on separate training histories, and an explicit
finite-sample confidence statement. It also constructs two
observationally indistinguishable worlds in which that route answers
different causal questions. The confidence construction and finite
examples are project derivations. The longitudinal treatment/observation
identification principle is inherited from Hernán and Robins; the
importance of independent policy evaluation and cumulative, rather than
current-action, ratios is also explicit in Jiang and Li. Their results
do not themselves prove the composition below.
\citep{hernan2020,jiang2016,exec13_servicing_argument,exec13_servicing_exact}

\hypertarget{the-servicing-information-clock-and-the-eligible-population}{%
\section{The servicing information clock and the eligible
population}\label{the-servicing-information-clock-and-the-eligible-population}}

Fix a finite horizon \(T\). An independently sampled customer has a
complete potential history with pre-action information \(H_t\), binary
assistance \(A_t\), and subsequent net contribution \(R_t\), for
\(t=0,\ldots,T-1\). History contains every recorded past variable used
by the rule or the assignment mechanism, including earlier rewards when
relevant. A finite table, or an explicitly sufficient finite summary,
indexes the probability models. Arbitrary discretization of a continuous
history does not establish sufficiency.

Let \(O_{-1}=1\). Among records still observed at date \(t\), the bank
first records \(H_t\), then selects \(A_t\), then the observation
indicator \(C_t\) determines whether the following reward and next
history are recorded. Set \(O_t=O_{t-1}C_t\). Dropout is absorbing. Thus
\(C_t=1\) denotes retention here, the opposite coding from a
conventional censoring indicator. Define

\[
\begin{aligned}
 e_t(a\mid h)&=\Pr(A_t=a\mid H_t=h,O_{t-1}=1),\\
 g_t(h,a)&=\Pr(C_t=1\mid H_t=h,A_t=a,O_{t-1}=1).
\end{aligned}
\]

The stipulated observation law has four substantive restrictions. First,
consistency connects the recorded actions to the defined assistance
intervention. Second, conditional on \(H_t\), action selection is
independent of subsequent potential histories under the candidate
policies. Third, conditional on \(H_t,A_t\), retention is independent of
the subsequent complete history; dropout merely hides records and does
not change repayment. Fourth, all histories reachable under the
candidate policies satisfy known floors \(e_t(a\mid h)\ge c_e>0\) for
both actions and \(g_t(h,a)\ge c_g>0\), with \(c_e\le1/2\). Infeasible
actions must instead be removed from both the declared policy class and
the support requirement.

The independent sampling unit is the whole customer history. Dependence
within that history is allowed. Independent training and evaluation
cohorts follow the same complete-history, assignment and observation
law. Distinct customer identifiers do not guarantee this condition when
common calendar shocks, household links or shared staff information
remain. The construction does not qualify those sampling regimes.

The target is

\[
 V(\pi)=\mathbb E_\pi\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} R_t\right],
 \qquad |R_t|\le B_t,
\]

per original eligible customer, with known finite \(B_t\). Discounting
and a bounded terminal account can be included in the dated rewards. A
sale, default or account closure that changes the economic outcome is
not automatically analytical dropout. Treating it as missing information
would change the target. The present example assigns neither a currency
value to customer welfare nor a bank-specific loss threshold.

\hypertarget{identification-with-action-and-retention-prefixes}{%
\section{Identification with action and retention
prefixes}\label{identification-with-action-and-retention-prefixes}}

For a history-based policy \(\pi_t(a\mid h)\), define

\[
 W_t^\pi=\prod_{s=0}^{t}
 \frac{\pi_s(A_s\mid H_s)}{e_s(A_s\mid H_s)}
 \frac{C_s}{g_s(H_s,A_s)}.
\]

An observed score stops at dropout; its subsequent contributions are
zero, without accessing unrecorded histories or evaluating undefined
denominators. Under the stated restrictions,

\[
 V(\pi)=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb E[W_t^\pi R_t].
\]

To verify the identity, factor a retained prefix into its
initial-history law, action probabilities, retention probabilities and
transition/reward kernels. Multiplication by the weight cancels each
action and retention factor and replaces each action factor with the
target policy. Sequential exchangeability and the observation
restriction make the remaining transition/reward kernels those of the
complete intervention law. Summing that prefix gives
\(\mathbb E_\pi R_t\). The observation factor for date \(t\) is required
because dropout occurs before that reward is recorded. Weighting only by
the current action leaves the incoming history distributed under
historical practice.

This argument uses the entire history law and does not require a Markov
state. A Markov reduction is an additional restriction that must be
checked in the selected construction. Nor does fitting \(e_t\) supply
the exchangeability premise: the observed conditional probability exists
even in a confounded world.

\hypertarget{a-finite-table-permits-an-explicit-probability-error-budget}{%
\section{A finite table permits an explicit probability error
budget}\label{a-finite-table-permits-an-explicit-probability-error-budget}}

Use \(m\) independent training histories to fit action and retention
probabilities. The same training set may select the policy; the
evaluation sample is independent of every such selection. Before
training, fix all \(J\) Bernoulli table cells: an action-one cell for
each relevant time/history and a retention cell for each relevant
time/history/action. Estimate each probability by its observed fraction,
conditional on reaching that cell. A customer contributes at most one
observation to a given dated cell.

Let \(N_j\) be that cell's training count and allocate total nuisance
failure probability \(\alpha_N\). For \(N_j>0\), put

\[
 \epsilon_j=\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{\log(2J/\alpha_N)}{2N_j}}\right\}.
\]

For an empty cell choose any fixed estimate and set \(\epsilon_j=1\).
Conditional on the membership indicators for one cell, its observed
outcomes are independent Bernoulli variables with that cell's fixed
probability. Hoeffding's inequality gives failure probability at most
\(\alpha_N/J\); averaging over its random count preserves the bound.
Different cells can be dependent because customers visit several times:
a union bound, not cell independence, gives simultaneous error control
at least \(1-\alpha_N\).

For completeness, the concentration step follows from the
bounded-variable exponential-moment bound
\(\mathbb E e^{\lambda(X-\mathbb EX)}\le e^{\lambda^2/8}\) for
\(0\le X\le1\). Independence, exponential Markov inequality, and
optimization at \(\lambda=4x\) give \(\Pr(|\bar X-p|>x)\le2e^{-2Nx^2}\).
The bound follows by convexity of the exponential and bounding the
second derivative of the log Bernoulli moment-generating function by
\(1/4\).

Project each action-one estimate onto \([c_e,1-c_e]\) and obtain the
action-zero estimate by complement. Project retention onto \([c_g,1]\).
Projection cannot increase error when the true probability is in the
interval. It does not turn an unverified support floor into a scientific
fact. Let \(\epsilon_{e,t}\) and \(\epsilon_{g,t}\) be the largest
corresponding cell radii at time \(t\). On the simultaneous event,

\[
 \left|\frac{e_t}{\widehat e_t}-1\right|
 \le\frac{\epsilon_{e,t}}{c_e},\qquad
 \left|\frac{g_t}{\widehat g_t}-1\right|
 \le\frac{\epsilon_{g,t}}{c_g}.
\]

These statements hold for every policy measurable with respect to
training, including a rule selected using the same estimated
probabilities. There is no independence requirement between the policy
and those fits. Adaptive table construction, future-driven history
definitions and pooled time cells without a stationarity assumption are
excluded from this proof.

\hypertarget{propagating-fitted-probabilities-into-a-valid-interval}{%
\section{Propagating fitted probabilities into a valid
interval}\label{propagating-fitted-probabilities-into-a-valid-interval}}

For the frozen training-selected rule, use the fitted denominators in
the prefix score \(Y_i^\pi=\sum_t\widehat W_{it}^\pi R_{it}\), and
average it over \(n\) evaluation histories. Conditional on training,
cancellation of the true observed law gives

\[
 \mathbb E[Y_i^\pi\mid D_{\rm train}]
 =\sum_t\mathbb E_\pi\left[R_t
 \prod_{s=0}^t\frac{e_sg_s}{\widehat e_s\widehat g_s}\right].
\]

For nonnegative factors \(r_k\) with \(|r_k-1|\le d_k\), telescoping the
product gives \(|\prod_k r_k-1|\le\prod_k(1+d_k)-1\). This remains valid
when a lower bound \(1-d_k\) is negative. Therefore the conditional bias
is at most

\[
 D=\sum_t B_t\left[
 \prod_{s=0}^t
 \left(1+\frac{\epsilon_{e,s}}{c_e}\right)
 \left(1+\frac{\epsilon_{g,s}}{c_g}\right)-1\right].
\]

Independently of the nuisance event, each evaluation score lies in
\([-M,M]\), where

\[
 M=\sum_t B_t(c_ec_g)^{-(t+1)}.
\]

Applying the same bounded-variable argument after rescaling this range,
the radius

\[
 r_E=M\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\alpha_E)}{n}}
\]

bounds evaluation error with probability at least \(1-\alpha_E\),
conditional on any training sample. Consequently

\[
 I_\pi=[\bar Y^\pi-D-r_E,\ \bar Y^\pi+D+r_E]
 \cap[-B_\Sigma,B_\Sigma],\qquad B_\Sigma=\sum_t B_t,
\]

covers \(V(\pi_{D_{\rm train}})\) with unconditional probability at
least \(1-\alpha_N-\alpha_E\). This is a confidence statement about the
value of the realized trained policy. It is not the value of an unknown
optimal policy or the expectation of a policy-learning algorithm over
fresh training sets. Conditional coverage over evaluation is controlled
on the nuisance event; arbitrary bad training samples do not acquire a
conditional guarantee.

An empty intersection must be reported as an incompatible result, not
replaced by a point or silently dropped. For known action or retention
laws set their radii to zero and use their actual lower bounds. The
conservative total interval remains valid with estimated laws; an
evaluation-only normal standard error generally ignores the training
bias when both sample sizes are comparable.

For fixed \(J,T,c_e,c_g\), suppose each training cell has probability at
least \(p_{\min}>0\) of being reached. A multiplicative binomial bound
yields \(\Pr(\min_j N_j<mp_{\min}/2)\le J e^{-mp_{\min}/8}\). On its
complement, \(\max_j\epsilon_j\le\sqrt{\log(2J/\alpha_N)/(mp_{\min})}\).
Expanding the finite product shows
\(D=O(\sqrt{\log(J/\alpha_N)/(mp_{\min})})\), with constants depending
on horizon and support floors; \(r_E=O(n^{-1/2})\). Thus both
uncertainty terms can shrink in this finite class. Rare histories, a
growing horizon or a growing table can destroy useful precision. No
arbitrary-learner or continuous-history rate follows.

\hypertarget{policy-comparisons-preserve-the-selection-target}{%
\section{Policy comparisons preserve the selection
target}\label{policy-comparisons-preserve-the-selection-target}}

For \(K\) prespecified policies, or \(K\) rules constructed only from
training, replace \(\alpha_E\) by \(\alpha_E/K\). The nuisance event
already covers all their table cells. This gives simultaneous intervals
\([L_k,U_k]\), intersected with the value range, without asserting
independence between policy scores on the same customers.

The finite-class best value lies in \([\max_k L_k,\max_k U_k]\). If the
selected rule is member \(j\), its finite-class regret lies in

\[
 \left[\max\{0,\max_k L_k-U_j\},\ \max_k U_k-L_j\right].
\]

If any component interval is empty the family result is flagged
incompatible. Simultaneous coverage allows selecting a member after
inspecting these intervals, provided every candidate was fixed before
evaluation and all were covered. Adding candidates after viewing
evaluation outcomes needs a new argument. For an individual paired
contrast, one may instead bound the paired score and its nuisance error
directly; treating separately fitted values as independent loses their
covariance. Neither approach turns a finite candidate class into
unrestricted policy optimization.

\hypertarget{exact-small-references-and-the-cost-of-conservatism}{%
\section{Exact small references and the cost of
conservatism}\label{exact-small-references-and-the-cost-of-conservatism}}

A two-decision example uses observed stress \(S_t\in\{0,1\}\), with
initial probability \(1/2\). Historical assistance has probability
\(.3+.4S_t\). Next stress has probability \(.2+.5S_t-.15A_t\), retention
probability is \(.9-.1S_t-.1A_t\), and dated contribution is
\(2-3S_{t+1}-.25A_t\). These are hypothetical utility units; their
coefficient signs express an assistance cost and an improvement in
future stress. Every path probability is rational. Retention uses a draw
independent of the next stress innovation given current state and
action.

No assistance, always assist, and assist only when stressed form a fixed
finite policy class. Exhaustive path sums under interventions are
compared with a separate backward value recursion. Summation over
observed prefixes reproduces the same values with true denominators.
Perturbing action-one probabilities by \(+.04\) and retention
probabilities by \(-.03\) verifies the fitted-law bias expression and
its conservative envelope. A deliberately incorrect
current-action/retention shortcut is kept as a negative reference. The
program enumerates all paths; it draws no final evaluation sample and
measures no empirical coverage. \citep{exec13_servicing_exact}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lrr@{}}
\toprule
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.25\columnwidth}\raggedright
Policy\strut
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{0.33\columnwidth}\raggedleft
Exact intervention value\strut
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{0.33\columnwidth}\raggedleft

\end{minipage}\tabularnewline
\midrule
\endhead
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.25\columnwidth}\raggedright
No assistance\strut
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[t]{0.33\columnwidth}\raggedleft

\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[t]{0.33\columnwidth}\raggedleft
+.21997\strut
