linkage, label and audit truth. Reviewing a source dictionary may prevent a
semantic error; it does not supply sampled identity labels or independent
calendars. The cost of obtaining those scientific inputs belongs in the
information budget, and their absence remains a legitimate stop condition for
an effect calculation.

\section{A complete cost model}

For request $i$, a prospective accounting identity is
\[
 C_i=C_{i,\mathrm{model}}+C_{i,\mathrm{retrieval}}+
     C_{i,\mathrm{numeric}}+C_{i,\mathrm{review}}+
     C_{i,\mathrm{data}}+C_{i,\mathrm{operation}}.
\]
The terms represent distinct resource uses, not independently measured values
in the current project. Model cost includes all calls and retries. Retrieval
includes acquisition and any permitted indexing. Numerical cost includes the
complete fit, uncertainty calculation and serialization. Review includes time
spent on wrong, refused and unsupported answers. Data cost includes audits and
additional information. Operations include storage, recovery and support.

A natural-workflow comparison measures the quality and cost of complete
workflows. A matched-budget comparison holds selected resources fixed to study
one contribution. The two can produce different rankings without contradiction.
An agent that improves answers by using more expert review may be valuable,
but the result is about the combined workflow. It does not isolate autonomous
reasoning quality.

The experimental unit must also match the cost and outcome calculation.
Repeated prompts about one mechanism are correlated observations within that
mechanism. Counting them as independent bank decisions understates uncertainty
and can exaggerate the amount of evidence. Error bars for incremental value
should use the prespecified mechanism or decision clusters and retain the
paired comparison wherever both workflows face the same problem.

\section{What can be concluded before a live evaluation}

The local controller demonstrates preservation of declarations, alternatives,
refusals and numerical set topology in selected authored examples. It makes
zero live model calls. Its measured interface behavior cannot reveal a
provider's accuracy, token use, price or review burden on unfamiliar questions.
Those fields remain unavailable rather than being filled with zeros.

Published benchmarks support the design of a prospective evaluation. They
cannot be combined across different model revisions, task distributions and
information budgets into a bank ROI estimate. CausalDS in particular reports
divergence between symbolic success, interval quality, abstention and cost,
which supports measuring them separately~\citep{v12_la_2607_08093}.

The next empirical step requires a specified backend and custody arrangement,
actual prices and budget, independent held-out mechanisms, adjudicators and
qualified numerical baselines. For bank adoption it additionally requires
feasible actions, authentic records and accepted loss thresholds. Until those
inputs exist, exact decision examples can check the accounting and expose
threshold errors. They cannot establish that assistance crosses an institutional
investment threshold. The following cost calculation makes the review and error-loss tradeoff explicit, before the selective-automation examples show why cost and quality must be evaluated over every requested decision.

\hypertarget{full-cost-and-the-investment-threshold}{%
\section{Full cost and the investment
threshold}\label{full-cost-and-the-investment-threshold}}

\label{exec14:cost-development}

Cost is an accounting identity before it is a performance result. For
request \(i\), retain input, output and cache tokens with their actual
dated prices; numerical compute; retrieval and storage; tool retries;
analyst review and rework; escalation; and any failed-run charges. Add
fixed integration, security and maintenance costs separately. Unmeasured
components remain missing. Token counts alone cannot establish either
dollar savings or cost per usable causal decision.

An explicitly illustrative price scenario makes the arithmetic concrete.
An ordinary review takes 30 minutes at USD 60/hour plus USD 1 compute,
for USD 31/request. Assisted review takes 10 minutes at the same rate,
USD 2 tools, 30,000 input tokens at USD 2/million and 5,000 output
tokens at USD 8/million, USD 0.20 retrieval and USD 0.20 expected retry
charges. The assumed token cost is USD 0.10. If 20\% of requests
additionally require a 30-minute escalation, expected escalation cost is
USD 6 and total assisted cost is USD 18.50. These prices, times and
escalation frequencies are scenario assumptions, not provider quotations
or measured productivity.

The resulting variable saving is USD 12.50/request before incremental
error losses and fixed costs. With USD 12,500 fixed cost, 1,000 requests
reach arithmetic break-even only if all those assumptions hold and
decision quality is otherwise unchanged. If the assisted method
increases a USD 10,000-loss error by 0.1 percentage points per request,
the added expected loss is USD 10 and net saving falls to USD 2.50,
requiring 5,000 requests to recover the same fixed cost. At a 0.2
percentage-point increase, variable net value is already negative. With
all other inputs fixed and no added error loss, escalation probability
must be below \(37/60\approx61.67\%\) for positive variable savings.
These sensitivities explain why an inexpensive-looking model call is not
a business case. \citep{exec14_evaluation_oracle}

The prospective analysis should compare paired decision loss plus cost
per requested case, as well as cost per valid result. The latter ratio
needs its numerator and denominator reported; selective refusal can
improve the ratio while reducing service. In bank data the relevant
error loss may be unknown, so the proposal can report break-even
surfaces and identify which uncertainty a prototype should resolve. It
must not assign invented observed losses to satisfy an ROI gate.

\hypertarget{a-study-that-can-be-registered-after-a-prototype}{%
\subsection{A study that can be registered after a
prototype}\label{a-study-that-can-be-registered-after-a-prototype}}

The proposed evaluation protocol is a reviewed prospective design, not a
registered or executed study. Its 400 mechanisms, four label/evidence
conditions and three repetitions are a planning allocation. They would
generate 4,800 requests per workflow arm, but the independent unit is
the mechanism and repetitions/conditions are nested. For a single
Bernoulli proportion, 400 independent observations give an approximate
worst-case 95\% normal half-width of 0.049. For a paired difference
bounded in \([-1,1]\), the worst-case normal half-width can be 0.098. An
elementary distribution-free bounded-mean calculation at half-width 0.05
and failure probability 0.05 requires at least 2,952 independent
mechanisms. To see this, the second derivative of the log
moment-generating function of a variable in \([-1,1]\) is a tilted
variance at most one. Integrating twice gives
\(\log E\exp\{\lambda(D-ED)\}\leq\lambda^2/2\). Independence and the
exponential Markov inequality then give
\(P(|\bar D-E\bar D|\geq\epsilon)\leq2\exp(-n\epsilon^2/2)\). Solving
for \(n\) yields the stated conservative count. This calculation does
not choose a final sample size or justify normal inference in every
stratum. \citep{exec14_evaluation_oracle}

First use public, development-only examples to measure feasibility and
costs for a numerical baseline, an ordinary analyst workflow, a single
assistant, retrieval assistance and a hybrid numerical assistant. Add
debate only as a separate ablation. Cross unfamiliar labels with
held-out mechanism families, misleading retrieval, clock violations,
proxy measurement and nonidentification. Keep an equal-information
comparison separate from an equal-resource comparison; a system
receiving a scientific source or more numerical fitting has a different
information or compute budget. For a human study, assign cases and
workflow order to avoid the learning/selection confounding illustrated
by CausalChat, and include review, adjudication and rework time.

Use the development pilot to choose decision-relevant tolerances,
feasible budgets and a justified final allocation. Before a final run,
bind provider/model revision, actual settings, package/container
identities, independent holdout and truth, retrieval corpus, human
adjudication protocol, prices, stopping rules and the analysis script.
Freeze paired mechanism-level analyses and the multiplicity policy.
Retain every planned attempt, including malformed, unsupported,
timed-out and unavailable requests. Quality thresholds concern
target/clock errors, unjustified causal claims, calibration where
eligible, justified refusal, decision loss and full cost; a single
composite score cannot establish all of them. These are future
prototype/experiment inputs, not reasons to block this
literature-and-design proposal.

The immediate investment is a narrow prototype using public data and
stipulated mechanisms. Its purpose is to resolve target errors,
unsupported assumptions, tool failures and review burden before an
expensive bank experiment. Hidden evaluation, actual prices,
bank-specific loss and institutional review remain later inputs; the
proposal does not invent their outcomes.

\label{exec14:cost-development-end}

\section{Selective automation must be valued over requested decisions}
\label{exec14:l8-development}

An assisted workflow chooses both an answer and whether to act on it. These
choices change the population on which accuracy is reported. Let $R_i=1$ mean
that request $i$ receives an automated recommendation and $R_i=0$ mean that it
is referred to a fallback. Let $a_i$ and $b_i$ denote the respective actions,
$\theta_i$ the decision-relevant state, and $\ell(a,\theta)$ the loss relative
to an explicitly specified feasible comparator. If $C_i$ includes all work
before referral, $H_i$ the additional fallback cost and $D_i$ the loss caused
by delay, a complete per-request accounting variable is
\[
 Z_i=C_i+R_i\ell(a_i,\theta_i)
       +(1-R_i)\{H_i+D_i+\ell(b_i,\theta_i)\}.
\]
Loss is monetary here only because the example stipulates a monetary mapping.
Legal feasibility, access to assistance and other constraints can instead
restrict the allowed actions; they should not be silently converted into an
invented dollar penalty. A comparison estimates the change in $Z_i$ over the
same requested population, including requests on which either workflow fails.
An unanswered request has a subsequent action or an unresolved consequence,
not a disappearing row. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

Consider 100 generated offer decisions: 80 with a USD~100 loss for a wrong
action and 20 with a USD~10,000 loss. Workflow A answers all 80 low-consequence
requests and ten high-consequence requests. It makes one error in each group.
Workflow B answers 60 low-consequence and ten high-consequence requests, making
three errors in the first group and none in the second. A's conditional answer
accuracy is $88/90$, higher than B's $67/70$. These are invented counts that
define the example, not estimates of either a model or a bank's error rate.

Assume A costs USD~2 and B costs USD~4 for every requested decision. Each
referral costs another USD~40 and resolves the action correctly in this
particular construction. Delay costs USD~5 for a low-consequence referral and
USD~50 for a high-consequence referral. The full accounting is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z_A^{\mathrm{total}}&=200+10{,}100+400+500=11{,}200,\\
 Z_B^{\mathrm{total}}&=400+300+1{,}200+600=2{,}500.
 \end{aligned}
\]
B is less accurate among its answers and automates fewer requests, yet has
USD~8,700 less total loss and cost in the constructed portfolio. The fallback
is assumed correct, so these totals are optimistic about review; allowing
review errors adds their losses through the same equation. Equally, the
construction does not imply that more referral is always better. Raising its
cost, delay or error rate can reverse the result. The point is that automation
coverage and conditional accuracy do not determine economic value even when
both have been measured correctly. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

The review decision can be made explicit. Suppose an unreviewed recommendation
has error probability $q$, a reviewed recommendation has probability $r$, an
error loses $L$, and review plus delay costs $c$. Under this binary-loss model,
review improves expected value precisely when
\[
 (q-r)L>c.
\]
For stipulated $q=.01$, $r=.002$ and $c=20$, the loss threshold is USD~2,500.
Reviewing a USD~100-consequence decision has net value minus USD~19.20;
reviewing a USD~10,000-consequence decision has net value USD~60. The same
apparent confidence therefore supports different review choices. A language
model's stated confidence does not supply $q$, and agreement between model
and reviewer does not identify $r$. These probabilities concern correctness
conditional on the target population and routing rule; they require suitable
labels and a separately reviewed evaluation. If review can introduce errors,
$r$ may exceed $q$. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

CausalChat supplies a reason to study the presentation and review components
together. Its six-student study reports mean edge-editing times of 3.3 minutes
with LLM text and 0.9 minutes with CausalChat Lite. The study used a fixed
sequence of stages and participants chose which edges to resolve. The paper
also reports concerns about missing citations and the reliability of scientific
support. Those observations motivate a banking comparison of review burden,
target errors and evidence inspection. They do not identify a transferable
productivity effect or justify multiplying 2.4 minutes by a bank salary and
calling the result a saving. A prospective comparison should control task
difficulty, learning and reviewer allocation, while preserving the time spent
on consequential mistakes and unresolved cases. \citep{v12_la_2410_14146}

\section{Retry and fallback costs depend on the failure mechanism}
\label{exec14:l8-retry}

Agent workflows often retry after malformed output, unavailable tools or a
failed scientific check. Let $T$ be the first attempt that passes a specified
check and let $m$ be a fixed attempt cap. The number of attempted calls is
$N=\min(T,m)$, with $T>m$ when none passes. For integer $N$,
$N=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbf1\{N\geq j\}$, giving
\[
 \mathbb E N=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\Pr(T\geq j).
\]
This identity needs no independence assumption. With an identical per-attempt
cost $c$ and terminal fallback charge $F$, expected execution cost is
$c\mathbb E N+F\Pr(T>m)$. Attempt-specific review and transfer costs can be
included inside the corresponding indicators. Passing an operational check
is still separate from answering the causal question correctly; a protocol
that detects only malformed JSON needs an additional scientific-error term.
\citep{exec14_l8_economics}

Two stipulated mechanisms have the same 20\% first-attempt failure rate.
In the first, failures are independent with probability $1/5$. At $m=3$,
\[
 \mathbb E N=1+\tfrac15+\tfrac1{25}=\tfrac{31}{25},
 \qquad \Pr(T>3)=\tfrac1{125}.
\]
In the second, one tenth of requests have a permanent defect. Other requests
have independent transient failure probability $1/9$ per attempt. For $k\geq1$,
the probability that the first $k$ attempts all fail is
\[
 \tfrac1{10}+\tfrac9{10}\left(\tfrac19\right)^k.
\]
The first-attempt failure rate is again $1/5$, but
$\mathbb E N=1+1/5+1/9=59/45$ and the terminal failure probability is
$41/405$, approximately 10.12\%. At USD~2 per attempt and USD~50 for the
terminal fallback, expected costs are USD~2.88 and approximately USD~7.68.
Full enumeration of permanent status and all three transient outcomes gives
the same values as the tail-sum calculation. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

A missing identification method, inconsistent units, inaccessible evidence or
an ambiguous causal target can behave like the permanent component. A new
prompt does not necessarily change the missing information. Independent
retry arithmetic would substantially understate terminal workload in that
case. The proposed agent should classify the failure, retain the failed
request and route to an appropriate remedy: repair a format, select a supported
method, seek evidence or return an unresolved decision. A retry budget limits
spending; it does not establish that repeated reasoning supplies independent
evidence. The classification itself should be checked because a mistaken
``transient'' label can generate costly repetition.

CausalDS reports marked differences in tool-use strategy and total tokens,
alongside tool-output-management failures and distinct content and abstention
outcomes. Its reported ATE interval coverage uses only seven eligible cases
per model, or five for one model, in that particular exam. These scoped results
support retaining trajectories and component outcomes. They do not supply the
permanent-failure fraction of a banking workflow, and total tokens do not
determine dollars without dated input/output/cache prices and the relevant
billing rules. The prototype should measure the actual sequence of attempts,
which input changed between them, and the eventual fallback. No named service
price or bank runtime is assumed here. \citep{v12_la_2607_08093}

\section{Causal ambiguity needs a declared decision rule}
\label{exec14:l8-ambiguity}

The funding example in Section~\ref{exec13:funding-journey} maps a supplied
response set through a stated profit function and obtains net values from
minus USD~625 to plus USD~1,625. Holding the rate fixed has zero incremental
value in that example. To examine the decision rule, temporarily treat those
endpoints as a declared ambiguity set containing the true state; this is a
conditional decision construction. If the set came from a confidence procedure,
its coverage uncertainty remains an additional issue. It is not a posterior
probability law over the possible profits.

A robust net-value rule holds because the worst net value from acting is
negative. A deterministic minimax-regret rule acts. To see the difference,
define regret in state $\theta$ as
\[
 \mathcal R(a,\theta)=\max_{b\in\{\mathrm{hold},\mathrm{act}\}}
          V(b,\theta)-V(a,\theta).
\]
Acting has worst regret USD~625, whereas holding has worst regret USD~1,625.
Robust value protects the attained payoff; minimax regret protects the shortfall
relative to what could have been chosen with state knowledge. Neither rule is
deduced from the graph or interval alone. They express different preferences
for the same scientifically unresolved funding question.

If randomizing the entire action were an admissible policy, choose action with
probability $p$. Expected regret within the adverse and favorable states is
$625p$ and $1625(1-p)$. Their maximum is minimized at
\[
 p=\frac{1625}{625+1625}=\frac{13}{18},
 \qquad \mathcal R_{\max}=\frac{8125}{18}\approx451.39.
\]
This is a randomized decision across instances, not permission to replace the
rate change by $13/18$ of its size. The latter needs a response model for the
new intervention. A bank may prohibit randomized treasury actions, so the
deterministic analysis can remain the relevant one. An assistant should explain
which criterion generated a recommendation and preserve the alternatives.
It should never silently convert an interval midpoint into a uniquely justified
choice. \citep{exec14_l8_economics,exec13_funding_exact}

Sequential servicing adds a second information requirement: the joint values
of the feasible policies. Suppose two generated worlds give net policy values
$(V_A,V_B)=(-100,-200)$ and $(100,0)$. Policy A exceeds B by USD~100 in both
worlds. Separate coordinate projections give $V_A\in[-100,100]$ and
$V_B\in[-200,0]$, whose unrestricted difference spans $[-300,100]$. That
box suggests a possible advantage for B by combining coordinates from
incompatible worlds. It is a conservative enlargement, but it can conceal a
strict policy ranking. A useful policy interface should preserve the joint
world or region identity where available and state when only coordinate
bounds have been computed. An LLM can explain this distinction; it cannot
recover lost joint information from two displayed intervals.
\citep{exec14_l8_economics}

For discovery, the information purchase should concern an unresolved feature
that can change an action, such as a consequential orientation or an admissible
intervention regime. Improving unrelated edges may have no value for the
specified offer. For observation construction, the consequential distinction
may instead be the origin map, inclusion design or label law. A timestamp
audit can be useful while leaving those questions untouched. The four journeys
therefore share an accounting language but require different information.
Their proposed acceptance cases keep unsupported estimators, equal-law
counterexamples and unresolved scientific premises visible.
\citep{exec14_l8_design}

\section{A public prototype buys an option to make a later investment}
\label{exec14:l8-option}

A proposal need not know bank ROI before it can justify a small prototype.
It does need an account of which later decision the prototype could change.
Let $G$ be the eventual net value of constructing a selected capability, after
all subsequent implementation and operating costs in a declared horizon.
The choice today is to build or decline. A pilot supplies a signal $S$, costs
$K$ today and delays the later value by a discount factor $d\in(0,1]$.
Under an explicitly stipulated joint probability model, the two option values
are
\[
 W_0=\max\{0,\mathbb E G\},\qquad
 W_{\mathrm{pilot}}=-K+d\,\mathbb E[\max\{0,\mathbb E(G\mid S)\}].
\]
The maximum inside the expectation represents the option to decline after
an unfavorable signal. It must correspond to a feasible stop decision: costs
already committed before the signal cannot be removed by a retrospective
choice. Pilot cost is excluded from $G$ because it is subtracted separately.
The law of $S$ describes how the prototype informs the commercial and scientific
state; a benchmark score is not automatically such a signal.
\citep{exec14_l8_economics}

For an exact planning example, let $G$ be USD~100,000 or minus USD~60,000 with
equal probability. Immediate construction has expected net value USD~20,000.
Stipulate a pilot signal with sensitivity and specificity both $4/5$. Positive
and negative signals each occur with probability $1/2$. Conditional expected
construction values are USD~68,000 and minus USD~28,000, so the pilot policy
builds only after a positive signal. Expected value before pilot cost and delay
is USD~34,000. This also follows directly from
\[
 \tfrac12\tfrac45(100{,}000)
       +\tfrac12\tfrac15(-60{,}000)=34{,}000,
\]
which keeps the loss from an unfavorable state with a positive signal explicit.
At $K=10{,}000$ and $d=.9$, the pilot option is worth USD~20,600: only USD~600
more than immediate construction. Without delay it is worth USD~24,000.
Comparing the USD~34,000 gross value with a zero baseline would incorrectly
discard the already available USD~20,000 construction option.
\citep{exec14_l8_economics}

The example gives testable planning thresholds instead of a declared ROI.
At signal quality $4/5$, the pilot is weakly preferred to immediate construction exactly when
$d\geq15/17$. With $d=.9$ and symmetric signal quality $s$ in the regime
$s>5/8$, where the negative signal leads to declining construction, the gross
option value is $80{,}000s-30{,}000$. The break-even quality is
\[
 s\geq \frac{30{,}000+(20{,}000+K)/d}{80{,}000}
       =\frac{19}{24}\approx.7917.
\]
At lower quality the correct action after each signal must be recalculated;
the displayed branch cannot be extrapolated through a change of optimal action.
Perfect information would have gross value USD~50,000, an incremental
USD~30,000 over immediate construction before costs and delay. No imperfect
signal about this same fixed state and action set exceeds that perfect-information
value, because conditional maximization cannot outperform choosing with the
state observed. This comparison says nothing about pilots that themselves
create new feasible capabilities, which require a different model.
\citep{exec14_l8_economics}

For the causal proposal, the first signal should come from a bounded public or
generated prototype: can a selected adapter preserve the target; can it refuse
an unidentified request; does a proposed uncertainty method have useful width
under its declared law; and how much review and recovery does the complete
workflow require? These outcomes can change a construction decision without
claiming bank validation. A later authentic experiment becomes justified when
its expected information can resolve a consequential uncertainty that the
prototype cannot. The staged decision should include delay and the ability to
stop, as well as favorable technical results. \citep{exec14_l8_design}

\section{Transferring workflow value requires the deployment mixture}
\label{exec14:l8-transfer}

Even if a prototype measured paired workflow value exactly on its own cases,
the average need not transport to the requested bank population. Write
$\Delta_j$ for the incremental saving, after errors and full costs, in stratum
$j$, and $w_j$ for the deployment proportion. Under the strong assumption that
within-stratum values transport, deployment value is
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{deploy}}=\sum_j w_j\Delta_j.
\]
This assumption includes task difficulty, information availability, feasible
actions, review and losses within each stratum. Matching a topic name alone
does not establish it. If the weights are unknown but constrained to a set
$\mathcal W$, the corresponding value set is the range of the displayed linear
function over $\mathcal W$. Its extrema can be computed without inventing a
single deployment average. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

Suppose the workflow saves USD~10 on a routine case and loses USD~30 on a
difficult case, with all components stipulated. If $w$ is the difficult-case
fraction, incremental value is $10-40w$ dollars per requested case. A public
development collection with $w=1/5$ has a USD~2 advantage, while a deployment
mix with $w=3/5$ has a USD~14 disadvantage. The threshold is $w=1/4$. Knowing
only that $w\in[.1,.4]$ gives a value range from minus USD~6 to plus USD~6.
Neither a public positive result nor uncertainty about the target mixture
justifies choosing its favorable endpoint. Selection by the assistant can
change the mix again; the routing policy and fallback outcomes must be part
of the transported object. \citep{exec14_l8_economics}

This is especially relevant when business translation is the proposed benefit.
A public dataset with clean treatment and outcome names can test numerical
orchestration yet supply little information about ambiguous requests, changing
population definitions or delayed records. A difficult-case stratum should be
defined by the causal task and information obstacle, not merely by a model's
low confidence. Language assistance can suggest the strata and identify missing
fields, but their prevalence and consequences need separate evidence. Feng
et al.'s reliability study restricts its accessible-corpus analysis and notes
its largely commonsense setting; it does not provide an error law for all
closed models or complex dynamic banking problems. That limitation supports
explicit transport assumptions, not an extrapolated bank failure rate.
\citep{v12_la_2407_19638}

Prices also need a transport argument. A prototype's observed analyst minutes
are resource use; converting them into savings requires a decision about
reassigned capacity, wage overhead and whether staffing expenditure changes.
Compute cost can have minimum charges, cached inputs, reserved capacity or
shared infrastructure. A model with lower variable cost can require more
adjudication or a larger fixed integration. For annual requested volume $n$,
eligible-use fraction $u$, per-used-request incremental value $v$ and additional
fixed cost $F$, the elementary no-discount scenario is $nuv-F$. Both $u$ and
$v$ can change with expansion, and $v$ already includes the fallback and loss
terms. A cost-per-answer claim should therefore be accompanied by the requested
denominator and resource totals. This proposal supplies the accounting and
break-even questions; actual deployment weights, prices and accepted values
are prospective measurements. \citep{exec14_l8_design}

\section{What each banking case still needs to justify further work}
\label{exec14:l8-research}

Funding has a concrete immediate prototype route: connect a selected summary
estimator to joint nuisance and dependence accounting, preserve the complete
response set, and propagate it through the stated profit map. Generated
calendars and known inclusion designs can reveal an invalid covariance or
misstated household unit cheaply. Public bank observations can establish
availability and preparation burden. Neither route by itself verifies a bank's
proxy exclusion, household truth or future margin. The economic question is
whether improved information or precision changes a treasury action enough to
justify the next acquisition. An interval that still spans consequential gains
and losses is an informative inconclusive result.

Servicing requires a policy that uses the information actually available at
each action, and an evaluation that preserves the original eligible cohort.
The finite-table example supplies an exact reference and a conservative bound
that is too wide for useful selection. A first prototype should compare a
specified estimator with that reference under controlled assignment, support
and dropout. Sharper valid uncertainty is a research objective; it is not
created by asking an agent to report a narrower interval. Hidden-state and
informative-observation examples with equal observed laws require an information
change or a defensible restriction. The eventual value of resolving them depends
on feasible servicing actions and rewards, including assistance costs.

Discovery requires a specified graph family, an honest identification state and
an effect or decision comparison after graph uncertainty. A prototype can first
check endpoint and node-order conversions against generated truth, then test a
selected discovery procedure under its own assumptions. The investment question
is whether a retained ambiguity changes the offer decision, and which additional
evidence can resolve it. Agreement among packages or among repeated language
answers is not an authenticated signal of the causal state. A stronger claim
about language-assisted discovery requires a separate controlled comparison of
the data, source evidence and expert effort supplied to each alternative.

Observation construction needs different evidence again. Valid clocks and
unchanged hashes can coexist with false labels, duplicated origins and wrong
inclusion probabilities. A public/generated prototype can test measurement
correction and the transmission of its uncertainty, including singular cases.
The agent's contribution may be to expose the missing audit or distinguish an
outcome clock from a feature clock. Authentic truth labels, ownership and joint
inclusion evidence are later inputs when the decision benefit warrants their
cost. The observation module should report which uncertainty remains instead
of awarding a truthful-population label from a successful timestamp check.
\citep{exec14_l8_design}

These routes have known engineering steps and genuine scientific limits. We
know how to implement a bounded adapter, preserve failed requests, compare exact
references, collect workflow costs and prepare a controlled pilot. We do not
know a universal theorem for arbitrary hidden-state decisions, unrestricted
dependent learners or arbitrary temporal graph effects, and no language model
can make observationally equivalent worlds distinguishable without additional
information. We also do not yet know the empirical accuracy, calibrated risk,
review burden or accepted bank value of the proposed assistance. A coherent
proposal treats each unknown as a specific next decision: prove a restricted
claim, change the information, test a prototype or decline the unsupported
use. Independent journeys can proceed under their own prerequisites. Bank
experiments follow demonstrated prototype merit and a useful information
question. \citep{exec14_l8_design}

The final chapter brings these conditions into one investment recommendation. The relevant comparison includes the option to retain an established analyst workflow, build a narrow reusable component, or defer an information-intensive capability. Each choice must be judged against the same decision and full cost, with the evidence that would reverse it stated explicitly.

\label{exec14:l8-development-end}

chapters.title: The first investment and the evidence that would reverse it

segments.text:
\chapter{The first investment and the evidence that would reverse it}
\label{rewrite:investment-decision}

The immediate proposal is a minimal comparative integration for a fixed
offer study, with explicit population weights, information dates and
a complete financial report. Reuse a transparent estimator and retain
a documented alternative. The seventeen-area comparison establishes
which further capabilities are plausible candidates and why they need
separate assumptions. It is not a reason to build all seventeen before
evaluating the first study.

\section{Compare equivalent completed studies}
There are four economically serious alternatives. Expert composition
uses existing methods and bespoke study documentation. Minimal integration
adds a reusable request and result description around selected methods.
A broad shared service adds more methods, languages, maintenance and
operating commitments. A commercial route can provide supported
procedures and existing institutional integration, but its relevant
entitlements, actual prices and matched capabilities are unknown here.
The detailed commercial discussions preserve documented features and
unknowns; an unobserved feature is not evidence that it is absent.

The proposed first comparison selects minimal integration against expert
composition. Its potential gains come from repeated target specification,
information-date checks, error detection and reporting. Fitting a regression
may occupy little of the total work. Any proposed saving must therefore
be measured over preparation, correction, interpretation and failed
attempts. Bespoke causal reasoning remains part of every alternative.

Let $N$ be annual studies genuinely eligible for this restricted route;
$h$ hours saved per completed study at equivalent quality; $w$ loaded
hourly cost; $D$ reduction in expected decision loss per study; $C$ annual
operating cost; and $K$ annualised development and adoption cost. Then
\[
 B=N(wh+D)-C-K.
\]
The conditional break-even study volume is $(C+K)/(wh+D)$ only when
$wh+D>0$. A negative denominator cannot be repaired by doing more studies.
The illustrative investment account in Section~\ref{r3:investment}
retains its actual stipulated inputs and arithmetic, including the
26.74-study threshold. That threshold belongs to that account. It must
not be imported as an observed requirement for the newly selected scope.

The deposit example's \pounds3 population contribution concerns one
constructed customer action. It is not $D$, the improvement in decision
loss due to choosing one analytical workflow over another. Counting
that whole contribution as a software benefit would confuse policy value
with the incremental value of analysis. Similarly, correction hours
counted in $h$ must not be counted again in $D$. These distinctions
prevent an attractive worked example from becoming an invented ROI.

\section{The multi-year investment account and institutional variation}
\label{r3:investment}

A common causal product earns its cost by improving repeated scientific
work. The appropriate alternative is a capable quantitative team composing
the same open-source methods with ordinary engineering, documentation and
review. Such a team can produce good causal studies without a new platform.
The investment question is whether the shared representations and qualified
operations reduce the cost of equivalent work or enable additional valuable
decisions, after construction, support and adoption are included.

\subsection{Define equivalent output before pricing reuse}
\label{r3:equivalent-output}

An equivalent completed study has a reconstructed population and observation
clock, a clear intervention and financial outcome, a defensible identification
argument or useful nonidentification conclusion, appropriate inference,
reproducible artifacts and review. The comparison must include negative
results. An early finding that a requested target is unidentified can save
substantial work; forcing every study to return a numerical effect would
reward scientific error.

The proposed service would help analysts reconstruct what was known when
a decision was made, keep the population and outcome consistent, document
why an effect is identified, and carry uncertainty into the financial
comparison. It would reuse existing numerical methods where their
assumptions fit. Each business would still specify its products, costs and
constraints. A mortgage policy, an individual collections decision and a
macroeconomic shock need not share the same economic quantity of interest.

Comparator costs should include the same required outputs and review
quality. Reduced effort from omitting uncertainty or failing to investigate
weak support is not a saving. Conversely, building a generic model interface
for a one-off study can cost more than a small, clearly documented expert
analysis. The portfolio of genuinely repeated requests, not the total
number of database rows, determines the economic opportunity.

\subsection{An auditable cost model}
\label{r3:cost-model}

For alternative $j\in\{E,P\}$, expert composition or shared product,
let $K_j$ be initial construction cost, $F_j$ annual shared cost,
$c_j$ marginal cost per equivalent completed study, and $n_t$ completed
studies in year $t$. With horizon $H$ and discount rate $r$,
\begin{equation}
 C_j=K_j+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\frac{F_j+c_jn_t}{(1+r)^t}.
 \label{r3:present-cost}
\end{equation}
The categories are disjoint: method maintenance and common infrastructure
belong in $F_j$, while study-specific preparation, fitting, review and
rework belong in $c_j$. Failed-study costs must be included in one
category; a completed-study denominator cannot make them disappear.

Use the following illustrative USD-million assumptions to expose the
break-even logic:
\[
 (K_E,F_E,c_E)=(1,.6,.15),\qquad
 (K_P,F_P,c_P)=(4,1.8,.06),\qquad H=3,\quad r=.10.
\]
These are planning inputs, not observed bank prices, measured productivity
or enterprise vendor quotations. Let
$a_H=\sum_{t=1}^H(1+r)^{-t}$. At constant annual volume $n$, the cost-only
threshold, when $c_E>c_P$, is
\begin{equation}
 n^*=\frac{(K_P-K_E)/a_H+(F_P-F_E)}{c_E-c_P}.
 \label{r3:reuse-threshold}
\end{equation}
If the marginal saving is zero or negative, this particular reuse argument
does not establish a positive-volume crossover. Under the stipulated
numbers, $a_H=2.48685$ and $n^*=26.74$ studies annually.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small

\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}
\toprule Scenario & Expert cost & Platform cost & Platform saving\\\midrule
Low reuse & 5.476 & 9.670 & -4.194\\
Moderate reuse & 11.445 & 12.057 & -0.613\\
High reuse & 15.921 & 13.848 & 2.073\\
Adoption ramp & 8.402 & 10.840 & -2.438\\
\bottomrule\end{tabular}

\caption{Three-year present cost in illustrative USD millions. Annual
volumes are 8, 24 and 36, or the ramp $(4,16,30)$. Both alternatives
deliver the same specified scientific outputs.}
\label{r3:reuse-economics}
\end{table}

At eight annual studies the product costs about USD\,4.19 million more.
At 24 it still costs about USD\,.61 million more. At 36 it saves about
USD\,2.07 million. The ramp leaves a USD\,2.44 million premium even
though final-year volume exceeds the constant-volume threshold:
construction occurs before most reuse. Halving marginal savings doubles
the threshold to 53.47 studies; increasing the annual shared-cost
premium to USD\,2 million raises it to 35.63.

\begin{figure}[htbp]\centering
\includegraphics[width=.88\textwidth]{derivations/reuse_economics.pdf}
\caption{The crossover follows from the declared account. It is not
a forecast of demand or evidence that the shared layer already saves effort.}
\end{figure}

The simple model holds study mix fixed. A more realistic portfolio has
classes $k$ with costs $c_{jk}$ and volumes $n_{tk}$, replacing
$c_jn_t$ by $\sum_k c_{jk}n_{tk}$. A few expensive bespoke latent
models may have little shared work with many routine rollouts.
Reuse should therefore be measured by operation and data contract, not
assumed from a common causal-inference label.

\subsection{Separate business value from construction savings}
\label{r3:incremental-value}

Let $D_t$ be incremental realized decision value attributable to the
product relative to the equivalent expert workflow. Then
\begin{equation}
 \Delta\operatorname{NPV}
 =C_E-C_P+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\frac{D_t}{(1+r)^t}.
 \label{r3:incremental-npv}
\end{equation}
The first term already counts workflow savings. Released analyst time
must not be added again as business value. If it permits extra studies,
their costs, capacity use, outcome lags and incremental decisions
belong in the expanded account.

At 24 annual studies the illustrative cost premium requires about
USD\,.246 million of additional constant annual decision value.
The adoption ramp requires about USD\,.980 million. The size of a
bank's balance sheet does not establish either amount. The expert
comparator may already identify the same profitable policy or reject
the same loss-making offer.

The deposit study illustrates the attribution problem. Finding a
negative contribution can prevent a loss only if the finding changes
what would otherwise have been done. The prevented loss cannot be
credited to the product merely because its report contains the estimate.
Likewise the simulated collections gain is a property of the declared
environment; it supplies no observed revenue to this investment account.
Latent-state research can be worthwhile even while operational value
remains uncertain.

Costs and gains also mature on different clocks. Data access,
implementation and review are paid before customer outcomes are
observed. A six-month retention measure may mature during an early
evaluation; credit losses or a persistent pricing response may not.
A continuation model supplies a conditional forecast for those outcomes,
not an observation. Report the cash timing and model dependence explicitly.

\subsection{Measure the common-product hypothesis}
\label{r3:adoption-experiment}

The complete-workflow measurements in Section~\ref{s4:workflow-results}
refine the resource account but do not estimate its labor terms. A response
workflow over 3.85 million versioned records takes about 3.38 seconds on the
recorded host; a 3,200-customer latent workflow with 19 bootstrap refits takes
about 48.27 seconds. Both the product and expert-composition arms can use
these same numerical operations. Pricing one arm from a bare estimator call
and the other from reconstruction plus inference would be an unequal-output
comparison. The illustrative per-study dollar inputs above therefore remain
unchanged pending matched measurements of preparation, review and rework.

The first tranche should compare matched tasks in the intervention,
sequential-decision and dynamic-systems workspaces. Agree their outputs,
scientific scope and reviewer rubric before measuring effort. Give the
expert-composition arm the same sources, data access and expertise, and
allow sensible reusable templates. Counterbalance task order where
possible to reduce learning effects.

Measure analyst and reviewer hours, calendar delay, machine cost,
failed starts, rework and unresolved material findings separately.
Ask a second analyst to reconstruct the population, target and financial
conclusion from the exported artifacts. Deliberately introduced clock,
weight and sign errors can test whether review finds the defects.
This tests the proposed product's specific value proposition, rather
than whether a polished interface is pleasant.

A planning target of 30\% lower median analyst/reviewer effort can be
useful if review quality and output scope are held fixed. It remains
a hypothesis until measured across repeated uses and teams. A successful
first-author demonstration is insufficient evidence of institutional
reuse. Conversely, more early rejections can be a benefit if they
correctly avoid expensive unidentified studies.

Progression can be written as
\[
 n_t^{\rm usable}=n_t^{\rm started}
 p_t^{\rm data}p_t^{\rm design}p_t^{\rm execution}p_t^{\rm review},
\]
where each probability conditions on reaching the preceding stage.
This is the chain rule, not an independence assumption. It separates
volume aspirations from usable output and makes adoption bottlenecks
visible. Charges for unsuccessful studies remain in the cost account.

\subsection{A staged construction budget and stopping rules}
\label{r3:investment-sequence}

An illustrative first tranche assigns six people for six months:
one product/economics lead, two causal/econometric scientists, two
data/platform engineers and one application engineer. At USD\,25,000
per loaded person-month, staff cost is USD\,900,000; USD\,50,000
compute/tooling and 20\% contingency give USD\,1.14 million.
This tranche is included in the illustrative USD\,4 million initial
product cost, not added to it. Data-owner, independent validation,
security and application-owner participation are unpriced and must
be estimated consistently for both alternatives before a bank funds work.

The tranche should implement the shared observation/request/evidence
objects and qualify a narrow adjusted/cohort and observed-history
policy path. Controlled-state fitting and temporal discovery should
enter the architecture immediately through finite, explicitly conditional
research operations. Six people cannot qualify every method in the
44-project survey for production in six months.

The next tranche depends on concrete outcomes. Continue if repeated
requests share observation and scientific contracts, reviewers can
reconstruct results, the required estimators/inference pass their
acceptance exercises, and measured effort supports the economic case.
Narrow the scope if most work remains application-specific. Retain
expert composition when reuse is low. Stop a particular policy analysis
when its data cannot distinguish materially different decisions and
additional evidence is not worth its cost.

These are different decisions: discontinuing an unidentified analysis,
deferring a numerical adapter, and declining investment in the shared
product should not be collapsed into a single project-failure flag.
The source archive and scientific representations remain useful even
if one deployment case is rejected.

\subsection{An independent offering must price institutional variation}
\label{r3:commercial-product}

An independent product can distribute the scientific core as an embedded
library and provide the three workspaces with deployment, support and
upgrade services. A design-partner engagement is a plausible first
commercial form: a named study portfolio, paid integration scope,
reproducible evidence export and a recurring support boundary.
No willingness-to-pay, sales-cycle or customer-retention estimate is
established by this proposal.

Each institution adds semantic mapping, legal-entity structure, observation
systems, scientific review and operational requirements. Code reuse
reduces some common work but does not remove those costs. A commercial
comparison should price onboarding, customer-specific adapters, method
maintenance, support and validation participation, and state which
customizations remain owned by the customer.

Procurement should compare products on the same reconstructed studies,
supported identification routes, uncertainty objects, data-locality
requirements and export/replay obligations. Repository activity or an
enterprise demonstration is not evidence that these scientific
operations are available. The source review establishes open-source
construction alternatives; it does not assert uninspected private-vendor
capabilities or prices.

The multi-year account prices the reuse hypothesis rather than a causal
method in isolation. Its cost and volume assumptions are sensitivity inputs
to the decision in this chapter, not observed bank demand.

\hypertarget{pd15:investment}{%
\section{The value of obtaining additional evidence}\label{pd15:investment}}

\hypertarget{proposal-acceptance-and-later-qualification}{%
\subsection{The evidence needed before investing}\label{proposal-acceptance-and-later-qualification}}

The investment decision requires a comparison of feasible alternatives,
their costs and the evidence for their expected benefits. Reproducible
public and simulated studies can support that comparison within their
stated assumptions. A restricted result may justify a narrow prototype
while leaving broader research questions unresolved.

Public evidence informs three choices: which existing methods to reuse,
where language assistance is useful, and how analysts should conduct a
reproducible study. A dataset can reveal a timing error or support a
controlled comparison without settling every question about those choices.

Later bank qualification asks a different question: do the assumptions,
precision, workflows and economics hold for a specific institution? That
stage may need genuine offer histories, logging information, independent
labels, owner-reviewed semantics, production constraints and prospective
outcomes. The relevant input should be requested only for the capability
and target population under test. An internal bank pilot is not required
to demonstrate that the proposal has a reproducible public baseline and
a sensible experiment design.

\hypertarget{a-value-of-information-decision}{%
\subsection{A value-of-information
decision}\label{a-value-of-information-decision}}

Let \(d\in\{\text{stop},\text{build},\text{pilot}\}\) denote an
investment choice, \(\theta\) unresolved technical and economic
conditions, and \(U(d,\theta)\) its net value. Let \(E\) denote current
public/prototype evidence and \(Z\) the possible result of a proposed
experiment. A planning expression for the expected value of sample
information is

\[
\operatorname{EVSI}
=\mathbb E_{Z\mid E}\!\left[\max_d\mathbb E\{U(d,\theta)\mid E,Z\}\right]
-\max_d\mathbb E\{U(d,\theta)\mid E\}.
\]

An experiment merits consideration when its expected decision
improvement exceeds its full incremental cost, including data
preparation, customer burden where relevant, security review, labeling,
analyst time and opportunity cost. This is a project decision framework,
not an empirically estimated ROI. Where a probability model for
\(\theta\) is unjustified, use a scenario table and sensitivity bounds
instead of a precise-looking EVSI number.

A simple illustrative calculation shows the sequencing. Suppose, purely
for planning, a small bank study costing 20,000 could avert an
unsuitable 200,000 build in 20\% of scenarios, with no other benefits or
costs. Its gross avoided-spend value would be 40,000 and its net would
be 20,000 under those assumptions. If the study changes the build
decision in only 2\% of scenarios, the same gross value is 4,000 and it
is not justified on that ground. These are stipulated arithmetic
examples, not quotations, bank probabilities or forecasts.

The decision should identify the uncertainty that matters. If a public
benchmark shows repeated action-clock mistakes, improve the formulation
layer before requesting confidential data. If a correct estimator is too
slow on modest data, fix or replace it before commissioning a platform
pilot. If all plausible effects lead to the same action, a costly
precision improvement may have little value. If policy value reverses
when a missing hardship variable is plausible, a carefully scoped bank
measurement study can have high value even when the public-data
implementation is technically sound.

\hypertarget{conditions-for-moving-to-expensive-evidence}{%
\subsection{Conditions for moving to expensive
evidence}\label{conditions-for-moving-to-expensive-evidence}}

An actionable next-experiment recommendation specifies the proposed
intervention, target population, candidate baseline, decision-loss
threshold and the smallest information addition that could alter the
decision. It also states an explicit stop or redesign outcome. A bank
experiment should not be recommended merely to fill a missing-evidence
cell.

For funding, the missing addition may be time-stamped offers and an
assignment mechanism, not more aggregate deposits. For servicing, it may
be feasible-action and hardship information at each decision time. For
discovery, it may be one feasible intervention that distinguishes
competing graphs. For observation construction, it may be a
representative independently resolved sample of uncertain identities
with known inclusion probabilities. Public data help design each
measurement and estimate its computational burden, while the bank
supplies the later population-specific truth.

Authentic institutional approval, independent acceptance, actual
workflow prices and production service levels remain future
qualification requirements. A proposal can be complete without them. It
cannot honestly claim those outcomes without obtaining them.

\hypertarget{remaining-survey-and-prototype-gaps}{%
\subsection{Remaining survey and prototype
gaps}\label{remaining-survey-and-prototype-gaps}}

The public-data portfolio supports specific analyses, including the
earnings experiment and the UCI timing comparison in this volume. These
executions do not qualify every candidate dataset. Current-source web
snapshots still need exact data-file vintages for future analyses.
Several benchmark datasets need data-specific rights checks. Mortgage
histories require registration and use review; the HMDA publication
endpoint was inaccessible in this run. The Criteo license is a material
constraint for a commercial proposal. These affect individual options;
project-generated alternatives and the already local public data keep
the prototype work moving.

No inspected public financial source supplies the complete logged bank
servicing action process or independent real-bank linkage truth. That
finding is limited to the surveyed sources. It calls for transparent
semi-synthetic experiments now and a justified targeted measurement
later, rather than a claim of impossibility. Public reasoning benchmarks
also cannot establish a live agent's quality without an actual
controlled run, nor resolve the business owner's normative choice of
outcome and feasible intervention.

Finally, public data do not repair the open mathematical arguments for
persistent dependence, hidden states, graph-equivalence effect sets or
arbitrary learning procedures. Those questions remain scoped research
obligations. The proposal can present negative findings and restricted
supported regimes, compare alternatives and describe what evidence would
change the recommendation. That is a strong proposal standard without
pretending that an accepted bank product already exists.

\section{A spending sequence with real alternatives}
The first expenditure buys a matched analyst comparison using the
constructed and public cases, with independently assessed scientific
quality and recorded full effort. It asks whether the small integration
changes decisions or reduces work enough to pay for its ongoing cost.
A bank-data pilot follows only if that evidence is favourable and the
bank supplies a defensible target, data access, assignment information
and a meaningful precision requirement. An operating trial then tests
the relevant interfaces and platform under its actual conditions.

Several observations would reverse or narrow the recommendation. Equal
quality and effort favour the established workflow. A commercial
entitlement supplying equivalent outputs at lower full cost favours
that route. Frequent lack of treatment support or reliable observation
truth favours better study design and data collection. A repeated
need for unsupported dependent inference limits the offer route rather
than justifying a broad claim. Evidence of consequential, reproducibly
avoided errors or lower full effort can justify extending the integration.

This is a conditional proposal with a selected next experiment. It
preserves the larger scientific and software programme without treating
its unfinished questions as already solved. The detailed comparisons
and operating evidence developed in the book allow a reader to inspect those
restrictions and alternatives before funding the next step.
